knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polar decomposition of a finite vector measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The unit-density identity is understood almost everywhere with respect to the total-variation measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\lambda\in\mathcal M^d(\Omega)\), there exists a Borel map \(u:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) such that \(\lambda=u\,|\lambda|\) and \(|u|=1\) \(|\lambda|\)-almost everywhere. Consequently, for every Borel \(\xi:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) integrable with respect to \(|\lambda|\), \[\int_\Omega \xi\cdot d\lambda=\int_\Omega(\xi\cdot u)\,d|\lambda|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite vector measure has a polar decomposition as its total-variation measure multiplied by a Borel unit vector field. Integration against the vector measure therefore reduces to scalar integration against its total variation.
assumptions_latex: \xi:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\text{ is Borel and }|\xi|\in L^1(\Omega,|\lambda|)\text{ for the integral identity}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists u:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\text{ Borel}:\quad \lambda=u|\lambda|,\quad |u|=1\ \ |\lambda|\text{-a.e.},\quad \int\xi\cdot d\lambda=\int(\xi\cdot u)\,d|\lambda|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lp bound for interpolation toward an atomic target
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm growth along an optimal-transport interpolation with atomic target and strictly convex translation-invariant cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\gamma\) be an optimal transport plan between \(\mu\) and an atomic measure \(\nu\) for \(c(x,y)=h(y-x)\), where \(h:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) is strictly convex. Set \(\mu_t=(\pi_t)_\#\gamma\), where \(\pi_t(x,y)=(1-t)x+ty\). For \(0\le t<1\), \[\|\mu_t\|_{L^p}\le (1-t)^{-d/p'}\|\mu\|_{L^p},\] where \(p'\) is the conjugate exponent of \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For optimal transport toward an atomic target under a strictly convex translation-invariant cost, the interpolated measure has Lp norm at most (1−t)^(−d/p′) times the source Lp norm.

children.title: Marginal Measures
children.top_down_role: Source and target measure data for static transport problems.

assumptions_latex: \(\gamma\) is a probability measure on \(X\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The marginal measures of \(\gamma\) are \(\mu=(p_X)_\#\gamma\) and \(\nu=(p_Y)_\#\gamma\).

notation.meaning: Canonical coordinate projections from the product space
Pushforward of a measure by a measurable map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability marginals on a measurable product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every measurable \(A\subseteq X\) and \(B\subseteq Y\), define
\[
\mu(A):=\gamma(A\times Y),\qquad \nu(B):=\gamma(X\times B).
\]
Equivalently, \(\mu=(p_X)_\#\gamma\) and \(\nu=(p_Y)_\#\gamma\). The measures \(\mu\) and \(\nu\) are respectively the first and second marginal measures of \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The marginals of a probability measure on a product space are its pushforwards under the two coordinate projections.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Measures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the Marginal Measures leaf and is mathematically standard, but no citation or inspectable locator is supplied. The product measurable space should also be understood as equipped with the product sigma-algebra.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-support approximations of marginal measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic mesh and empirical representations of transport marginals, with the equal-mass two-marginal specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A probability measure \(\mu\) may be approximated by \(\widehat\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}m_i\delta_{x_i}\), where \(m_i\ge 0\) and \(\sum_i m_i=1\). For disjoint measurable cells \(V_i\) covering the support and anchors \(a_i\in V_i\), the mesh approximation is \(\widehat\mu^{\mathrm{mesh}}=\sum_i\mu(V_i)\delta_{a_i}\). For i.i.d. samples \(X_i\sim\mu\), the empirical approximation is \(\widehat\mu_\ell=\ell^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{X_i}\); on \(\mathbb R^d\), \(\widehat\mu_\ell\) converges narrowly to \(\mu\) almost surely. If two marginals are each discretized into the same number \(\ell\) of equal-mass atoms, the resulting two-marginal discrete transport problem admits an optimal permutation coupling and hence a Monge solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A marginal measure can be approximated by finitely many weighted atoms, using either mesh-cell masses or equal-weight empirical samples. Empirical measures on Euclidean space converge narrowly almost surely. Equal-mass discretizations of two marginals with the same number of atoms admit an optimal permutation, and therefore Monge, coupling.
assumptions_latex: V_1,\ldots,V_\ell\ \text{are disjoint measurable cells covering the support and }a_i\in V_i
N=2\ \text{and both discretized marginals have }\ell\text{ atoms of mass }1/\ell\ \text{for the Monge assertion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\mu^{\mathrm{mesh}}=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\mu(V_i)\delta_{a_i},\qquad \widehat\mu_\ell=\frac1\ell\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\delta_{X_i}\rightharpoonup\mu\ \text{a.s.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Benamou–Brenier velocity and momentum representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic Wasserstein transport on Euclidean space, including the distributional continuity equation and the boundary cases of the convex perspective integrand.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For quadratic cost on \mathbb{R}^d, the squared Wasserstein distance admits the dynamic representation
\[
\mathcal W_2^2(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)=\inf_{(\alpha_t,v_t)}\int_0^1\int_{\mathbb R^d}\|v_t(x)\|^2\,d\alpha_t(x)\,dt,
\]
where \(\partial_t\alpha_t+\operatorname{div}(\alpha_t v_t)=0\) in distributions and \(\alpha_{t=0}=\alpha_0,\ \alpha_{t=1}=\alpha_1\). Setting \(J_t=\alpha_t v_t\) gives the equivalent convex formulation
\[
\mathcal W_2^2(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)=\inf_{(\alpha,J)\in\mathcal C(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)}\int_0^1\int_{\mathbb R^d}\theta(\alpha_t(x),J_t(x))\,dx\,dt,
\]
with \(\mathcal C(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)=\{(\alpha,J):\partial_t\alpha_t+\operatorname{div}J_t=0,\ \alpha_{0}=\alpha_0,\ \alpha_{1}=\alpha_1\}\) and
\[
\theta(a,b)=\begin{cases}\|b\|^2/a,&a>0,\\0,&(a,b)=(0,0),\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
The lower-semicontinuous convex, positively one-homogeneous integrand extends to measures and forces zero momentum wherever the transported mass vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For squared Euclidean transport cost, the squared 2-Wasserstein distance is the minimum kinetic action over measure paths and velocity fields satisfying the continuity equation in the distributional sense and the prescribed endpoint measures. Replacing velocity by momentum yields an equivalent convex optimization problem with a lower-semicontinuous perspective integrand; its exceptional cases require zero momentum where mass is zero, and its positive one-homogeneity permits an unambiguous measure-valued interpretation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal W_2^2(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)=\inf_{(\alpha,v)}\int_0^1\!\int\|v_t\|^2\,d\alpha_t\,dt=\inf_{(\alpha,J)\in\mathcal C(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)}\int_0^1\!\int\theta(\alpha_t,J_t),\quad J_t=\alpha_t v_t,

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness of the Monotone Transport Plan in One Dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-monotone couplings of probability measures on the real line.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R)\) and \(\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\). If, for all \((x,y),(x',y')\in\operatorname{spt}(\gamma)\), \(x<x'\) implies \(y\le y'\), then \(\gamma=\gamma_{\mathrm{mon}}\). In particular, exactly one coupling satisfies this support-monotonicity property. Moreover, if \(\mu\) is atomless, then \(\gamma=\gamma_{T_{\mathrm{mon}}}\), the plan induced by the monotone transport map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupling of two probability measures on the real line whose support preserves order is the unique monotone transport plan. If the source measure is atomless, that plan is induced by the monotone transport map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma=\gamma_{\mathrm{mon}}\text{, uniquely among couplings satisfying the support condition};\qquad \mu\text{ atomless}\Rightarrow\gamma=\gamma_{T_{\mathrm{mon}}}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multi-marginal couplings and map-induced transport plans
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate marginals, multi-marginal couplings, map-induced plans, graph representations, and inverse transport plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For N\ge2 and \mathbf X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_N, define \pi^i(x_1,\ldots,x_N)=x_i and \pi^{i,j}(x_1,\ldots,x_N)=(x_i,x_j). For \boldsymbol\mu\in\mathcal P(\mathbf X), its marginals are \mu^i:=\pi^i_\#\boldsymbol\mu and \boldsymbol\mu^{ij}:=\pi^{i,j}_\#\boldsymbol\mu. Given \mu^i\in\mathcal P(X_i), define \Gamma(\mu^1,\ldots,\mu^N):=\{\boldsymbol\mu\in\mathcal P(\mathbf X):\pi^i_\#\boldsymbol\mu=\mu^i,\ i=1,\ldots,N\}. For N=2 its elements are transport plans, and \Gamma(\mu^1,\mu^2)=\{\mu^1\times\mu^2\} if either marginal is a Dirac mass. If \mu^2=\mathbf r_\#\mu^1 for a Borel map \mathbf r:X_1\to X_2, then (\mathbf i\times\mathbf r)_\#\mu^1\in\Gamma(\mu^1,\mu^2) is induced by \mathbf r. Conversely, a transport plan concentrated on a measurable graph admits this representation for a \mu^1-measurable map; when X_1,X_2 are Polish, the corresponding assertion holds with Borel graphs and Borel maps. For \sigma(x_1,x_2)=(x_2,x_1), define the inverse plan by \boldsymbol\mu^{-1}:=\sigma_\#\boldsymbol\mu.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginals are pushforwards under coordinate projections, and a multi-marginal coupling is a joint probability measure with prescribed marginals. A transport map induces a graph-supported plan, while graph-supported plans admit a map representation under the stated measurability conditions. Swapping coordinates defines the inverse plan.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf r:X_1\to X_2\text{ is Borel and }\mu^2=\mathbf r_\#\mu^1\text{ for the induced-plan construction}
\boldsymbol\mu\text{ is concentrated on a measurable graph for the converse representation}
X_1,X_2\text{ are Polish for the Borel-graph/Borel-map version}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Gamma(\mu^1,\ldots,\mu^N)=\{\boldsymbol\mu\in\mathcal P(\mathbf X):\pi^i_\#\boldsymbol\mu=\mu^i\ \forall i\},\quad \mu^2=\mathbf r_\#\mu^1\Rightarrow(\mathbf i\times\mathbf r)_\#\mu^1\in\Gamma(\mu^1,\mu^2),\quad \boldsymbol\mu^{-1}=\sigma_\#\boldsymbol\mu.

children.title: Pushforward Measures
children.top_down_role: Measure transport represented through measurable maps.

assumptions_latex: \(T:X\to Y\) is measurable and \(\mu\) is a measure on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pushforward \(T_\#\mu\) is the measure on \(Y\) given by \((T_\#\mu)(B)=\mu(T^{-1}(B))\).

notation.meaning: Pushforward, or image, measure of mu under T
Inverse image of a measurable set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pushforward under a measurable map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The pushforward of \(\mu\) by \(T\) is the measure \(T_\#\mu\) on \((Y,\Sigma_Y)\) defined by
\[
(T_\#\mu)(B):=\mu\bigl(T^{-1}(B)\bigr),\qquad B\in\Sigma_Y.
\]
Equivalently, for every nonnegative measurable function \(\varphi:Y\to[0,+\infty]\),
\[
\int_Y\varphi(y)\,d(T_\#\mu)(y)=\int_X\varphi(T(x))\,d\mu(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pushforward transfers a measure through a measurable map by assigning each target set the mass of its inverse image.
knowledge_statements.title: Pushforward Measures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pushforward definition and integration identity match the leaf and are internally consistent, but the record has no source or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pushforward measure and its basic properties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition, integration identity, absolute-continuity preservation, composition, narrow continuity, and support behavior of pushforward measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X_1,X_2 be separable metric spaces, \mu\in\mathcal P(X_1), and let \mathbf r:X_1\to X_2 be Borel, or more generally \mu-measurable. Define (\mathbf r_\#\mu)(B):=\mu(\mathbf r^{-1}(B)) for B\in\mathcal B(X_2). For every bounded Borel, or \mathbf r_\#\mu-integrable Borel, function f:X_2\to\mathbb R, \int_{X_1}f(\mathbf r(x))\,d\mu(x)=\int_{X_2}f(y)\,d(\mathbf r_\#\mu)(y). If \nu\ll\mu, then \mathbf r_\#\nu\ll\mathbf r_\#\mu. For measurable \mathbf s:X_1\to X_2 and \mathbf r:X_2\to X_3, (\mathbf r\circ\mathbf s)_\#\mu=\mathbf r_\#(\mathbf s_\#\mu). If \mathbf r is continuous, then \mathbf r_\#:\mathcal P(X_1)\to\mathcal P(X_2) is narrowly continuous and \mathbf r(\operatorname{supp}\mu)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(\mathbf r_\#\mu)=\overline{\mathbf r(\operatorname{supp}\mu)}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pushforward measure assigns to each Borel set the measure of its inverse image. Integration against it equals integration of the pulled-back function. Pushforwards preserve absolute continuity and composition; continuous maps also induce narrowly continuous pushforward operators, with support equal to the closure of the image of the original support.
assumptions_latex: f:X_2\to\mathbb R\text{ is bounded Borel or }\mathbf r_\#\mu\text{-integrable Borel}
\mathbf s:X_1\to X_2,\ \mathbf r:X_2\to X_3\text{ are measurable for composition}
\mathbf r\text{ is continuous for narrow continuity and the support assertions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mathbf r_\#\mu)(B)=\mu(\mathbf r^{-1}(B)),\quad \int f\circ\mathbf r\,d\mu=\int f\,d(\mathbf r_\#\mu),\quad \nu\ll\mu\Rightarrow\mathbf r_\#\nu\ll\mathbf r_\#\mu,\quad (\mathbf r\circ\mathbf s)_\#\mu=\mathbf r_\#(\mathbf s_\#\mu),\quad \mathbf r_\#\text{ is narrowly continuous if }\mathbf r\text{ is continuous},\quad \mathbf r(\operatorname{supp}\mu)\subseteq\operatorname{supp}(\mathbf r_\#\mu)=\overline{\mathbf r(\operatorname{supp}\mu)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Narrow convergence of pushforwards under varying maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint stability of pushforward measures when both the measures and maps vary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X_1,X_2 be separable metric spaces. Let \mathbf r_n:X_1\to X_2 be Borel maps converging uniformly to \mathbf r on compact subsets of X_1, and let (\mu_n)\subset\mathcal P(X_1) be tight and converge narrowly to \mu. If \mathbf r is continuous, then (\mathbf r_n)_\#\mu_n converges narrowly to \mathbf r_\#\mu.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a tight narrowly convergent sequence of probability measures is pushed forward by Borel maps converging uniformly on compact sets to a continuous map, then the resulting pushforward measures converge narrowly to the limiting pushforward.

children.title: Map-Induced Coupling Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distinction between general couplings and those representable by transport maps.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupling \(\gamma\) is map-induced if and only if its conditional measures \(\gamma_x\) are Dirac measures for \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\).

notation.meaning: Coupling induced by the graph of T
Disintegration of gamma over its first marginal
Dirac probability measure at a point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between deterministic plans and general Kantorovich couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coupling \(\gamma\) is induced by a measurable map \(T:X\to Y\), namely \(\gamma=(\operatorname{id}_X,T)_\#\mu\), if and only if a disintegration \(\gamma(dx,dy)=\mu(dx)\gamma_x(dy)\) satisfies \(\gamma_x=\delta_{T(x)}\) for \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\). Consequently, any coupling whose conditional measure \(\gamma_x\) is non-Dirac on a set of positive \(\mu\)-measure is not map-induced. In particular, \(\mu\otimes\nu\) is not map-induced when \(\nu\) is non-Dirac.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupling comes from a deterministic map exactly when its conditional target distribution is almost everywhere a Dirac mass.
knowledge_statements.title: Map-Induced Coupling Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the container, and the standard-Borel hypothesis is appropriate for the disintegration characterization. An authoritative locator is required for the existence and measurable Dirac-kernel characterization used in the equivalence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity for disintegrated compactly supported measures and a continuous transport cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb R^d=\mathbb R^k	imes\mathbb R^{d-k}\), and let compactly supported \(\mu,
u\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d)\) have disintegrations \(\mu=\mu^+\otimes\mu^{x^+}\) and \(
u=
u^+\otimes
u^{y^+}\). If \(c\) is continuous, then the functional \[F(\eta)=\int \mathcal T_c\!\left(\mu^{x^+},
u^{y^+}ight)\,d\eta(x^+,y^+)\] is continuous on \(\Pi(\mu^+,
u^+)\) for the weak topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For compactly supported disintegrated probability measures and a continuous cost, integrating the optimal conditional transport cost against a coupling of the conditioning marginals defines a weakly continuous functional of that coupling.

children.title: Finite-Valued Cost Functions
children.top_down_role: Transport costs taking finite values throughout their domain.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite-valued transport cost is a measurable map \(c:X\times Y\to[0,+\infty)\).

notation.meaning: Transport cost assigned to a source-target pair

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative costs finite at every source-target pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite-valued transport cost is a measurable function
\[
c:X\times Y\longrightarrow[0,+\infty).
\]
Thus \(c(x,y)<+\infty\) for every \((x,y)\in X\times Y\). For a coupling \(\gamma\in\mathcal P(X\times Y)\), its total cost is the extended integral \(\int_{X\times Y}c(x,y)\,d\gamma(x,y)\), which may still equal \(+\infty\) despite pointwise finiteness of \(c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-valued transport cost is measurable and finite at every pair, although its integral under a coupling may still be infinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Valued Cost Functions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Finite-Valued Cost Functions leaf and correctly distinguishes pointwise finiteness from integrability. No citation or specific locator supports the adopted transport-cost convention.

children.title: Extended-Valued Cost Functions
children.top_down_role: Costs encoding forbidden transport through infinite values.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An extended-valued transport cost is a measurable map \(c:X\times Y\to[0,+\infty]\), with \(+\infty\) encoding forbidden transport pairs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative costs permitting infinite values as hard constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An extended-valued transport cost is a measurable function
\[
c:X\times Y\longrightarrow[0,+\infty].
\]
Its effective domain is \(\operatorname{dom}c:=\{(x,y)\in X\times Y:c(x,y)<+\infty\}\). Assigning \(c(x,y)=+\infty\) excludes the pair \((x,y)\) from every finite-cost plan: if \(\gamma(\{c=+\infty\})>0\), then \(\int c\,d\gamma=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-valued cost may equal infinity, thereby encoding transport pairs that no finite-cost coupling can charge.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Valued Cost Functions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Extended-Valued Cost Functions leaf and correctly describes infinite cost as a finite-cost feasibility constraint. No source reference or locator is supplied.

children.title: Cost Integrability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes determined by integrability of the transport objective.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The planwise finite-cost condition is \(c\in L^1(\gamma)\), while feasibility of the transport problem requires some \(\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) with \(\int c\,d\gamma<+\infty\).

notation.meaning: Cost functional evaluated at a coupling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Planwise and problemwise integrability for nonnegative costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The cost is integrable with respect to \(\gamma\) precisely when
\[
\mathcal C_c(\gamma):=\int_{X\times Y}c(x,y)\,d\gamma(x,y)<+\infty,
\]
equivalently \(c\in L^1(\gamma)\) for nonnegative \(c\). Define
\[
\Pi_c(\mu,\nu):=\{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu):\mathcal C_c(\gamma)<+\infty\}.
\]
The transport problem has a finite-cost feasible plan exactly when \(\Pi_c(\mu,\nu)\neq\varnothing\), equivalently when \(\inf_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\mathcal C_c(\gamma)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A plan is cost-integrable when its cost integral is finite; the transport problem is finite-cost feasible when at least one such coupling exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Cost Integrability Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the integrability-regime leaf, and the planwise and problemwise conditions are precise for nonnegative measurable costs. No source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Nonintegrable Cost Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure modes caused by infinite or undefined transport costs.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\int_X a\,d\mu=+\infty\) or \(\int_Y b\,d\nu=+\infty\), then every \(\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) has \(\int c\,d\gamma=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp marginal-moment obstruction for separable nonnegative costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\), the marginal identities give
\[
\int_{X\times Y}c(x,y)\,d\gamma(x,y)=\int_X a(x)\,d\mu(x)+\int_Y b(y)\,d\nu(y).
\]
Hence, if either marginal integral is infinite, then \(\Pi_c(\mu,\nu)=\varnothing\): no choice of dependence structure can produce a finite-cost coupling. This failure can occur even when \(a\), \(b\), and therefore \(c\), are finite-valued pointwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a separable cost, an infinite required marginal moment forces every coupling to have infinite cost, even if the cost is pointwise finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonintegrable Cost Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and separable-cost obstruction fit the leaf, but no source or locator is supplied. The displayed marginal identity is followed by derivational language and should be recast as a direct statement when the record is revised after sourcing.

children.title: Tightness of Transport Plans
children.top_down_role: Uniform concentration properties for admissible transport-plan families.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family \(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) is uniformly tight in \(\mathcal P(X\times Y)\).

notation.meaning: Set of couplings with fixed marginals
Compact subsets selected to capture marginal mass

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform tightness arising from fixed tight marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), choose compact sets \(K_X\subseteq X\) and \(K_Y\subseteq Y\) such that \(\mu(K_X)\geq1-\varepsilon/2\) and \(\nu(K_Y)\geq1-\varepsilon/2\). Then every \(\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) satisfies
\[
\gamma(K_X\times K_Y)\geq1-\varepsilon.
\]
Therefore the entire family \(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) is uniformly tight as a subset of \(\mathcal P(X\times Y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Couplings with fixed probability marginals are uniformly tight because compact sets capturing each marginal jointly capture every coupling.
knowledge_statements.title: Tightness of Transport Plans

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform-tightness property is correct for fixed probability marginals on Polish spaces and fits the leaf. The record lacks a source locator and is written partly as a proof by instructing the reader to choose compact sets and deriving the conclusion.

Then \(\Pi(\mathcal P,\mathcal Q):=\{\pi\in P(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y):(\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal X})_\#\pi\in\mathcal P,\ (\operatorname{pr}_{\mathcal Y})_\#\pi\in\mathcal Q\}\) is tight in \(P(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)\).

\(\mathcal P\subset P(\mathcal X)\) and \(\mathcal Q\subset P(\mathcal Y)\) are tight families.

children.title: Escape-of-Mass Failures
children.top_down_role: Loss of compactness through mass migration beyond controlled regions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(\gamma_n\in\Pi(\mu_n,\nu_n)\), the family \(\{\gamma_n:n\in\mathbb N\}\) is not tight and has no weakly convergent subsequence.

notation.meaning: Dirac probability measure at the diagonal point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of compactness when prescribed marginals vary without uniform tightness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(n\in\mathbb N\), the unique coupling of \(\mu_n=\delta_n\) and \(\nu_n=\delta_n\) is \(\gamma_n=\delta_{(n,n)}\). For any compact set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^2\), one has \((n,n)\notin K\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and hence \(\gamma_n(K)=0\) eventually. Thus \(\{\gamma_n:n\in\mathbb N\}\) is not tight and admits no weakly convergent subsequence. Fixed-marginal compactness therefore does not extend to arbitrarily varying, non-uniformly-tight marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dirac marginals escaping to infinity produce coupling measures that are not tight, so compactness fails when marginals vary without uniform tightness.
knowledge_statements.title: Escape-of-Mass Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample role exactly fits Escape-of-Mass Failures, and the example correctly shows loss of tightness for varying marginals. It has no citation or locator and includes proof-style derivation rather than only the counterexample statement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Genetic column generation for two-marginal optimal transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-support transport algorithm using generated offspring, dual-constraint violations, and pruning of old inactive configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given marginals \(\mu_1,\mu_2\), a feasible set \(\Omega\) satisfying condition (2), and \(\beta>1\), repeatedly solve \((\mathrm{ROT})\) and \((\mathrm{D\text{-}ROT})\) for \((\gamma^\star,u^\star)\). Sample a parent in \(\operatorname{supp}(\gamma^\star)\) and a child \((x',y')\) until either \(u_1^\star(x')+u_2^\star(y')>c(x',y')\) or all possible offspring have been tried. In the latter case, return \((\gamma^\star,u^\star)\) as optimal. Otherwise set \(\Omega\leftarrow\Omega\cup\{(x',y')\}\). If \(|\Omega|>\beta(\ell_1+\ell_2)\), remove the \(\ell_1+\ell_2\) oldest inactive configurations, and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the restricted primal-dual transport problems, generate offspring from a configuration in the current transport support, and add an offspring that violates the full-dual constraint. Prune the oldest inactive configurations when the size threshold is exceeded. If all possible offspring are tried without finding an accepted child, return the current pair as optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure either accepts a child satisfying }u_1^\star(x')+u_2^\star(y')>c(x',y')\text{ and continues, or returns }(\gamma^\star,u^\star)\text{ as optimal after all possible offspring have been tried without acceptance.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Genetic column-generation algorithm for MMOT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative restricted MMOT solution, neighboring-column search, and inactive-column deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(c\), marginals \(\mu_k\), a feasible reduced configuration set \(\Omega\), and \(\beta\geq2\), repeatedly solve the reduced primal-dual MMOT pair for \((\gamma,u)\). Draw \(r\in\operatorname{supp}\gamma\) and search among \(r'\notin\Omega\) differing from \(r\) in exactly one coordinate until \(\sum_i u_i(r_i')-c(r')>0\) or all such offspring have been tried; update \(\Omega\leftarrow\Omega\cup\{r'\}\). If \(|\Omega|>\beta\sum_{k=1}^N\ell_k\), remove the oldest \(\sum_{k=1}^N\ell_k\) inactive configurations from \(\Omega\setminus\operatorname{supp}\gamma\), and continue until convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method repeatedly solves a restricted MMOT problem, searches one-coordinate mutations of supported configurations for a violated full dual constraint, adds the resulting configuration, and deletes old inactive configurations when the pool exceeds the prescribed threshold.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_N\text{ is feasible for the reduced MMOT problem}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The iterates update the reduced configuration pool by neighboring-column generation and thresholded deletion until the convergence test is met.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multimarginal north-west corner construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy construction of a feasible finite multimarginal coupling from ordered marginal supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\Omega=\varnothing\), take the first support point in each marginal, and let each residual \(b_k\) equal the mass at the current point. While some coordinate has not reached its final support point, add the current tuple \(r\) to \(\Omega\), set \(\gamma(r)=\min_k b_k\), replace \(b_k\leftarrow b_k-\gamma(r)\), and whenever \(b_k=0\), advance coordinate \(k\) to its next support point and reset \(b_k\) to the corresponding marginal mass. Return \(\Omega\) and \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from the first atom of each ordered marginal, the rule assigns the smallest current residual mass to the current tuple, advances every exhausted marginal coordinate, and returns the accumulated configurations and transport plan.
assumptions_latex: \mu_k\text{ is supported on the ordered finite set }X_k=\{a_1^{(k)},\ldots,a_{\ell_k}^{(k)}\}\quad(k=1,\ldots,N)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure returns a configuration set }\Omega\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_N\text{ and a plan }\gamma\text{ constructed by the stated residual-mass updates.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multimarginal Optimal Transport Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines admissible multimarginal couplings and the associated cost-minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $N\ge 3$, let $X_1,\ldots,X_N$ be Polish metric spaces, and let $\mu_i\in\mathcal P(X_i)$ be Borel probability measures. Define $\Pi(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N)$ as the probability measures $\gamma$ on $X_1\times\cdots\times X_N$ whose $i$th marginal is $\mu_i$, equivalently satisfying $\int \mathbf 1_B(x_i)\,d\gamma(x_1,\ldots,x_N)=\mu_i(B)$ for every $i$ and every measurable $B\subseteq X_i$. The multimarginal optimal transport problem is $\inf_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N)}\int c(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\,d\gamma(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For three or more Borel probability measures on Polish metric spaces, an admissible multimarginal transport plan is a probability measure on the product space having each prescribed measure as its corresponding marginal. Multimarginal optimal transport minimizes the integral of the cost over all such plans.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_N\), and let \(\gamma^\star\) and \(u^\star=(u_1^\star,\ldots,u_N^\star)\) solve the reduced primal and dual MMOT problems on \(\Omega\). If \(\sum_{i=1}^N u_i^\star(r_i)-c(r)\leq0\) for every \(r\in X_1\times\cdots\times X_N\), then the zero extension \(\bar\gamma^\star(r)=\gamma^\star(r)\) for \(r\in\Omega\) and \(\bar\gamma^\star(r)=0\) otherwise is optimal for the full MMOT problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal restricted MMOT plan is globally optimal after zero extension whenever its optimal restricted dual variables satisfy every dual constraint of the full problem.
assumptions_latex: \gamma^\star\text{ solves the reduced primal MMOT problem on }\Omega
u^\star=(u_1^\star,\ldots,u_N^\star)\text{ solves the reduced dual MMOT problem on }\Omega
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar\gamma^\star(r):=\begin{cases}\gamma^\star(r),&r\in\Omega,\\0,&r\notin\Omega,\end{cases}\quad\text{is optimal for the full MMOT problem.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differentiability and Semiconvexity of c-Convex Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two alternative regularity regimes, with the stated exceptional-set and domain-boundary dimension bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that \(c\) satisfies \((\mathrm{Super})\) and \((\mathrm{Twist})\), and let \(\psi\) be c-convex. If \((\mathrm{Lip})\) holds, or if \((\mathrm{locLip})\) and \((\mathbf H_\infty)\) hold, then \(\psi\) is locally Lipschitz and differentiable in \(\mathcal X\) outside a set of zero volume. If \((\mathrm{SC})\) holds, or if \((\mathrm{locSC})\) and \((\mathbf H_\infty)\) hold, then \(\psi\) is locally semiconvex and differentiable in the interior in \(M\) of its domain outside a set of dimension at most \(n-1\); moreover, the boundary of its domain has dimension at most \(n-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Super and Twist, the stated global or local Lipschitz hypotheses make a c-convex function locally Lipschitz and differentiable outside a zero-volume set. The stated semiconcavity hypotheses make it locally semiconvex and differentiable in the interior of its domain outside a set of dimension at most n−1, with a domain boundary of dimension at most n−1.
assumptions_latex: (\mathrm{SC})\lor((\mathrm{locSC})\land(\mathbf H_\infty))\text{ for the semiconvexity and dimension conclusions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \psi\text{ has the corresponding local regularity and differentiability properties, with the stated exceptional-set and boundary bounds.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity, Twist, and Behavior-at-Infinity Conditions on a Transport Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A catalogue of alternative cost hypotheses used in solvability results for the Monge problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a smooth complete connected Riemannian manifold, \(\mathcal X\subset M\) closed, \(\mathcal Y\) Polish, and \(c:M\times\mathcal Y\to\mathbb R\) continuous. For first arguments in \(\operatorname{int}_M\mathcal X\), define: (Super), each \(c(\cdot,y)\) is everywhere superdifferentiable; (Twist), whenever defined, \(\nabla_xc(x,y)=\nabla_xc(x,y')\Rightarrow y=y'\); (Lip) and (SC), respectively local Lipschitz continuity and local semiconcavity in \(x\), uniformly over \(y\); and (locLip) and (locSC), the corresponding properties locally in \(y\). Condition \((\mathrm H\infty)_1\) requires that for every relevant \(x\) and measurable \(S\) with \(T_xS\) not contained in a half-space, there exist \(z_1,\ldots,z_k\in S\), a small open ball \(B\ni x\), and a compact \(C\subset\mathcal Y\) such that
\[
\inf_{w\in B}c(w,y)\ge \min_{1\le j\le k}c(z_j,y)\qquad(y\notin C).
\]
Condition \((\mathrm H\infty)_2\) requires that for every relevant \(x\) and every neighborhood \(U\ni x\), some small ball \(B\ni x\) satisfies
\[
\lim_{y\to\infty}\sup_{w\in B}\inf_{z\in U}\bigl[c(z,y)-c(w,y)\bigr]=-\infty.
\]
Write \((\mathrm H\infty)=(\mathrm H\infty)_1\wedge(\mathrm H\infty)_2\). In particular, (locSC) implies (Super), and the two behavior-at-infinity conditions are void when \(\mathcal Y\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous transport cost, the listed hypotheses distinguish superdifferentiability and twist from local Lipschitz or semiconcavity conditions that are either uniform in the target variable or only local in it. Two additional conditions control the cost as the target escapes to infinity; their conjunction is denoted (H-infinity). Local semiconcavity implies superdifferentiability, and the infinity conditions impose no restriction when the target space is compact.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is smooth, complete, and connected}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mathrm{locSC})\Rightarrow(\mathrm{Super}),\qquad (\mathrm H\infty):=(\mathrm H\infty)_1\wedge(\mathrm H\infty)_2,\qquad \mathcal Y\text{ compact}\Rightarrow(\mathrm H\infty)_1,(\mathrm H\infty)_2\text{ are void}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic-cost Monge solution under codimension-one nonconcentration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, uniqueness, and convex-subdifferential characterization for quadratic transport in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c(x,y)=|x-y|^2\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\mu,
u\) be probability measures satisfying \(\int |x|^2\,d\mu(x)+\int |y|^2\,d
u(y)<+\infty\). Assume that \(\mu(E)=0\) for every set \(E\) of dimension at most \(n-1\). Then there is a unique optimal transport plan \(\pi\), and it is deterministic. Among couplings of \((\mu,
u)\), the optimal coupling is characterized by the existence of a lower-semicontinuous convex function \(\psi\) such that \(y\in\partial\psi(x)\) almost surely. Equivalently, \(\operatorname{Spt}\pi\subset\operatorname{graph}(\partial\psi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For squared Euclidean cost, finite second moments and the condition that the source measure charges no set of dimension at most n−1 imply a unique deterministic optimal plan. The plan is characterized by concentration on the subdifferential of a lower-semicontinuous convex function.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^n)\) have finite second moments.
\(\mu(E)=0\) for every set \(E\) with \(\dim E\le n-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists!\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) optimal; \(\pi\) is deterministic and \(\operatorname{Spt}\pi\subset\operatorname{graph}(\partial\psi)\) for some lower-semicontinuous convex \(\psi\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: At-most-one-valued c-subdifferentials outside a small exceptional set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A Hausdorff-dimension estimate obtained from connectedness and a uniform shortening inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a smooth \(n\)-dimensional Riemannian manifold, and let \(c\) be a real-valued, bounded-below cost derived from a Lagrangian \(L\) on \(TM\times[0,1]\) satisfying the classical conditions of Definition 7.6. Assume (C), and assume that there are a uniform constant \(C>0\) and \(\beta>1-1/n\) such that whenever \(c(x_1,y_1)+c(x_2,y_2)\le c(x_1,y_2)+c(x_2,y_1)\) and \(\gamma_i\) are action-minimizing curves from \(x_i\) to \(y_i\), \[\sup_{0\le t\le1}d(\gamma_1(t),\gamma_2(t))\le C\,d(\gamma_1(1/2),\gamma_2(1/2))^\beta.\] Then, for every c-convex function \(\psi\), there is a set \(Z\subset M\) with \(\dim_H Z\le (n-1)/\beta<n\) such that \(\partial_c\psi(x)\) contains at most one element for every \(x\notin Z\). Consequently, \(Z\) has zero n-dimensional measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the classical Lagrangian-cost hypotheses, Assumption C, and the stated uniform shortening estimate with exponent beta greater than 1−1/n, every c-convex potential has a c-subdifferential containing at most one point outside an exceptional set of Hausdorff dimension at most (n−1)/beta.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is real-valued, bounded below, and derived from a Lagrangian satisfying the classical conditions of Definition 7.6.
For every c-convex \(\psi\) and every \(x\in M\), \(\partial_c\psi(x)\) is pathwise connected.
The stated shortening inequality holds uniformly with \(\beta>1-1/n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall\psi\text{ c-convex},\ \exists Z\subset M:\ \dim_H Z\le (n-1)/\beta<n\ \text{and}\ |\partial_c\psi(x)|\le1\ \forall x\notin Z.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Uniform Optimal Assignment Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equal-cardinality, uniformly weighted discrete specialization of the Monge transport problem, including the factorial size of its permutation search space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a cost matrix \(\mathbf C=(C_{ij})_{i\in\llbracket n\rrbracket,\,j\in\llbracket m\rrbracket}\) with \(n=m\), the optimal assignment problem is
\[
\min_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Perm}(n)}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}C_{i,\sigma(i)}.
\]
The feasible set contains \(|\operatorname{Perm}(n)|=n!\) permutations, so exhaustive evaluation requires considering \(n!\) assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equal-size cost matrix, the optimal assignment problem minimizes the average matched cost over all permutations. Its feasible set has n! elements, making exhaustive enumeration factorial in size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Perm}(n)}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}C_{i,\sigma(i)},\qquad |\operatorname{Perm}(n)|=n!

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-cost generalized transport with distinct source-regularity and geometric representation branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a smooth n-dimensional Riemannian manifold, let \(c(x,y)=d(x,y)^2\), and let \(\mu,
u\in\mathcal P(M)\). If \(\mu\) gives zero mass to every set of dimension at most \(n-1\), then there is a unique transport map \(T\) solving the generalized Monge problem. If \(\mu\ll\operatorname{vol}_M\), then \(T(x)=\exp_x(\widetilde

abla\psi\) in place of \(\widetilde
abla\psi\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness of deterministic c-cyclically monotone transport, with separate approximate- and true-gradient branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X\) be a closed subset of an n-dimensional Riemannian manifold \(M\) with \(\dim(\partial\mathcal X)\le n-1\), let \(\mathcal Y\) be Polish, and let \(c:M	imes\mathcal Y	o\mathbb R\) be continuous and bounded below. For \(\mu\in\mathcal P(M)\) and \(
u\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\), assume \((\mathrm{locSC})\), \((\mathrm{Twist})\), and that \(\mu\) gives zero mass to every set of dimension at most \(n-1\). Then there is a unique-in-law c-cyclically monotone coupling \(\pi\) of \(\mu\) and \(
u\); it is deterministic, and there is a c-convex \(\psi:M	o\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) such that \(\pi[\partial_c\psi]=1\). If \(\mu\ll\operatorname{vol}_M\), then \(\widetilde
abla\psi(x)+
abla_xc(x,y)=0\) for \(\pi\)-almost every \((x,y)\). Alternatively, retaining the original source-measure assumption and adding \((\mathbf H_\infty)\) or \((\mathrm{SC})\), one has \(
abla\psi(x)+

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stability of the selected Monge map under strictly convex cost approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence in source-measure of optimal maps for strictly convex radial costs approaching Euclidean distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^n)\) have finite first moments and \(\mu\ll\mathcal L^n\). Let \((\phi_\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}\) be nonnegative, nondecreasing, strictly convex functions on \(\mathbb R_+\) such that, for each \(d\ge0\), the map \(\varepsilon\mapsto\phi_\varepsilon(d)\) is convex, \(\phi_\varepsilon(d)\to d\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and its right derivative at \(0\) is \(\phi(d)\), where \(\phi\) is real-valued, strictly convex, and bounded below. Suppose that for some \(\varepsilon_0>0\), \(\int\phi_{\varepsilon_0}(|x-y|)\,d\pi(x,y)<\infty\) for every \(\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\). If \(T_\varepsilon\) is an optimal Monge map for cost \(\phi_\varepsilon(|x-y|)\) and \(T\) is the map selected by the secondary principle for Euclidean-distance transport, then \(T_\varepsilon\to T\) in \(\mu\)-measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal Monge maps for the strictly convex approximating costs converge in source-measure to the uniquely selected optimal map for Euclidean distance.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^n)\) have finite first moments and \(\mu\ll\mathcal L^n\)
Each \(\phi_\varepsilon:\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R_+\) is nondecreasing and strictly convex
For every \(d\ge0\), \(\varepsilon\mapsto\phi_\varepsilon(d)\) is convex and \(\phi_\varepsilon(d)\to d\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\)
\(\partial_\varepsilon^+\phi_\varepsilon(d)|_{\varepsilon=0}=\phi(d)\), where \(\phi\) is real-valued, strictly convex, and bounded below
\(T_\varepsilon\) is an optimal Monge map for cost \(\phi_\varepsilon(|x-y|)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall\delta>0,\quad\mu\bigl(\{x:|T_\varepsilon(x)-T(x)|>\delta\}\bigr)\to0\quad\text{as }\varepsilon\downarrow0.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique Monge Map under Superdifferentiability, Twist, and Potential Differentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-cost existence, uniqueness, determinism, and additional characterization and support conclusions under the condition at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a Riemannian manifold, let \(\mathcal X\subset M\) be closed with \(\dim(\partial\mathcal X)\le n-1\), and let \(\mathcal Y\) be Polish. Suppose \(c:\mathcal X	imes\mathcal Y	o\mathbb R\) is continuous and bounded below, \(\mu\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X)\), \(
u\in\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\), and \(C(\mu,
u)<\infty\). Assume \((\mathrm{Super})\), \((\mathrm{Twist})\), and that every c-convex function is differentiable \(\mu\)-almost surely on its domain of c-subdifferentiability. Then the optimal coupling is unique in law and deterministic, and there is a c-convex \(\psi\) satisfying \(
abla\psi(x)+
abla_xc(x,y)=0\) almost surely. Equivalently, a unique transport map \(T\), up to \(\mu\)-almost-everywhere equality, solves the Monge problem and satisfies \(
abla\psi(x)+
abla_xc(x,T(x))=0\) \(\mu\)-almost surely. If \((\mathbf H_\infty)\) also holds, the equation characterizes the optimal coupling; on the differentiability set \(Z\) of \(\psi\), \(T(x)\in\partial_c\psi(x)\) defines a continuous map, and \(\operatorname{Spt}
u=\overline{T(\operatorname{Spt}\mu)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated finite-cost problem, Super, Twist, and almost-everywhere differentiability of c-convex potentials imply a unique deterministic optimal coupling and Monge map satisfying the potential-gradient equation. Under H-infinity, that equation characterizes optimality, the map is continuous on the potential's differentiability set, and the target support is the closure of the source-support image.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Equivalence of Semiconvexity and Subdifferentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Riemannian nonsmooth regularity, including the rectifiability boundary of an extended-real-valued function's finite domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a smooth complete \(n\)-dimensional Riemannian manifold. If \(\psi:M\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is locally semiconvex and \(D=\psi^{-1}(\mathbb R)\), then \(\psi\) is locally subdifferentiable on \(\operatorname{int}D\), and \(\partial D\) is countably \((n-1)\)-rectifiable. Conversely, if \(U\subset M\) is open and \(\psi:U\to\mathbb R\) is locally subdifferentiable, then \(\psi\) is locally semiconvex. The analogous assertions hold with subdifferentiability and semiconvexity replaced by superdifferentiability and semiconcavity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a smooth complete Riemannian manifold, a locally semiconvex extended-real-valued function is locally subdifferentiable in the interior of its finite domain, whose boundary is countably codimension-one rectifiable. Conversely, a locally subdifferentiable real-valued function on an open set is locally semiconvex. The sign-reversed semiconcave statement also holds.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a smooth complete }n\text{-dimensional Riemannian manifold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \psi\text{ locally semiconvex}\Rightarrow \psi\text{ locally subdifferentiable on }\operatorname{int}D\text{ and }\partial D\text{ countably }(n-1)\text{-rectifiable};\quad \psi:U\to\mathbb R\text{ locally subdifferentiable}\Rightarrow\psi\text{ locally semiconvex}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity and Twist Properties of Lagrangian Cost Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Properties of an action-minimizing cost on a smooth Riemannian manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c(x,y)\) be the cost associated with a \(C^1\) Lagrangian \(L(x,v,t)\) on a smooth Riemannian manifold \(M\), and suppose every \(x,y\in M\) can be joined by a \(C^1\) minimizing curve. For every minimizing curve \(\gamma\) from \(x\) to \(y\),
\[
-\nabla_vL(x,\dot\gamma(0),0)\in\nabla_x^+c(x,y),
\]
so \(c(\cdot,y)\) is superdifferentiable at \(x\). If \(L\) is strictly convex in \(v\) and minimizing curves are determined uniquely by their initial position and velocity, then differentiability of \(c(\cdot,y)\) at \(x\) implies that \(y\) is uniquely determined by \(x\) and \(\nabla_xc(x,y)\), and the unique minimizer satisfies
\[
\nabla_xc(x,y)+\nabla_vL(x,\dot\gamma(0),0)=0.
\]
If, for every pair of compact sets \(K_0,K_1\subset M\), the velocities of minimizing curves from \(K_0\) to \(K_1\) are uniformly bounded, then \(c\) is locally Lipschitz and locally semiconcave in \(x\), locally in \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimizing Lagrangian trajectory supplies a supergradient of the induced cost through its initial momentum. Strict velocity convexity and uniqueness from initial data yield the twist property and identify the cost gradient with negative initial momentum. Uniform velocity bounds for minimizers between compact sets imply local Lipschitz continuity and local semiconcavity in the initial point, locally in the endpoint.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a smooth Riemannian manifold}
c\text{ is the cost associated with }L
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\nabla_vL(x,\dot\gamma(0),0)\in\nabla_x^+c(x,y);\quad \text{under strict convexity and trajectory uniqueness, }c\text{ satisfies twist};\quad \text{uniform compact-to-compact velocity bounds imply local Lipschitzness and semiconcavity}

notation.meaning: Coupling concentrated on the graph of T

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible maps and their graph-supported transport plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A deterministic transport map from \(\mu\) to \(\nu\) is a measurable function \(T:X\to Y\) satisfying
\[
T_\#\mu=\nu.
\]
It induces the coupling \(\gamma_T:=(\operatorname{id}_X,T)_\#\mu\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\), which is concentrated on the graph of \(T\). Its transport cost is
\[
\mathcal M_c(T):=\int_X c(x,T(x))\,d\mu(x)=\int_{X\times Y}c(x,y)\,d\gamma_T(x,y).
\]
The feasible deterministic class consists of all measurable maps satisfying the pushforward constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic transport map pushes the source measure to the target and induces a coupling concentrated on its graph.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Transport Maps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits Deterministic Transport Maps, and the pushforward constraint and induced coupling are standard. No source locator is supplied. Moreover, for arbitrary measurable spaces the graph of a measurable map need not be product-measurable, so the assertion that the coupling is concentrated on the graph requires suitable measurable-space hypotheses or a formulation avoiding measurable graph mass.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A Monge-solution theorem obtained from almost-everywhere at-most-one-valued c-subdifferentials.

Let \(M\) be an \(n\)-dimensional Riemannian manifold, let \(c\) be a cost on \(M	imes M\) with associated cost functional \(C\), and let \(\mu,
u\) be probability measures on \(M\). Assume \(C(\mu,
u)<+\infty\), the assumptions of Theorem 9.2 hold with exponent \( eta\), and \(\mu(E)=0\) for every set \(E\) of dimension at most \((n-1)/ eta\). Then there is a unique optimal transport plan \(\pi\); it is deterministic. Among couplings of \((\mu,

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Injectivity of intermediate maps induced by a deterministic optimal transport map.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Anisotropic quadratic transports converge to Knothe–Rosenblatt transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit theorem for quadratic transport costs whose coordinate weights are asymptotically separated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d)\) be absolutely continuous with compact supports. For \(\lambda_i(\varepsilon)>0\), let \(\gamma_\varepsilon\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) minimize \(c_\varepsilon(x,y)=\sum_{i=1}^d\lambda_i(\varepsilon)(x_i-y_i)^2\), and suppose \(\lambda_k(\varepsilon)/\lambda_{k+1}(\varepsilon)\to0\) for every \(k=1,\ldots,d-1\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurable-map feasibility for the Monge problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A measurable map \(T:X\to Y\) is a feasible transport map from \(\mu\) to \(\nu\) when its pushforward equals the target measure:
\[
T_\#\mu=\nu,
\qquad
\text{equivalently }\mu(T^{-1}(B))=\nu(B)\text{ for every Borel }B\subseteq Y.
\]
The feasible Monge class is
\[
\mathcal T(\mu,\nu):=\{T:X\to Y:T\text{ is measurable and }T_\#\mu=\nu\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic transport is feasible precisely when the mass that its measurable map sends into every target Borel set equals the target measure of that set.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Transport Maps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically precise and fits the leaf, but no inspectable transport reference is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The obstruction is non-Dirac conditional transport from a positive-mass set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The coupling \(\pi\) is induced by a deterministic transport map exactly when there is a measurable \(T:X\to Y\) such that
\[
\kappa_x=\delta_{T(x)}\quad\text{for }\mu\text{-almost every }x.
\]
Consequently, if the set of \(x\) for which \(\kappa_x\) assigns positive mass to two disjoint Borel subsets of \(Y\) has positive \(\mu\)-measure, then \(\pi\) cannot equal \((\mathrm{id},T)_\#\mu\) for any map \(T\). This is the mass-splitting obstruction to Monge representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transport plan is deterministic exactly when almost every source point has a Dirac conditional destination law; genuine conditional splitting prevents representation by a map.
knowledge_statements.title: Mass-Splitting Obstructions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification and disintegration criterion fit the leaf, but the claim lacks an inspectable authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Source Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic feasibility boundary for a countably atomic source measure with distinct atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu=\sum_{i\in I}a_i\delta_{x_i}\), where the points \(x_i\) are pairwise distinct. A feasible deterministic transport from \(\mu\) to \(\nu\) exists if and only if there are points \(y_i\in Y\) such that
\[
\nu=\sum_{i\in I}a_i\delta_{y_i}.
\]
Thus each source atom must be transported as a whole, although the masses of multiple atoms may merge at a common destination. In particular, no purely atomic source admits a deterministic transport to a nonatomic target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A countably atomic source can reach exactly those targets obtained by sending each whole source atom to one destination, with masses allowed to merge at common destinations.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is countable, the points \((x_i)_{i\in I}\subseteq X\) are pairwise distinct, \(a_i>0\), and \(\sum_{i\in I}a_i=1\).
\(X\) and \(Y\) are standard Borel spaces, \(\mu=\sum_{i\in I}a_i\delta_{x_i}\), and \(\nu\in\mathcal P(Y)\).

u)
eq\varnothing\) if and only if \(
u=\sum_{i\in I}a_i\delta_{y_i}\) for some family \((y_i)_{i\in I}\subseteq Y\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set \(\{(\mathrm{id},T)_\#\mu:T_\#\mu=\nu\}\) is not convex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvexity of graph-supported couplings with fixed marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(T_0(x)=0\) on \([0,1/2)\) and \(T_0(x)=1\) on \([1/2,1]\), and let \(T_1=1-T_0\). Both maps satisfy \((T_j)_\#\mu=\nu\). However, for
\[
\bar\pi:=\tfrac12(\mathrm{id},T_0)_\#\mu+\tfrac12(\mathrm{id},T_1)_\#\mu,
\]
the conditional destination law at every \(x\) is \(\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac12\delta_1\). Hence \(\bar\pi\) is not induced by any measurable map, although its two endpoints are feasible Monge couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two feasible graph couplings may have a midpoint that splits every source point between destinations and therefore is not a graph coupling.
knowledge_statements.title: Monge-Class Nonconvexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit counterexample correctly establishes Monge-class nonconvexity and the selected knowledge kind fits, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Monge-Class Nonclosure
children.top_down_role: Limits of map-induced plans that leave the deterministic class.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible Monge couplings are not closed under weak convergence in \(\mathcal P(X\times Y)\).

notation.meaning: Fractional part of a real number.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical oscillating-map counterexample to weak closure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak nonclosure caused by increasingly fine deterministic oscillations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\geq1\), define
\[
T_n(x):=\mathbf 1_{[1/2,1)}(\{nx\}).
\]
Each \(T_n\) pushes \(\mu\) to \(\nu\), so \(\pi_n=(\mathrm{id},T_n)_\#\mu\) is a feasible Monge coupling. As \(n\to\infty\),
\[
\pi_n\rightharpoonup\mu\otimes\nu.
\]
The limiting plan has conditional destination law \(\nu\) at every source point and is therefore not induced by a map. Thus the Monge class is not weakly closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rapidly oscillating feasible maps converge weakly to an independent coupling that splits mass at every source point and lies outside the Monge class.
knowledge_statements.title: Monge-Class Nonclosure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oscillating-map counterexample is mathematically appropriate for weak nonclosure, but it lacks an inspectable authoritative source.

children.title: Relaxed Limits Outside the Monge Class
children.top_down_role: General transport plans arising as limits of deterministic approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Limits Outside the Monge Class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disintegration-kernel representation of weak limits of deterministic graph measures on Polish spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The weak limit admits a disintegration kernel \(x\mapsto\kappa_x\) satisfying
\[
\int_{X\times Y}f(x,y)\,d\pi(x,y)
=
\int_X\left(\int_Y f(x,y)\,d\kappa_x(y)\right)d\mu(x)
\]
for every bounded Borel function \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\). The limiting plan belongs to the Monge class if and only if there is a measurable map \(T:X\to Y\) such that \(\kappa_x=\delta_{T(x)}\) for \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\). A non-Dirac conditional kernel therefore represents relaxed mass splitting outside the Monge class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weak limit of graph plans is represented by a conditional destination kernel and remains deterministic exactly when that kernel is almost everywhere Dirac.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are Polish spaces, \(\mu\in\mathcal P(X)\), and \(T_n:X\to Y\) is Borel measurable for every \(n\).
The first marginal of \(\pi\) is \(\mu\), and \(\pi(dx,dy)=\mu(dx)\kappa_x(dy)\) is a disintegration over that marginal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limit \(\pi\) is represented by \(x\mapsto\kappa_x\), and \(\pi=(\mathrm{id}_X,T)_\#\mu\) for some measurable \(T\) if and only if \(\kappa_x\) is Dirac for \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\).

notation.meaning: Conditional probability kernel of the limiting plan given the source point.
Weak convergence of probability measures on the stated Polish space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flat-torus squared distance and cut locus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the quadratic transport cost on the flat torus and records its minimizer, regularity, and cut-locus properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb T^d=\mathbb R^d/\mathbb Z^d\), define \(|[z]|:=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}|z+k|\), and set \(c(x,y)=\tfrac12|[x-y]|^2\). A minimizing lattice vector always exists. If \(z\in Q=[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12]^d\), a minimizer belongs to \(\{-1,0,1\}^d\), and it is unique and equal to \(0\) when \(z\notin\partial Q\); uniqueness fails on \(\partial Q\). The function \(z\mapsto\tfrac12|[z]|^2\) is semiconcave and is differentiable wherever the minimizing lattice vector is unique. For every \(x\in\mathbb T^d\), \(\operatorname{cut}(x)=\{y\in\mathbb T^d:y-x\in\partial Q+\mathbb Z^d\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the flat torus, distance is obtained by minimizing Euclidean distance over lattice translates. On the fundamental cube the minimizing translate is uniquely zero away from the boundary, while boundary points produce nonuniqueness. The squared distance is semiconcave and differentiable at points with a unique minimizing translate, and the cut locus of x consists exactly of points whose displacement from x lies on a translated boundary of the fundamental cube.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{cut}(x)=\{y:y-x\in\partial Q+\mathbb Z^d\},\quad z\mapsto\tfrac12|[z]|^2\text{ is semiconcave and differentiable whenever the minimizing }k\text{ is unique}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Uniqueness for Strictly Convex Displacement Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-domain transport with a strictly convex displacement cost. The extract uses \(\nabla h\) and its inverse without separately stating the corresponding smoothness and range hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu\) and \(\nu\) be probability measures on a compact domain \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d\), and let
\[
c(x,y)=h(x-y)
\]
with \(h\) strictly convex. Then an optimal transport plan exists. If additionally \(\mu\ll\mathcal L^d\) and \(\mathcal L^d(\partial\Omega)=0\), the optimal plan is unique and has the form
\[
\gamma=(\operatorname{id},T)_\#\mu.
\]
There exists a Kantorovich potential \(\varphi\), and, at the relevant points where the displayed gradients and inverse are defined,
\[
T(x)=x-(\nabla h)^{-1}(\nabla\varphi(x)).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly convex displacement cost on a compact Euclidean domain admits an optimal plan. With an absolutely continuous source and negligible domain boundary, the plan is unique, is induced by a map, and the map is recovered from a Kantorovich potential through the stated gradient formula.
assumptions_latex: \mu\ll\mathcal L^d\text{ and }\mathcal L^d(\partial\Omega)=0\text{ for uniqueness and Monge representation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\gamma\text{ optimal};\quad \mu\ll\mathcal L^d,\ \mathcal L^d(\partial\Omega)=0\Rightarrow \gamma=(\operatorname{id},T)_\#\mu\text{ uniquely, and }T(x)=x-(\nabla h)^{-1}(\nabla\varphi(x))\text{ where defined}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality condition and discrete velocity of a Fokker–Planck JKO step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euler condition expressed through the unique Kantorovich potential and optimal transport map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_{k+1}^\tau\) be the minimizer of the Fokker\text{--}Planck JKO step, and let \(\bar\varphi\) be the unique Kantorovich potential transporting \(\rho_{k+1}^\tau\) to \(\rho_k^\tau\). Then \[\log\rho_{k+1}^\tau+V+\frac{\bar\varphi}{\tau}=c\quad\text{a.e.}\] for some constant \(c\), so \(\log\rho_{k+1}^\tau\) is Lipschitz. If \(T_k^\tau\) is the optimal transport map from \(\rho_{k+1}^\tau\) to \(\rho_k^\tau\), then \[v_k^\tau:=\frac{\operatorname{id}-T_k^\tau}{\tau}=-\nabla\bigl(\log\rho_{k+1}^\tau+V\bigr)\quad\text{a.e.}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a Fokker–Planck JKO minimizer, the log-density plus the potential and the scaled Kantorovich potential is constant almost everywhere. Consequently the log-density is Lipschitz, and the discrete transport velocity equals the negative gradient of the log-density plus the potential.
assumptions_latex: \bar\varphi\text{ is the unique Kantorovich potential from }\rho_{k+1}^\tau\text{ to }\rho_k^\tau
T_k^\tau\text{ is the corresponding optimal transport map}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal static transport-plan formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The admissible transport plans are
\[
\Pi(\mu,\nu):=\{\pi\in\mathcal P(X\times Y):(p_X)_\#\pi=\mu,\ (p_Y)_\#\pi=\nu\}.
\]
The Kantorovich problem is represented by
\[
K_c(\mu,\nu):=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\int_{X\times Y}c(x,y)\,d\pi(x,y).
\]
Every feasible map \(T\) yields the graph plan \((\mathrm{id},T)_\#\mu\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\), while general plans may distribute the mass at one source point among several destinations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kantorovich transport minimizes expected cost over all joint probability measures having the prescribed source and target marginals, thereby relaxing deterministic graph transports.

knowledge_statements.title: Existence by Direct Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence for lower-semicontinuous, bounded-below costs on Polish spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The coupling set \(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) is nonempty and weakly compact, and the functional
\[
\pi\longmapsto\int_{X\times Y}c(x,y)\,d\pi(x,y)
\]
is weakly lower semicontinuous. The Kantorovich infimum is attained: there exists \(\pi^\star\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) such that
\[
\int_{X\times Y}c\,d\pi^\star
=
\min_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\int_{X\times Y}c\,d\pi
=
K_c(\mu,\nu).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a lower-semicontinuous bounded-below cost on Polish spaces, every finite Kantorovich problem has an optimal transport plan.

knowledge_statements.title: Stability Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of value stability under weak convergence alone for an unbounded cost without moment control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The marginals satisfy \(\mu_n\rightharpoonup\delta_0\) and \(\nu_n\rightharpoonup\delta_0\). Because the target is \(\delta_0\), the only coupling gives
\[
K_c(\mu_n,\nu_n)=\int_{\mathbb R}|x|\,d\mu_n(x)=1
\quad\text{for every }n.
\]
The limiting value is
\[
K_c(\delta_0,\delta_0)=0.
\]
Thus weak marginal convergence alone does not ensure value stability for an unbounded cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A single map-induced Kantorovich optimizer is uniquely characterized by minimizing every bounded-below strictly convex function of transport distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

u\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^n)\) have finite first moments, let \(\mu\ll\mathcal L^n\), and let \(\Pi_*(\mu,
u)\) denote the Kantorovich-optimal plans for \(c(x,y)=|x-y|\). There exists a unique \(\pi=(\operatorname{Id}	imes T)_\#\mu\in\Pi_*(\mu,

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity of a c-convex potential under the combined behavior-at-infinity hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \((\mathrm H\infty)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Discrete Kantorovich relaxation and coupling polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines mass-splitting couplings with prescribed marginals, their polyhedral and transpose-symmetry properties, and the resulting discrete optimal-transport linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf a\in\mathbb R_+^n\) and \(\mathbf b\in\mathbb R_+^m\) have equal total mass. The discrete Kantorovich relaxation replaces a deterministic transport assignment by a coupling \(\mathbf P\) in
\[
\mathbf U(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\{\mathbf P\in\mathbb R_+^{n\times m}:\mathbf P\mathbb 1_m=\mathbf a,\ \mathbf P^{\mathsf T}\mathbb 1_n=\mathbf b\}.
\]
The set \(\mathbf U(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\) is a bounded convex polytope, and
\[
\mathbf P\in\mathbf U(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\iff \mathbf P^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbf U(\mathbf b,\mathbf a).
\]
For \(\mathbf C\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), the Kantorovich transport value is
\[
L_{\mathbf C}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\min_{\mathbf P\in\mathbf U(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)}\langle\mathbf C,\mathbf P\rangle
=\min_{\mathbf P\in\mathbf U(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)}\sum_{i,j}C_{ij}P_{ij}.
\]
This is a linear program, and its optimal coupling need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative source and target histograms having equal total mass, the Kantorovich relaxation permits mass splitting. Couplings are nonnegative matrices with the prescribed row and column sums; they form a bounded convex polytope and transpose into couplings with the marginals reversed. Minimizing transport cost over this set is a linear program whose optimizer need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf U(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\{\mathbf P\ge 0:\mathbf P\mathbb 1_m=\mathbf a,\ \mathbf P^{\mathsf T}\mathbb 1_n=\mathbf b\}\text{ is a bounded convex polytope},\quad \mathbf P\in\mathbf U(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\iff\mathbf P^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbf U(\mathbf b,\mathbf a),\quad L_{\mathbf C}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\min_{\mathbf P\in\mathbf U(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)}\langle\mathbf C,\mathbf P\rangle.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence for continuous transport costs on compact spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kantorovich minimization with compact metric marginals and a finite continuous cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let X and Y be compact metric spaces, let \mu\in\mathcal P(X) and 
u\in\mathcal P(Y), and let c:X	imes Y	o\mathbb R be continuous. Then there exists \gamma^\star\in\Pi(\mu,
u) such that \int_{X	imes Y}c\,d\gamma^\star=\min_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,
u)}\int_{X	imes Y}c\,d\gamma.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For probability measures on compact metric spaces and a continuous real-valued cost, the Kantorovich transport problem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\gamma^\star\in\Pi(\mu,\nu):\ \int_{X\times Y}c\,d\gamma^\star=\min_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\int_{X\times Y}c\,d\gamma.

notation.meaning: Pushforward of the source measure by the graph map.
Set of couplings having the prescribed marginals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-supported Kantorovich plans generated by deterministic transport maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The plan induced by \(T\) is \(\gamma_T:=(\operatorname{Id}_X,T)_\#\mu\), characterized by \[\int_{X\times Y}f(x,y)\,d\gamma_T(x,y)=\int_X f(x,T(x))\,d\mu(x)\] for every bounded Borel function \(f:X\times Y\to\mathbb R\). Its first marginal is \(\mu\), its second marginal is \(T_\#\mu\), and it is concentrated on the graph of \(T\). Consequently, \(\gamma_T\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) if and only if \(T_\#\mu=\nu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A measurable map induces a plan concentrated on its graph; this plan has the required marginals precisely when the map pushes the source measure to the target measure.
knowledge_statements.title: Map-Induced Plans

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically precise and fits the Map-Induced Plans container, but no inspectable citation or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak density of deterministic transport plans for an atomless source measure on a compact Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact Euclidean domain, every coupling with an atomless source measure is a weak limit of transport plans induced by measurable transport maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \overline{\{(\operatorname{id},T)_{\#}\mu:T_{\#}\mu=\nu\}}^{\,\mathrm{weak}}=\Pi(\mu,\nu).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Narrow Convergence of Map-Induced Plans
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between convergence of maps and convergence of their graph plans under a fixed reference measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X,Y$ be separable metric spaces, $\mu\in\mathcal P(X)$, and let $\mathbf r_n,\mathbf r:X\to Y$ be Borel maps. Then $(\mathbf i\times\mathbf r_n)_\#\mu\rightharpoonup(\mathbf i\times\mathbf r)_\#\mu$ narrowly in $\mathcal P(X\times Y)$ iff $\mathbf r_n\to\mathbf r$ in $\mu$-measure. Under these equivalent conditions, for $1\le p<\infty$, one has $\mathbf r_n\to\mathbf r$ in $L^p(\mu;Y)$ iff the pushforwards $(\mathbf r_n)_\#\mu$ have uniformly integrable $p$-moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For Borel maps defined on a fixed probability space, their graph plans converge narrowly to the graph plan of a limiting map exactly when the maps converge in measure. Under this convergence, convergence in Lp is equivalent to uniform integrability of the p-moments of the image measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mathbf i\times\mathbf r_n)_\#\mu\rightharpoonup(\mathbf i\times\mathbf r)_\#\mu\iff\mathbf r_n\to\mathbf r\text{ in measure};\quad \mathbf r_n\to\mathbf r\text{ in }L^p\iff\{(\mathbf r_n)_\#\mu\}\text{ has uniformly integrable }p\text{-moments under these equivalent conditions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists a lower semicontinuous convex function \(\varphi:\mathbb R^d	o(-\infty,+\infty]\) such that \(T:=

u\), and minimizes the Monge objective. Moreover, \(\gamma:=(\operatorname{Id},T)_\#\mu\) is the unique minimizer in \(\Pi(\mu,

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criterion for Unique Solvability of the Monge Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions ensuring that the Kantorovich optimizer is unique, deterministic, and therefore yields the unique Monge solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\mathcal X,\mu)$ and $(\mathcal Y,
u)$ be Polish probability spaces. Let $a\in L^1(\mu)$ and $b\in L^1(
u)$ be real-valued upper semicontinuous functions, and let $c:\mathcal X	imes\mathcal Y	o\mathbb R$ be lower semicontinuous with $c(x,y)\ge a(x)+b(y)$ for all $(x,y)$. Suppose $C(\mu,
u)<+\infty$ and, for every $c$-convex function $\psi:\mathcal X	o\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, the set $\{x\in\mathcal X:|\partial_c\psi(x)|>1\}$ is $\mu$-negligible. Then there is a unique-in-law optimal coupling $(X,Y)$ of $(\mu,
u)$, and it is deterministic. Among all couplings, it is characterized by the existence of a $c$-convex function $\psi$ such that $Y\in\partial_c\psi(X)$ almost surely. Consequently, the Monge problem from $\mu$ to $
u$ admits a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assume the stated semicontinuity, integrable lower-bound, and finite-cost conditions. If the c-subdifferential of every c-convex function contains at most one point for almost every source point, then the optimal coupling is unique in law and is induced by a transport map. It is characterized by lying almost surely in the c-subdifferential of a c-convex potential, and the Monge problem has a unique solution.
assumptions_latex: (\mathcal X,\mu)\text{ and }(\mathcal Y,\nu)\text{ are Polish probability spaces}
a\in L^1(\mu),\quad b\in L^1(\nu),\quad a,b\text{ are real-valued and upper semicontinuous}
c:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\to\mathbb R\text{ is lower semicontinuous and }c(x,y)\ge a(x)+b(y)\quad\forall(x,y)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\text{ an optimal coupling in law};\ \text{it is deterministic and is characterized by }Y\in\partial_c\psi(X)\ \text{a.s. for some }c\text{-convex }\psi;\ \text{hence the Monge problem admits a unique solution.}
