knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dacorogna–Moser realization of a divergence-constrained flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructs a deterministic transport plan realizing a sufficiently regular divergence-constrained vector field without directional cancellation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\mathbf w:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) is Lipschitz, \(\mathbf w\cdot\mathbf n=0\) on \(\partial\Omega\), and \(\nabla\cdot\mathbf w=f_0-f_1\), where \(f_0,f_1\) are Lipschitz probability densities bounded below by positive constants. Define \(f_t=(1-t)f_0+tf_1\) and \(\mathbf v_t=\mathbf w/f_t\), and solve \(y_x'(t)=\mathbf v_t(y_x(t))\), \(y_x(0)=x\). Let \(Y(x)=y_x(\cdot)\) and \(Q=Y_\#(f_0\,dx)\). Then \((e_t)_\#Q=f_t\,dx\) for every \(t\in[0,1]\). Consequently, \(x\mapsto y_x(1)\) transports \(f_0\,dx\) to \(f_1\,dx\), and \(\mathbf w_Q=\mathbf w\,dx\) and \(i_Q=|\mathbf w|\,dx=|\mathbf w_Q|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interpolate linearly between the two strictly positive densities and divide the prescribed vector field by that interpolation. The resulting nonautonomous flow transports the first density to the second. Its path measure realizes the original flow exactly, and its traffic intensity equals the flow magnitude, so no directional cancellation occurs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (e_t)_\#Q=f_t\,dx,\qquad (y_{(\cdot)}(1))_\#(f_0\,dx)=f_1\,dx,\qquad \mathbf w_Q=\mathbf w\,dx,\qquad i_Q=|\mathbf w|\,dx=|\mathbf w_Q|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Energy Representation and Cycle-Free Structure of Optimal Traffic Plans
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The occurrence $\theta_O$ in the extracted set definition is interpreted as the contextually consistent $\theta_Q$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every traffic plan $Q$ with $I_\alpha(Q)<+\infty$, let $\Gamma=\{x:\theta_Q(x)>0\}$. Then $\Gamma$ is sigma-finite with respect to $\mathcal H^1$ and $I_\alpha(Q)=\int_\Gamma\theta_Q^{\alpha-1}m_Q\,d\mathcal H^1$. If $Q$ is optimal, then it is concentrated on loop-free curves, $I_\alpha(Q)=\int_\Gamma\theta_Q^\alpha\,d\mathcal H^1$, and $Q$ is cycle-free.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite-energy traffic plan has an H^1-sigma-finite positive-multiplicity set and an integral energy representation. An optimal plan is supported on loop-free curves, its energy is the integral of theta_Q to the alpha power, and it is cycle-free.
assumptions_latex: Q\text{ is optimal for the loop-free, simplified-energy, and cycle-free conclusions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Gamma\text{ is }\mathcal H^1\text{-sigma-finite},\quad I_\alpha(Q)=\int_\Gamma\theta_Q^{\alpha-1}m_Q\,d\mathcal H^1;\qquad Q\text{ optimal}\Rightarrow I_\alpha(Q)=\int_\Gamma\theta_Q^\alpha\,d\mathcal H^1\text{ and }Q\text{ is loop-free and cycle-free}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reparametrization and weak-limit properties of traffic measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collects invariance, mass, lower-semicontinuity, and flow-stability properties of traffic intensity and traffic flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be a traffic plan. If \(T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C\) sends every curve to an admissible time reparametrization of the same oriented curve, then \(\mathbf w_{T_\#Q}=\mathbf w_Q\) and \(i_{T_\#Q}=i_Q\). Moreover, \(i_Q(\Omega)=\int_{\mathcal C}L(\omega)\,dQ(\omega)\), so \(i_Q\) and \(\mathbf w_Q\) are finite. If \(Q_n\rightharpoonup Q\) and \(i_{Q_n}\rightharpoonup i\), then \(i\ge i_Q\). If additionally \(\mathbf w_{Q_n}\rightharpoonup\mathbf w\), then \(\|\mathbf w-\mathbf w_Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le i(\Omega)-i_Q(\Omega)\). Hence \(Q_n\rightharpoonup Q\) and \(i_{Q_n}\rightharpoonup i_Q\) imply \(\mathbf w_{Q_n}\rightharpoonup\mathbf w_Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traffic intensity and traffic flow do not depend on the time parametrization of the oriented paths. The total intensity is the average path length. Intensity is lower semicontinuous under weak convergence, and any defect between the limiting flow and the flow induced by the limiting traffic plan is bounded by the loss of total intensity. In particular, convergence of traffic plans together with convergence of their intensities forces convergence of their flows.
assumptions_latex: Q\text{ and }Q_n\text{ are traffic plans on }\mathcal C
T(\omega)\text{ is an orientation-preserving time reparametrization of }\omega
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf w_{T_\#Q}=\mathbf w_Q,\quad i_{T_\#Q}=i_Q,\quad i_Q(\Omega)=\int L\,dQ,\quad i\ge i_Q,\quad \|\mathbf w-\mathbf w_Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le i(\Omega)-i_Q(\Omega).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finiteness and Weak-Convergence Metrization by the Branched Transport Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers the threshold $\alpha>1-1/d$, first on a cube and then on arbitrary compact domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\alpha>1-1/d$. If $\Omega=[-a,a]^d$, then $d_\alpha(\mu,\delta_0)<+\infty$ for every $\mu\in\mathcal P(\Omega)$, and consequently $d_\alpha(\mu,\nu)<+\infty$ for every $\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P(\Omega)$. The same pairwise finiteness holds on every compact domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$. Moreover, on any compact $\Omega$, $d_\alpha$ is a distance on $\mathcal P(\Omega)$ and metrizes weak convergence of probability measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When alpha is greater than 1 minus 1/d, the branched-transport cost from any probability measure on a cube to the Dirac mass at zero is finite, hence every pair has finite distance. This extends to compact domains, where d_alpha is a metric inducing weak convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_\alpha(\mu,\nu)<+\infty\quad(\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P(\Omega)),\qquad d_\alpha\text{ is a metric and }\mu_n\rightharpoonup\mu\iff d_\alpha(\mu_n,\mu)\to0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Acyclic traffic-plan component of a divergence-constrained flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposes a finite divergence-constrained vector measure into a cancellation-free traffic-plan component and a residual component with additive total variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf w\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{div}}^d(\Omega)\) be finite and let \(\mu,
u\in\mathcal P(\Omega)\) satisfy \(
abla\cdot\mathbf w=\mu-
u\). Then there exists a traffic plan \(Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal C)\) with \((e_0)_\#Q=\mu\) and \((e_1)_\#Q=
u\) such that \(|\mathbf w_Q|=i_Q\le|\mathbf w|\) as measures and \(\|\mathbf w-\mathbf w_Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}+\|\mathbf w_Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\|\mathbf w\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\). Equivalently, \(\|\mathbf w-\mathbf w_Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}+i_Q(\Omega)=\|\mathbf w\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\). Moreover, \(|\mathbf w_Q|=|\mathbf w|\) can occur only when \(\mathbf w_Q=\mathbf w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite vector measure whose divergence connects two probability measures contains a traffic-plan-induced component joining the same endpoints. That component has no directional cancellation, its intensity is dominated by the original total variation, and the total-variation norm splits additively between it and the residual. Its total-variation measure equals that of the original flow only when it is the whole flow.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf w\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{div}}^d(\Omega)\text{ is a finite vector measure}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists Q:\ (e_0)_\#Q=\mu,\ (e_1)_\#Q=\nu,\ |\mathbf w_Q|=i_Q\le|\mathbf w|,\ \|\mathbf w-\mathbf w_Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}+\|\mathbf w_Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=\|\mathbf w\|_{\mathrm{TV}},\quad |\mathbf w_Q|=|\mathbf w|\Rightarrow\mathbf w_Q=\mathbf w.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplicity Bounds, Semicontinuity, and Traffic-Intensity Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Properties of $\theta_Q$, $m_Q$, and $i_Q$ for a probability measure $Q$ on the curve space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For $Q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal C)$ and $x\in\Omega$, one has $0\le \theta_Q(x)\le m_Q(x)\le1$. If $Q$ is concentrated on loop-free curves, then $\theta_Q=m_Q$. The map $(x,Q)\mapsto\theta_Q(x)$ is upper semicontinuous when $x$ converges in $\Omega$ and $Q$ converges weakly in $\mathcal P(\mathcal C)$. Furthermore, if there is an $\mathcal H^1$-sigma-finite set $\Gamma$ such that $\omega(t)\in\Gamma$ for $Q$-almost every curve $\omega$ and almost every $t$, then $i_Q=m_Q\,\mathcal H^1$ as measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traffic-plan multiplicity satisfies zero at most theta_Q at most m_Q at most one, with theta_Q equal to m_Q for plans supported on loop-free curves. Theta_Q is jointly upper semicontinuous in the point and weakly convergent plan. If almost all trajectories lie in an H^1-sigma-finite set, the traffic intensity equals m_Q times H^1.
assumptions_latex: \Gamma\text{ is }\mathcal H^1\text{-sigma-finite and }\omega(t)\in\Gamma\text{ for }Q\text{-a.e. }\omega\text{ and a.e. }t\quad\text{for the representation conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le\theta_Q(x)\le m_Q(x)\le1;\quad Q\text{ loop-free}\Rightarrow\theta_Q=m_Q;\quad (x,Q)\mapsto\theta_Q(x)\text{ is u.s.c.};\quad i_Q=m_Q\mathcal H^1\text{ under the stated concentration condition}.

knowledge_statements.title: Divergence-Constrained Fluxes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional divergence constraint for the whole-space static Beckmann formulation of one-Wasserstein transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A flux \(w\in\mathcal M(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)\) is feasible for transport from \(\mu\) to \(\nu\) when \(-\operatorname{div}w=\mu-\nu\) in \(\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^d)\); equivalently,
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^d}\nabla\varphi(x)\cdot dw(x)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\varphi(x)\,d(\mu-\nu)(x)
\quad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^1(\mathbb R^d).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible whole-space Beckmann flux has negative distributional divergence equal to the source-minus-target measure.
assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathcal M(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)\) is a finite vector-valued Radon measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w\) is feasible exactly when \(-\operatorname{div}w=\mu-\nu\) distributionally.

notation.meaning: compactly supported continuously differentiable test functions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard distributional feasibility constraint in the whole-space Beckmann formulation

children.title: Density–Flux Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between transport densities and minimizing fluxes.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compatible transport density is \(\sigma=|w|\), with polar direction of unit norm \(\sigma\)-almost everywhere.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polar decomposition of vector measures underlying Beckmann transport density
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility in the exact transport-density representation, rather than the relaxed domination condition \(|w|\leq\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The density-flux pair \((\sigma,w)\) is compatible when \(w\ll\sigma\) and its Radon--Nikodym field \(v=dw/d\sigma\) satisfies \(|v(x)|=1\) for \(\sigma\)-almost every \(x\). Equivalently, the polar decomposition is
\[
w=v\sigma,
\qquad |v|=1\ \sigma\text{-almost everywhere},
\qquad \sigma=|w|.
\]
Consequently, the Beckmann cost obeys \(|w|(\Omega)=\sigma(\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transport density and flux are compatible when the density is exactly the flux's total variation and the flux has a unit polar direction almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Density–Flux Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact compatibility condition is mathematically coherent and the content kind fits, but no citation with an inspectable locator supports the polar-decomposition interpretation in the Beckmann setting.

children.title: Graph Metric Transport
children.top_down_role: Optimal transport over vertices and edges equipped with graph distances.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected graph with positive edge lengths \(\ell_e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Graph transport is the Kantorovich problem on \(V\) with cost equal to the weighted shortest-path distance \(d_G\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite Kantorovich transport with shortest-path ground cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite weighted-graph version of one-Wasserstein transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The graph-metric transport cost between \(a\) and \(b\) is
\[
W_{1,G}(a,b)=\min_{\pi\in\Pi(a,b)}\sum_{u,v\in V}d_G(u,v)\pi_{uv},
\]
where \(d_G(u,v)\) is the minimum total edge length among paths joining \(u\) to \(v\), and \(\Pi(a,b)\) consists of nonnegative arrays satisfying \(\sum_v\pi_{uv}=a_u\) and \(\sum_u\pi_{uv}=b_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph metric transport is finite optimal transport between vertex masses, using weighted shortest-path distance as the movement cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph Metric Transport

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite weighted-graph definition is precise and matches the leaf, but it has no inspectable citation or locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Discrete Gradient on a Graph
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edge-difference operator for vertex potentials in graph-metric transport, using an oriented-edge indexing convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \mathcal X=\llbracket 1,n\rrbracket be the vertex set of a graph with oriented edge index set \mathcal E. For \mathbf f\in\mathbb R^n, the discrete gradient \nabla:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{\mathcal E} is defined by
\[
(\nabla\mathbf f)_{i,j}:=\mathbf f_i-\mathbf f_j,\qquad (i,j)\in\mathcal E.
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of Metric-Cost c-Transforms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The c-transform for optimal transport whose source and target share a metric ground space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $(\mathcal X,d)$ be a metric space, let $\mathcal Y=\mathcal X$, and set $c(x,y)=d(x,y)$. For $f\in\mathcal C(\mathcal X)$,
\[
(\exists g\in\mathcal C(\mathcal X)\; f=g^c)\iff \operatorname{Lip}(f)\le 1.
\]
Moreover, every such $1$-Lipschitz function satisfies $f^c=-f$.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Potential and Minimum-Cost-Flow Formulations of Graph One-Wasserstein Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent edge-Lipschitz potential and nonnegative-flow formulations on a finite connected weighted graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \mathbf a,\mathbf b\in\mathbb R_+^n have equal total mass, and let \mathcal E be the oriented-arc representation of a finite connected undirected graph with nonnegative edge lengths \mathbf w_{i,j}. With the shortest-path ground metric,
\[
\mathrm W_1(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\max_{\mathbf f\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf f_i(\mathbf a_i-\mathbf b_i):\ |(\nabla\mathbf f)_{i,j}|\leq \mathbf w_{i,j}\ \forall(i,j)\in\mathcal E\right\},
\]
and
\[
\mathrm W_1(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\min_{\mathbf s\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal E}}\left\{\sum_{(i,j)\in\mathcal E}\mathbf w_{i,j}\mathbf s_{i,j}:\ \operatorname{div}(\mathbf s)=\mathbf a-\mathbf b\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For equal-mass vertex measures on a connected weighted graph, the one-Wasserstein distance equals both the maximum pairing with an edge-Lipschitz vertex potential and the minimum cost of a nonnegative edge flow having the prescribed divergence.
assumptions_latex: \text{the weighted undirected graph is finite and connected}
\mathcal E\text{ uses oriented arcs and is closed under reversal}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm W_1(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\max_{\substack{\mathbf f\in\mathbb R^n\\ |(\nabla\mathbf f)_{i,j}|\leq\mathbf w_{i,j}}}\langle\mathbf f,\mathbf a-\mathbf b\rangle=\min_{\substack{\mathbf s\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal E}\\ \operatorname{div}(\mathbf s)=\mathbf a-\mathbf b}}\sum_{(i,j)\in\mathcal E}\mathbf w_{i,j}\mathbf s_{i,j}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Discrete Divergence of a Graph Flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertex divergence of an oriented-edge flow in graph-metric transport.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete–Network Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence for measures supported on network vertices, with an explicitly fixed incidence convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Orient every edge arbitrarily and define the incidence matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{V\times E}\) by \(B_{ve}=1\) when \(v\) is the tail of \(e\), \(B_{ve}=-1\) when \(v\) is its head, and \(B_{ve}=0\) otherwise. Then
\[
W_{1,G}(a,b)=W_{1,\Gamma}(a,b)=\min\left\{\sum_{e\in E}\ell_e|q_e|:q\in\mathbb R^E,\ Bq=a-b\right\}.
\]
The value of the flux problem is unchanged if an edge orientation is reversed together with the sign of its flux coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For vertex-supported masses, graph transport and transport on the geometric network agree, and both equal the minimum weighted edge-flow cost under an explicitly signed balance constraint.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Displacement interpolations are Wasserstein geodesics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamical representation, existence, and compactness of geodesics in $P_p(\mathcal X)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(\mathcal X,d)$ be a complete, separable, locally compact length space and let $p>1$. Given $\mu_0,\mu_1\in P_p(\mathcal X)$ and a continuous curve $(\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ valued in $P(\mathcal X)$, the following are equivalent: (i) $\mu_t=\operatorname{law}(\gamma_t)$ for a random minimizing constant-speed geodesic $\gamma$ such that $(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)$ is an optimal coupling; (ii) $(\mu_t)$ is a geodesic in $(P_p(\mathcal X),W_p)$. At least one such curve exists for every endpoint pair. If $\mathcal K_0,\mathcal K_1\subset P_p(\mathcal X)$ are compact subsets of $P(\mathcal X)$, then the families of such geodesic curves and of dynamical optimal plans with endpoint marginals in $\mathcal K_0$ and $\mathcal K_1$ are compact and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous curve of probability measures is a Wasserstein geodesic exactly when its marginals arise from optimally coupled random constant-speed minimizing geodesics in the base space. Such curves exist, and compact endpoint families produce nonempty compact families of geodesics and dynamical plans.
assumptions_latex: $(\mathcal X,d)$ is complete, separable, locally compact, and a length space.
$(\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ is continuous and valued in $P(\mathcal X)$.
For compactness, $\mathcal K_0,\mathcal K_1\subset P_p(\mathcal X)$ are compact subsets of $P(\mathcal X)$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mu_t)\text{ has the dynamical optimal-geodesic representation}\iff(\mu_t)\text{ is a }W_p\text{-geodesic};\quad\text{the stated existence, compactness, and nonemptiness hold.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique optimal subplans along a constant-speed Wasserstein geodesic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior-time uniqueness, transport induction, and endpoint-plan factorization along a constant-speed geodesic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be a separable Hilbert space, let \(p>1\), and let \((\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\) be a constant-speed geodesic in \(\mathcal P_p(X)\). For every \(t\in(0,1)\), \(\Gamma_o(\mu_t,\mu_1)\) and \(\Gamma_o(\mu_0,\mu_t)\) contain unique plans \(\boldsymbol\mu^{t1}\) and \(\boldsymbol\mu^{0t}\), respectively, and each is induced by a transport. Moreover,
\[
\boldsymbol\mu:=\boldsymbol\mu^{t1}\circ\boldsymbol\mu^{0t}\in\Gamma_o(\mu_0,\mu_1),
\qquad
\boldsymbol\mu^{0t}=(\pi_t^{1,1\to2})_\#\boldsymbol\mu,
\quad
\boldsymbol\mu^{t1}=(\pi_t^{1\to2,2})_\#\boldsymbol\mu.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every interior time of a constant-speed Wasserstein geodesic, the optimal plans for its two adjacent subsegments are unique and transport-induced. Their composition is an optimal endpoint plan, and the subplans are recovered by the stated interpolation pushforwards.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ is a separable Hilbert space}
(\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\text{ is a constant-speed geodesic in }\mathcal P_p(X)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Gamma_o(\mu_0,\mu_t)=\{\boldsymbol\mu^{0t}\},\quad \Gamma_o(\mu_t,\mu_1)=\{\boldsymbol\mu^{t1}\},\quad \boldsymbol\mu^{0t},\boldsymbol\mu^{t1}\text{ are transport-induced},\quad \boldsymbol\mu^{t1}\circ\boldsymbol\mu^{0t}\in\Gamma_o(\mu_0,\mu_1)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Velocity representation of a plan-induced Wasserstein geodesic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity-equation and metric-speed representation in the inherited strictly convex displacement setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p>1\), let \(\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) be optimal for \(c(x,z)=|x-z|^p\), and set \(\mu_t=(\pi_t)_\#\gamma\), where \(\pi_t(x,z)=(1-t)x+tz\). Let \(X_t,Z_t\) be the endpoint-recovery maps. For every \(t\in(0,1)\), the field \(\mathbf v_t=Z_t-X_t\) is well defined on \(\operatorname{spt}(\mu_t)\) and satisfies
\[
\partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\!\cdot(\mu_t\mathbf v_t)=0,
\qquad
\|\mathbf v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t)}=|\mu'|(t)=W_p(\mu,\nu).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a displacement geodesic generated by an optimal p-power transport plan with p greater than one, subtracting the recovered initial point from the recovered final point gives a velocity field satisfying the continuity equation. Its L-p norm equals both the metric speed and the endpoint Wasserstein distance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between constant-speed Wasserstein geodesics and displacement interpolations generated by optimal endpoint plans.

\[
\mu_t=((1-t)p^1+tp^2)_\#\boldsymbol\alpha,
\qquad t\in[0,1],

\[
(p^{0,1})_\#\boldsymbol\alpha\in\Pi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\nu,\mu_0)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(p^{0,2})_\#\boldsymbol\alpha\in\Pi_{\mathrm{opt}}(\nu,\mu_1).
\]
The induced coupling of the two endpoint coordinates need not be optimal between \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mather's Shortening Lemma
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hölder control of the full separation of two action minimizers by their separation at one intermediate time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a smooth Riemannian manifold with geodesic distance \(d\), and let \(c\) be induced by a Lagrangian \(L(x,v,t)\) on \(TM\times[0,1]\). Suppose \(c(x_1,y_1)+c(x_2,y_2)\le c(x_1,y_2)+c(x_2,y_1)\), and let \(\gamma_i\) minimize the action from \(x_i\) to \(y_i\). Let \(V\) be a bounded neighborhood of their graphs, let \(S\) strictly exceed their maximal speeds, and set \(\mathcal V=\bigcup_{(x,t)\in V}(x,B_S(0),t)\). Assume that minimizing curves are trajectories of a Lipschitz flow, that \(L\) is \(C^{1,\alpha}\) in \((x,v)\) on \(\mathcal V\) for some \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), and that \(L\) is \((2+\kappa)\)-convex in \(v\) there. Then, for every \(t_0\in(0,1)\), there exist \(C_{t_0}=C(L,\mathcal V,t_0)\) and \(\beta=\beta(\alpha,\kappa)>0\) such that \[\sup_{0\le t\le1}d(\gamma_1(t),\gamma_2(t))\le C_{t_0}d(\gamma_1(t_0),\gamma_2(t_0))^\beta.\] If \(\alpha=1\) and \(\kappa=0\), one may take \(\beta=1\) and \(C_{t_0}=C(L,\mathcal V)/\min\{t_0,1-t_0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Lipschitz-flow, Hölder-regularity, and power-type velocity-convexity assumptions, two cost-monotone action minimizers remain uniformly close whenever they are close at one interior time. In the Lipschitz and quadratic-convexity case the estimate is linear, with deterioration proportional to the reciprocal distance from the endpoint times.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a smooth Riemannian manifold with geodesic distance }d
c\text{ is the action cost induced by }L:TM\times[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}
\mathcal V=\bigcup_{(x,t)\in V}(x,B_S(0),t)\text{ for the stated bounded neighborhood and speed bound}
\text{Minimizers are trajectories of a Lipschitz flow}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists C_{t_0}>0,\ \beta(\alpha,\kappa)>0:\ \sup_{t\in[0,1]}d(\gamma_1(t),\gamma_2(t))\le C_{t_0}d(\gamma_1(t_0),\gamma_2(t_0))^\beta

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized Wasserstein Geodesic with a Fixed Base Measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a generalized geodesic by interpolating quadratic-cost optimal transport maps from a common absolutely continuous base measure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reference distortion coefficients for curvature-dimension bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers finite dimension, the cases N=1 and N=infinity, t=0, model-space interpretation, and parameter monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\in\mathbb R\), \(N\in[1,\infty]\), \(t\in[0,1]\), and \(x,y\) belong to a metric space \((\mathcal X,d)\). For \(0<t\le1\) and \(1<N<\infty\), put \(\alpha=\sqrt{|K|/(N-1)}\,d(x,y)\) and define
\[
\beta_t^{(K,N)}(x,y)=
\begin{cases}
+\infty,&K>0,\ \alpha>\pi,\\
\left(\dfrac{\sin(t\alpha)}{t\sin\alpha}\right)^{N-1},&K>0,\ 0\le\alpha\le\pi,\\
1,&K=0,\\
\left(\dfrac{\sinh(t\alpha)}{t\sinh\alpha}\right)^{N-1},&K<0.
\end{cases}
\]
The limiting cases are
\[
\beta_t^{(K,1)}(x,y)=\begin{cases}+\infty,&K>0,\\1,&K\le0,\end{cases}
\qquad
\beta_t^{(K,\infty)}(x,y)=\exp\!\left(\frac K6(1-t^2)d(x,y)^2\right),
\]
and \(\beta_0^{(K,N)}(x,y)=1\). On the \(\operatorname{CD}(K,N)\) model space these are its distortion coefficients. Overall, \(\beta_t^{(K,N)}\) is nondecreasing in \(K\) and nonincreasing in \(N\); for \(K>0\) it increases with \(\alpha\) and decreases with \(t\), with the directions reversed for \(K<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The curvature-dimension reference coefficient is defined by trigonometric, flat, or hyperbolic comparison formulas according to the sign of K, with separate formulas for dimensions one and infinity and value one at time zero. It agrees with distortion in the model space, increases with K, and decreases with N.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \beta_t^{(K,N)}(x,y)\text{ is given by the stated comparison formulas and monotonicity properties.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Jacobi-field formula for distortion coefficients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the infimum over minimizing geodesics and the conjugate-point boundary case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be an \(n\)-dimensional Riemannian manifold and \(x,y\in M\). Then
\[
\bar\beta_t(x,y)=\inf_{\gamma}\bar\beta_t^{[\gamma]}(x,y),
\]
where \(\gamma\) ranges over minimizing geodesics from \(x\) to \(y\). If \(x\) and \(y\) are not conjugate along \(\gamma\), let \(\mathbf E\) be an orthonormal basis of \(T_yM\), and let \(\mathbf J^{0,1}\) be the Jacobi-field matrix satisfying \(\mathbf J^{0,1}(0)=0\) and \(\mathbf J^{0,1}(1)=\mathbf E\). Then
\[
\bar\beta_t^{[\gamma]}(x,y)=\frac{\det\mathbf J^{0,1}(t)}{t^n}\quad(0<t\le1),\qquad
\bar\beta_0^{[\gamma]}(x,y)=\lim_{s\to0}\frac{\det\mathbf J^{0,1}(s)}{s^n}.
\]
If the endpoints are conjugate along \(\gamma\), then \(\bar\beta_1^{[\gamma]}(x,y)=1\) and \(\bar\beta_t^{[\gamma]}(x,y)=+\infty\) for \(0\le t<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The distortion coefficient is the infimum of geodesic-specific coefficients. Along a minimizing geodesic without conjugate endpoints, the coefficient is the normalized determinant of the Jacobi-field matrix; conjugate endpoints give infinity before time one and value one at time one.
assumptions_latex: \gamma\text{ is a minimizing geodesic from }x\text{ to }y
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar\beta_t(x,y)=\inf_\gamma\bar\beta_t^{[\gamma]}(x,y)\text{ with the stated Jacobi-determinant and conjugacy formulas.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Lipschitz Transport from Intermediate Times
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trajectory separation and deterministic optimal transport induced by evaluation of a displacement interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a Riemannian manifold, let \(c\) satisfy the smooth Lagrangian assumptions of the compact-set shortening estimate, let \(K\subset M\) be compact, and let \(\Pi\) be a dynamical optimal transport supported in \(K\). Then \(\Pi\) is supported on a set \(S\) of geodesics such that, for each \(t_0\in(0,1)\), there is \(C_K(t_0)>0\) with \[\sup_{0\le t\le1}d(\gamma(t),\widetilde\gamma(t))\le C_K(t_0)d(\gamma(t_0),\widetilde\gamma(t_0))\qquad(\gamma,\widetilde\gamma\in S).\] Consequently, if \((\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\) is a displacement interpolation between compactly supported probability measures, then for every \(t_0\in(0,1)\) and \(t\in[0,1]\), the map \(T_{t_0\to t}(\gamma(t_0))=\gamma(t)\) is \(\mu_{t_0}\)-almost surely well-defined and Lipschitz on its domain, and it is the unique Monge solution from \(\mu_{t_0}\) to \(\mu_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For compactly supported dynamical optimal transport under the smooth shortening assumptions, evaluation at an interior time determines every other point of the trajectory in a Lipschitz way. Thus every pair of times with one interior time is connected by a unique optimal deterministic transport map.
assumptions_latex: c\text{ satisfies the smooth Lagrangian hypotheses of the compact-set shortening estimate}
\Pi\text{ is a dynamical optimal transport supported on geodesics contained in }K
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{t\in[0,1]}d(\gamma(t),\widetilde\gamma(t))\le C_K(t_0)d(\gamma(t_0),\widetilde\gamma(t_0)),\quad T_{t_0\to t}\text{ is a.e. well-defined, Lipschitz, and the unique Monge solution}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distortion coefficient on a weighted Riemannian manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes unique and multiple minimizing geodesics and the endpoint definitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be an \(n\)-dimensional Riemannian manifold with reference measure \(\nu=e^{-V}\operatorname{vol}\), where \(V\in C(M)\), and let \(x,y\in M\). For \(0<t<1\), if \(x\) and \(y\) are joined by a unique minimizing geodesic, define
\[
\bar\beta_t(x,y)=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{\nu([x,B_r(y)]_t)}{\nu(B_{tr}(y))}=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{\nu([x,B_r(y)]_t)}{t^n\nu(B_r(y))}.
\]
If several minimizing geodesics join \(x\) to \(y\), define
\[
\bar\beta_t(x,y)=\inf_{\gamma}\limsup_{s\to1^-}\bar\beta_t(x,\gamma_s),
\]
where the infimum is over all minimizing \(\gamma\) with \(\gamma_0=x\) and \(\gamma_1=y\). Set \(\bar\beta_1(x,y)=1\) and \(\bar\beta_0(x,y)=\liminf_{t\to0^+}\bar\beta_t(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a weighted Riemannian manifold, the distortion coefficient is the infinitesimal ratio between the measure of a geodesically contracted ball and that of the corresponding radius-scaled ball. With multiple minimizing geodesics it is the infimum of the limiting coefficients along those geodesics; its endpoint values are defined by one and a lower limit at zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar\beta_t(x,y)\text{ is defined by the stated volume-ratio, geodesic-infimum, and endpoint formulas.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Distortion domination is equivalent to Jacobian determinant concavity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the equivalence for all dimensions N at least n, including the logarithmic N=infinity case and reduction to N=n.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be an \(n\)-dimensional Riemannian manifold, \(x,y\in M\), and let \(\{\beta_t(x,y)\}_{t\in[0,1]}\) and \(\{\beta_t(y,x)\}_{t\in[0,1]}\) be nonnegative. The following are equivalent: (a) for every \(t\in[0,1]\), \(\beta_t(x,y)\le\bar\beta_t(x,y)\) and \(\beta_t(y,x)\le\bar\beta_t(y,x)\); (b) for every \(N\ge n\), every geodesic \(\gamma\) from \(x\) to \(y\), every \(t_0\in[0,1]\), and every local vector field \(\xi\) near \(x_0=\gamma(t_0)\) with \(\nabla\xi(x_0)\) symmetric, if \(\mathcal J(s)\), the Jacobian determinant at \(x_0\) of \(\exp((s-t_0)\xi)\), is nonzero for \(0<s<1\), then for all \(t\in[0,1]\),
\[
\mathcal J(t)^{1/N}\ge(1-t)\beta_{1-t}(y,x)^{1/N}\mathcal J(0)^{1/N}+t\beta_t(x,y)^{1/N}\mathcal J(1)^{1/N}
\]
when \(N<\infty\), while for \(N=\infty\),
\[
\log\mathcal J(t)\ge(1-t)\log\mathcal J(0)+t\log\mathcal J(1)+(1-t)\log\beta_{1-t}(y,x)+t\log\beta_t(x,y);
\]
(c) property (b) holds for \(N=n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pair of nonnegative coefficient families is bounded above by the Riemannian distortion coefficients in both directions exactly when every nonvanishing geodesic Jacobian satisfies the corresponding dimension-N concavity inequality. It suffices to verify the inequality in dimension n.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (a)\Longleftrightarrow(b)\Longleftrightarrow(c).

\tfrac12\delta_{(-1/2,1/2)}+\tfrac12\delta_{(1/2,-1/2)}.
\]
These midpoint measures differ; hence the associated plan-induced constant-speed \(W_2\)-geodesics are distinct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric pair of two-atom measures has two optimal matchings whose midpoint measures differ, demonstrating nonuniqueness of quadratic-Wasserstein geodesics.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mollified approximation of continuity-equation curves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial regularization of time-continuous probability-measure solutions having finite p-integrable velocity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let p\geq 1 and let (\mu_t)_{t\in[0,T]} be a time-continuous solution of \partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\!\cdot(v_t\mu_t)=0 such that \int_0^T\!\int_{\mathbb R^d}|v_t(x)|^p\,d\mu_t(x)\,dt<\infty. For strictly positive smooth spatial mollifiers \rho_\varepsilon, define \mu_t^\varepsilon=\mu_t*\rho_\varepsilon, E_t^\varepsilon=(v_t\mu_t)*\rho_\varepsilon, and v_t^\varepsilon=E_t^\varepsilon/\mu_t^\varepsilon. Then \mu_t^\varepsilon is a continuous solution of the continuity equation with velocity v_t^\varepsilon, the fields v_t^\varepsilon satisfy the local regularity assumptions (8.1.8), and \int_{\mathbb R^d}|v_t^\varepsilon|^p\,d\mu_t^\varepsilon\leq\int_{\mathbb R^d}|v_t|^p\,d\mu_t for every t\in(0,T). Moreover, as \varepsilon\downarrow0, E_t^\varepsilon\rightharpoonup v_t\mu_t narrowly and \|v_t^\varepsilon\|_{L^p(\mu_t^\varepsilon;\mathbb R^d)}\to\|v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t;\mathbb R^d)} for every t\in(0,T).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convolving a continuity-equation solution and its momentum produces a regular solution without increasing its pointwise p-energy. As the smoothing vanishes, the momentum converges narrowly and the velocity norms converge to their original values.
assumptions_latex: \rho_\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^d)\text{ is a strictly positive spatial mollifier}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mu_t^\varepsilon,v_t^\varepsilon)\text{ solves the continuity equation},\quad \int|v_t^\varepsilon|^p\,d\mu_t^\varepsilon\leq\int|v_t|^p\,d\mu_t,\quad E_t^\varepsilon\rightharpoonup v_t\mu_t,\quad \|v_t^\varepsilon\|_{L^p(\mu_t^\varepsilon)}\to\|v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity-equation representation of Wasserstein Lipschitz curves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes Lipschitz curves in $\mathcal P_2(M)$ by tangent velocity fields satisfying the continuity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M$ be a smooth complete Riemannian manifold and let $(\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\subset\mathcal P_2(M)$ satisfy $W_2(\mu_s,\mu_t)\le L|t-s|$. Define $H_t:=\overline{\operatorname{Vect}\{\nabla\psi:\psi\in C_c^1(M)\}}^{L^2(\mu_t;TM)}$. Then there exists a measurable field $\xi_t(x)\in L^\infty(dt;L^2(\mu_t;TM))$, unique $\mu_t(dx)dt$-almost everywhere, such that $\xi_t\in H_t$ and $\partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\!\cdot(\xi_t\mu_t)=0$ weakly. Conversely, if a path satisfies this continuity equation for a measurable field with $\|\xi_t\|_{L^2(\mu_t)}\le L$ for almost every $t$, then the path is $W_2$-Lipschitz with $\|\dot\mu\|\le L$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Wasserstein-2 Lipschitz path has an essentially bounded, almost-everywhere unique tangent velocity field satisfying the weak continuity equation. Conversely, a continuity-equation solution whose velocity has uniformly bounded L2 norm is a Wasserstein Lipschitz path with the same speed bound.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a smooth complete Riemannian manifold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\,\xi\ \mu_t(dx)dt\text{-a.e.}:\ \xi_t\in H_t,\ \partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(\xi_t\mu_t)=0;\quad \|\xi_t\|_{L^2(\mu_t)}\le L\text{ a.e.}\Rightarrow \operatorname{Lip}_{W_2}(\mu)\le L.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preserves the proposition's characterization using conditions (8.3.6) and (8.3.7), whose definitions are not included in this extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu_t:I\to\mathcal P_p(X)\) be absolutely continuous and let \(v_t\in L^p(\mu_t;X)\) satisfy condition \((8.3.7)\). Then \(v_t\) also satisfies condition \((8.3.6)\) if and only if

Conditions \((8.3.6)\) and \((8.3.7)\) determine \(v_t\) uniquely for \(\mathcal L^1\)-almost every \(t\in I\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chain Rule Along Absolutely Continuous Wasserstein Curves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise approximate chain rule, with absolute continuity and an almost-everywhere applicability conclusion under additional convexity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:\mathcal P_p(X)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be regular and satisfy (10.3.1a,b), and let \(t\mapsto\mu_t\in D(\phi)\) be absolutely continuous on \((a,b)\) with tangent velocity \(\mathbf v_t\). Let \(\Lambda\) consist of the times \(t\) for which \(|\partial\phi|(\mu_t)<\infty\), \(\phi\circ\mu\) is approximately differentiable, and condition (8.4.6) holds. Then, for every \(t\in\Lambda\) and every \(\boldsymbol\gamma_t\in\partial\phi(\mu_t)\), \[\frac{\widetilde d}{dt}\phi(\mu_t)=\int\langle x_2,\mathbf v_t(x_1)\rangle\,d\boldsymbol\gamma_t(x_1,x_2).\] If, moreover, \(\phi\) is \(\lambda\)-convex and (10.1.17) holds, then \(t\mapsto\phi(\mu_t)\) is absolutely continuous and \((a,b)\setminus\Lambda\) is \(\mathcal L^1\)-negligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each time having finite slope, approximate energy differentiability, and the stated compatibility condition, the approximate energy derivative equals the pairing of the tangent velocity with any subdifferential plan. Under lambda-convexity and condition (10.1.17), the energy is absolutely continuous and the exceptional set is negligible.
assumptions_latex: \mu:(a,b)\to D(\phi)\text{ is absolutely continuous with tangent velocity }\mathbf v_t
t\in\Lambda:\ |\partial\phi|(\mu_t)<\infty,\ \phi\circ\mu\text{ is approximately differentiable at }t,\ \text{and (8.4.6) holds}
\text{For the final conclusion, }\phi\text{ is }\lambda\text{-convex and (10.1.17) holds}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\widetilde d}{dt}\phi(\mu_t)=\int\langle x_2,\mathbf v_t(x_1)\rangle\,d\boldsymbol\gamma_t\quad\forall\boldsymbol\gamma_t\in\partial\phi(\mu_t),\ \forall t\in\Lambda;\quad \phi\text{ being }\lambda\text{-convex together with (10.1.17) implies }\phi\circ\mu\in AC(a,b)\text{ and }\mathcal L^1((a,b)\setminus\Lambda)=0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The statement is subject to the source chapter's standing assumptions on the ambient space X and exponent p, which are not included in this extract.

Let \(\mu\in\mathcal P_p(X)\), \(v\in L^p(\mu;X)\), and \(\mu_\varepsilon=(\mathbf i+\varepsilon v)_\#\mu\) for \(\varepsilon>0\). If \(v\in\operatorname{Tan}_\mu\mathcal P_p(X)\), then

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variational Selection of Wasserstein Tangent Vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes tangent vectors by norm minimality modulo measure-divergence-free fields and establishes the canonical tangent representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu\in\mathcal P_p(X)\). A vector \(v\in L^p(\mu;X)\) belongs to \(\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu}\mathcal P_p(X)\) if and only if
\[
\|v+w\|_{L^p(\mu;X)}\geq\|v\|_{L^p(\mu;X)}
\quad\text{for every }w\in L^p(\mu;X)\text{ satisfying }\nabla\!\cdot(w\mu)=0.
\]
For every \(u\in L^p(\mu;X)\), its equivalence class modulo such divergence-free fields contains a unique \(\Pi(u)\in\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu}\mathcal P_p(X)\), which minimizes the \(L^p\)-norm in that class. Moreover,
\[
\int_X\langle j_p(v),u-\Pi(u)\rangle\,d\mu=0
\]
for every \(v\in\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu}\mathcal P_p(X)\) and \(u\in L^p(\mu;X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A field is Wasserstein-tangent exactly when adding any μ-divergence-free field cannot reduce its Lp norm. Every equivalence class modulo such fields has a unique minimal-norm tangent representative, with the stated dual orthogonality property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\in\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu}\mathcal P_p(X)\iff \|v+w\|_{L^p(\mu;X)}\geq\|v\|_{L^p(\mu;X)}\ \forall w\text{ with }\nabla\cdot(w\mu)=0;\quad \Pi(u)\text{ exists uniquely, is norm-minimal, and satisfies the stated dual orthogonality identity}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Analytic properties of the Benamou–Brenier functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity, weak lower semicontinuity, dual and density representations, the necessary finiteness conditions, the velocity representation, and mollification monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The functional \(\mathcal B_p\) is convex and lower semicontinuous on \(\mathcal M(X)\times\mathcal M^d(X)\) for weak convergence. Moreover,
\[
\mathcal B_p(\rho,E)\ge0
\]
and
\[
\mathcal B_p(\rho,E)=\sup_{(a,b)\in L^\infty(X;K_q)}\left(\int_X a\,d\rho+\int_X b\cdot dE\right).
\]
If \(\rho,E\ll\lambda\) for a common positive measure \(\lambda\), then
\[
\mathcal B_p(\rho,E)=\int_X f_p\!\left(\frac{d\rho}{d\lambda},\frac{dE}{d\lambda}\right)d\lambda.
\]
If \(\mathcal B_p(\rho,E)<+\infty\), then \(\rho\ge0\) and \(E\ll\rho\). Whenever \(\rho\ge0\) and \(E\ll\rho\), writing \(E=v\rho\) gives
\[
\mathcal B_p(\rho,E)=\int_X\frac{|v|^p}{p}\,d\rho.
\]
Finally, if \(X=\mathbb R^d\), \(\eta_\varepsilon\) is a standard even mollifier, \(\rho^\varepsilon=\rho*\eta_\varepsilon\), and \(E^\varepsilon=E*\eta_\varepsilon\), then
\[
\mathcal B_p(\rho^\varepsilon,E^\varepsilon)\le\mathcal B_p(\rho,E).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Benamou–Brenier functional is nonnegative, convex, and weakly lower semicontinuous, and its dual supremum can be taken over bounded measurable fields valued in K_q. Under domination by a common positive measure it is the integral of the action density. Finite value requires rho to be nonnegative and E to be absolutely continuous with respect to rho. When E=v rho, the functional equals the integral of |v|^p/p against rho. Simultaneous convolution with a standard even mollifier cannot increase it.
assumptions_latex: For the density representation, \(\rho,E\ll\lambda\) for a common positive measure \(\lambda\)
For the velocity representation, \(\rho\ge0\) and \(E\ll\rho\), with \(E=v\rho\)
For mollification, \(X=\mathbb R^d\) and \(\eta_\varepsilon\) is a standard even mollifier
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B_p\) has the stated convexity, weak lower-semicontinuity, nonnegativity, dual and density representations, necessary finiteness conditions, velocity representation, and mollification inequality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Time rescaling of distributional continuity equations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence under an increasing bi-absolutely-continuous change of time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathfrak t:[0,T']\to[0,T] be strictly increasing and absolutely continuous, with absolutely continuous inverse. Define \widehat\mu_s:=\mu_{\mathfrak t(s)} and \widehat v_s:=\mathfrak t'(s)v_{\mathfrak t(s)}. Then (\mu_t,v_t) is a distributional solution of \partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\!\cdot(v_t\mu_t)=0 on (0,T) if and only if (\widehat\mu_s,\widehat v_s) is a distributional solution of the corresponding continuity equation on (0,T').
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly increasing time change whose map and inverse are absolutely continuous preserves and reflects distributional solutions when the velocity is multiplied by the derivative of the time change.
assumptions_latex: \mathfrak t:[0,T']\to[0,T]\text{ is strictly increasing and absolutely continuous}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mu,v)\text{ solves the continuity equation on }(0,T)\iff(\widehat\mu,\widehat v)\text{ solves it on }(0,T')

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal Displacement Maps Are Wasserstein Tangent Vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Places uniquely defined optimal-map displacements in the Wasserstein tangent space for regular source measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\in(1,+\infty)\) and \(\mu\in\mathcal P_p^{r}(X)\). Then
\[
\operatorname{Tan}^{r}_{\mu}\mathcal P_p(X)\subseteq\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu}\mathcal P_p(X).
\]
Equivalently, for every \(\sigma\in\mathcal P_p(X)\), if \(\mathbf t_{\mu}^{\sigma}\) is the unique optimal transport map from \(\mu\) to \(\sigma\), then
\[
\mathbf t_{\mu}^{\sigma}-\mathbf i\in\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu}\mathcal P_p(X).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If p is strictly between 1 and infinity and μ is a regular p-Wasserstein measure, every unique optimal transport displacement from μ is tangent at μ; hence the optimal-map-generated tangent cone is contained in the Wasserstein tangent space.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf t_{\mu}^{\sigma}\text{ is the unique optimal transport map from }\mu\text{ to }\sigma

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support-function representation of the Benamou–Brenier action density
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the complete boundary behavior in the scalar density variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p,q\in(1,\infty)\) satisfy \(1/p+1/q=1\), and set
\[
K_q:=\left\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d:a+\frac{|b|^q}{q}\le0\right\}.
\]
Then, for every \((t,x)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d\),
\[
\sup_{(a,b)\in K_q}(at+b\cdot x)=f_p(t,x):=\begin{cases}
\dfrac{|x|^p}{p\,t^{p-1}},&t>0,\\
0,&t=0,\ x=0,\\
+\infty,&t<0\text{ or }(t=0,\ x\ne0).
\end{cases}
\]
In particular, \(f_p\) is convex and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For conjugate exponents p and q, the support function of the set defined by a+|b|^q/q≤0 is the perspective action density |x|^p/(p t^(p−1)) for positive t, zero at (0,0), and infinite for negative t or for t=0 with x nonzero. The resulting function is convex and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{(a,b)\in K_q}(at+b\cdot x)=f_p(t,x)\) with the stated piecewise values; moreover, \(f_p\) is convex and lower semicontinuous.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let I=(0,T), let (\mu_t)_{t\in I}\subset\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d) be a Borel family, and let v:\mathbb R^d\times I\to\mathbb R^d be Borel with \int_0^T\int_{\mathbb R^d}|v_t(x)|\,d\mu_t(x)\,dt<\infty. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm Characterization of Measure-Divergence-Free Fields
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes μ-divergence-free fields by their norm separation from every Wasserstein tangent vector, retaining the equality boundary under the equivalent conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu\in\mathcal P_p(X)\) and \(w\in L^p(\mu;X)\). Then
\[
\nabla\!\cdot(w\mu)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\|v-w\|_{L^p(\mu;X)}\geq\|v\|_{L^p(\mu;X)}
\quad\text{for every }v\in\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu}\mathcal P_p(X).
\]
Under these equivalent conditions, equality holds for some \(v\in\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu}\mathcal P_p(X)\) if and only if \(w=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A field is μ-divergence-free exactly when subtracting it cannot reduce the norm of any Wasserstein tangent vector. Subject to this equivalent condition, equality for some tangent vector occurs exactly when the field is zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla\cdot(w\mu)=0\iff \|v-w\|_{L^p(\mu;X)}\geq\|v\|_{L^p(\mu;X)}\ \forall v\in\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu}\mathcal P_p(X);\quad \text{under these conditions, }(\exists v\text{ with equality})\iff w=0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Everywhere Differentiability of Wasserstein Distance Along Curves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiates the pth power of the distance from an absolutely continuous Wasserstein curve to a fixed measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[
\frac{d}{dt}W_p^p(\mu_t,\sigma)

\]
for every \(\gamma\in\Gamma_o(\mu_t,\sigma)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Benamou–Brenier functional on measure-flux pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual definition using bounded continuous fields valued in the conjugate constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\rho\in\mathcal M(X)\), \(E\in\mathcal M^d(X)\), and \(K_q:=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d:a+|b|^q/q\le0\}\), define
\[
\mathcal B_p(\rho,E):=\sup\left\{\int_X a\,d\rho+\int_X b\cdot dE:(a,b)\in C_b(X;K_q)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a scalar measure rho and a vector measure E on X, the Benamou–Brenier functional is the supremum of the pairing of (rho,E) with bounded continuous fields (a,b) whose values satisfy a+|b|^q/q≤0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Optimal-Transport Representation Along Wasserstein Curves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives optimal-plan, pushforward, and regular-source optimal-map representations of the tangent velocity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu_t:I\to\mathcal P_p(X)\) be absolutely continuous and let \(v_t\in\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu_t}\mathcal P_p(X)\) be the tangent vector characterized by Proposition 8.4.5. For \(\mathcal L^1\)-a.e. \(t\in I\), every selection \(\boldsymbol\mu_h\in\Gamma_o(\mu_t,\mu_{t+h})\) satisfies, as \(h\to0\),
\[
\left(\pi^1,\frac{\pi^2-\pi^1}{h}\right)_{\#}\boldsymbol\mu_h
\longrightarrow(\mathbf i\times v_t)_{\#}\mu_t
\quad\text{in }\mathcal P_p(X\times X),
\]
and
\[
\frac{W_p\!\left(\mu_{t+h},(\mathbf i+h v_t)_{\#}\mu_t\right)}{|h|}\longrightarrow0.
\]
In particular, for almost every such \(t\) with \(\mu_t\in\mathcal P_p^r(X)\), the unique optimal transport map satisfies
\[
\frac{\mathbf t_{\mu_t}^{\mu_{t+h}}-\mathbf i}{h}\longrightarrow v_t
\quad\text{in }L^p(\mu_t;X).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At almost every time, every selection of nearby optimal plans recovers the tangent velocity after rescaling, and identity plus h times the velocity gives a first-order pushforward approximation. When the source measure is in the stated regular class, the rescaled unique optimal maps converge to the velocity in Lp.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and estimates for characteristic flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Carathéodory-type characteristics for spatially locally Lipschitz Borel velocity fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let v be Borel and suppose that for every compact B\subset\mathbb R^d, \int_0^T(\sup_{x\in B}|v_t(x)|+\operatorname{Lip}(v_t;B))\,dt<\infty. For every x\in\mathbb R^d and s\in[0,T], the problem X_s(x,s)=x,\ \dot X_t(x,s)=v_t(X_t(x,s)) has a unique maximal solution on a relatively open interval I(x,s)\subset[0,T] containing s as a relative interior point. If |X_t(x,s)| remains bounded in the interior of I(x,s), then I(x,s)=[0,T]. If S:=\int_0^T(\sup_{\mathbb R^d}|v_t|+\operatorname{Lip}(v_t;\mathbb R^d))\,dt<\infty, then \int_0^T\sup_x|\partial_tX_t(x,s)|\,dt\le S and \sup_{t,s\in[0,T]}\operatorname{Lip}(X_t(\cdot,s);\mathbb R^d)\le e^S.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local integrability of the velocity's size and spatial Lipschitz modulus gives unique maximal characteristics; bounded characteristics continue for the full time interval, and global bounds yield uniform speed-integral and Lipschitz estimates for the flow.
assumptions_latex: S:=\int_0^T(\sup_{\mathbb R^d}|v_t|+\operatorname{Lip}(v_t;\mathbb R^d))\,dt<\infty\text{ for the global estimates}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!\text{ maximal characteristic }X_\cdot(x,s);\quad \sup_{\operatorname{int}I}|X_t|<\infty\Rightarrow I=[0,T];\quad \int_0^T\sup_x|\partial_tX_t(x,s)|dt\le S,\ \sup_{t,s}\operatorname{Lip}(X_t(\cdot,s))\le e^S

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular Approximation of Divergence-Free Measure–Velocity Pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximates a divergence-free measure–velocity pair by regular finite-dimensional pairs without losing divergence or Lp energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu\in\mathcal P_p(X)\), \(v\in L^p(\mu;X)\), and suppose \(\nabla\cdot(v\mu)=0\) in duality with smooth cylindrical functions. For every complete orthonormal system \((e_n)_{n\ge1}\), there exist \(\mu_h\in\mathcal P_p(X)\) and \(v_h\in L^p(\mu_h;X)\) such that, with \(X_h=\operatorname{span}(e_1,\ldots,e_h)\) and \(X_h=X\) in finite dimension, \(\operatorname{supp}\mu_h\subset X_h\), \(\mu_h|_{X_h}\in\mathcal P_p^r(X_h)\), \(v_h(x)\in X_h\), and \(\nabla\cdot(v_h\mu_h)=0\). Furthermore, \(\mu_h\to\mu\) in \(\mathcal P_p(X)\), and for every continuous \(f:X\times X\to\mathbb R\) with \(p\)-growth, \(\int f(x,v_h(x))\,d\mu_h(x)\to\int f(x,v(x))\,d\mu(x)\). Consequently, \(v_h\mu_h\to v\mu\) against \(C_b^0(X;X)\) and \(\|v_h\|_{L^p(\mu_h;X)}\to\|v\|_{L^p(\mu;X)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every divergence-free Lp measure–velocity pair can be approximated by regular pairs supported on increasing finite-dimensional subspaces. The approximants remain divergence-free and converge in Wasserstein measure, vector-measure duality, all continuous p-growth integrals, and Lp velocity norm.
assumptions_latex: \nabla\cdot(v\mu)=0\text{ in duality with smooth cylindrical functions}
(e_n)_{n\ge1}\text{ is a complete orthonormal system of }X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(\mu_h,v_h):\ \operatorname{supp}\mu_h\subset X_h,\ \mu_h|_{X_h}\in\mathcal P_p^r(X_h),\ v_h(x)\in X_h,\ \nabla\cdot(v_h\mu_h)=0,\ \mu_h\to\mu,\ v_h\mu_h\to v\mu,\ \|v_h\|_{L^p(\mu_h)}\to\|v\|_{L^p(\mu)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Absolutely Continuous Wasserstein Curves and the Continuity Equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes absolute continuity in Wasserstein space through distributional continuity equations and admissible velocity fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subset\mathbb R\) be an open interval. If \(\mu:I\to\mathcal P_p(X)\) is absolutely continuous with metric derivative \(|\mu'|\in L^1(I)\), then there exists a Borel vector field \(v_t\in L^p(\mu_t;X)\) such that \(\|v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t;X)}\le |\mu'|(t)\) for \(\mathcal L^1\)-a.e. \(t\), and \(\partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(v_t\mu_t)=0\) distributionally, meaning \(\int_I\int_X(\partial_t\varphi+\langle v_t,\nabla_x\varphi\rangle)\,d\mu_t\,dt=0\) for every \(\varphi\in\operatorname{Cyl}(X\times I)\). Moreover, \(j_p(v_t)\) belongs for a.e. \(t\) to the \(L^q(\mu_t;X)\)-closure of the subspace generated by cylindrical gradients. Conversely, if \(\mu:I\to\mathcal P_p(X)\) is narrowly continuous and satisfies the continuity equation for a Borel field \(v_t\) with \(t\mapsto\|v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t;X)}\in L^1(I)\), then \(\mu\) is absolutely continuous and \(|\mu'|(t)\le\|v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t;X)}\) for a.e. \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An absolutely continuous Wasserstein curve has a distributional velocity field whose Lp norm is no greater than its metric speed, with the corresponding dual field approximable by cylindrical gradients. Conversely, a narrowly continuous curve with an integrable Lp velocity satisfying the continuity equation is absolutely continuous, and its metric speed is bounded by the velocity norm.
assumptions_latex: I\subset\mathbb R\text{ is an open interval}
\mu:I\to\mathcal P_p(X)\text{ is absolutely continuous with }|\mu'|\in L^1(I)
\text{In the converse branch, }\mu\text{ is narrowly continuous}
\text{In the converse branch, }v\text{ is Borel, }\partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(v_t\mu_t)=0,\text{ and }t\mapsto\|v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t;X)}\in L^1(I)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists v:\ \|v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t;X)}\le |\mu'|(t),\quad \partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(v_t\mu_t)=0;\qquad \text{conversely, }|\mu'|(t)\le\|v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t;X)}\ \text{a.e.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Dimensional Projection of Measure–Velocity Pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projects a measure and an Lp vector field onto increasing finite-dimensional subspaces while preserving divergence-free structure and recovering the original pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu\in\mathcal P_p(X)\), \(v\in L^p(\mu;X)\), and let \((e_n)_{n\ge1}\) be a complete orthonormal system. For \(X^d=\operatorname{span}(e_1,\ldots,e_d)\), set \(\widehat\mu^d=\widehat\pi^d_{\#}\mu\) and define \(\widehat v^d(x)=\int_{(\widehat\pi^d)^{-1}(x)}\widehat\pi^d(v(y))\,d\mu_x(y)\) using the disintegration of \(\mu\). Then \(\operatorname{supp}\widehat\mu^d\subset X^d\), \(\widehat\mu^d\to\mu\) in \(\mathcal P_p(X)\), and regularity of \(\mu\) implies regularity of \(\widehat\mu^d|_{X^d}\). Moreover, \(\widehat v^d\in L^p(\widehat\mu^d;X^d)\) and \(\|\widehat v^d\|_{L^p(\widehat\mu^d)}\le\|v\|_{L^p(\mu)}\); for every bounded Borel field \(\zeta\), \(\int\langle\zeta,\widehat v^d\rangle\,d\widehat\mu^d=\int\langle\widehat\pi^d\zeta(\widehat\pi^d x),v(x)\rangle\,d\mu(x)\). If \(\nabla\cdot(v\mu)=0\) against smooth cylindrical functions, then \(\nabla\cdot(\widehat v^d\widehat\mu^d)=0\). Finally, for every continuous \(f:X\times X\to\mathbb R\) with \(p\)-growth, \(\int f(x,\widehat v^d(x))\,d\widehat\mu^d(x)\to\int f(x,v(x))\,d\mu(x)\); hence \(\widehat v^d\widehat\mu^d\to v\mu\) against \(C_b^0(X;X)\) and \(\|\widehat v^d\|_{L^p(\widehat\mu^d)}\to\|v\|_{L^p(\mu)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional averaging after finite-dimensional projection produces measure–velocity pairs supported on increasing finite-dimensional subspaces. Their Lp norms do not increase, divergence-free structure is preserved, and the measures, vector measures, p-growth integrals, and velocity norms converge to those of the original pair.
assumptions_latex: (e_n)_{n\ge1}\text{ is a complete orthonormal system of }X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\mu^d\to\mu\text{ in }\mathcal P_p(X),\quad \|\widehat v^d\|_{L^p(\widehat\mu^d)}\le\|v\|_{L^p(\mu)},\quad \nabla\cdot(v\mu)=0\Rightarrow\nabla\cdot(\widehat v^d\widehat\mu^d)=0,\quad \widehat v^d\widehat\mu^d\to v\mu,\quad \|\widehat v^d\|_{L^p(\widehat\mu^d)}\to\|v\|_{L^p(\mu)}.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Derivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General metric definition and almost-everywhere characterization for absolutely continuous curves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At any \(t\in(a,b)\) for which the limit exists, the metric derivative of \(\mu\) is
\[
|\dot\mu_t|=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{d(\mu_{t+h},\mu_t)}{|h|}.
\]
For every absolutely continuous metric-space curve, this limit exists for almost every \(t\). Moreover, \(|\dot\mu|\in L^1(a,b)\), and it is minimal almost everywhere among all \(g\in L^1(a,b)\) satisfying
\[
d(\mu_s,\mu_t)\leq\int_s^t g(r)\,dr
\quad\text{for every }a<s<t<b.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The metric derivative is the almost-everywhere limit of distance traveled divided by elapsed time and is the least integrable upper speed of an absolutely continuous curve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\dot\mu_t|\) exists for almost every \(t\) and is minimal almost everywhere among integrable upper speeds.

\]
Thus every admissible velocity field supplies an upper bound on the metric speed.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Speed Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical minimal tangent-velocity theorem for absolutely continuous curves in Euclidean quadratic-Wasserstein space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists a Borel velocity field \(v^{\min}\) satisfying
\[
\partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(v_t^{\min}\mu_t)=0
\]
distributionally, with \(v_t^{\min}\in\operatorname{Tan}_{\mu_t}\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)\) for almost every \(t\), such that
\[
\|v_t^{\min}\|_{L^2(\mu_t)}=|\dot\mu_t|
\quad\text{for almost every }t.
\]
For every other admissible Borel velocity field \(v\) solving the same continuity equation,
\[
|\dot\mu_t|\leq\|v_t\|_{L^2(\mu_t)}
\quad\text{for almost every }t.
\]
The tangent velocity \(v_t^{\min}\) is unique in \(L^2(\mu_t;\mathbb R^d)\) for almost every \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An absolutely continuous quadratic-Wasserstein curve has an almost-everywhere unique tangent velocity whose quadratic norm equals the metric derivative, while every other admissible velocity has at least that norm.
assumptions_latex: \((\mu_t)_{t\in(a,b)}\) is absolutely continuous in \((\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d),W_2)\).
Admissible velocities are Borel spacetime fields with integrable \(L^2(\mu_t)\)-norm that solve the continuity equation distributionally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is an almost-everywhere unique tangent velocity \(v_t^{\min}\) with \(\|v_t^{\min}\|_{L^2(\mu_t)}=|\dot\mu_t|\), and every admissible velocity has no smaller norm almost everywhere.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity-Equation Characterization of Absolutely Continuous Wasserstein Curves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-way correspondence between absolutely continuous Wasserstein curves and time-integrable Eulerian velocity fields, with both metric-speed inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $p>1$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact. If $(\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ is absolutely continuous in $\mathbb W_p(\Omega)$, then for almost every $t$ there exists $\mathbf v_t\in L^p(\mu_t;\mathbb R^d)$ such that
\[
\partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(\mathbf v_t\mu_t)=0
\]
in the weak sense and
\[
\|\mathbf v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t)}\le |\mu'|(t)
\quad\text{for a.e. }t.
\]
Conversely, suppose $\mu_t\in\mathcal P_p(\Omega)$ and $\mathbf v_t\in L^p(\mu_t;\mathbb R^d)$ solve the weak continuity equation and satisfy
\[
\int_0^1\|\mathbf v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t)}\,dt<\infty.
\]
Then $(\mu_t)_t$ is absolutely continuous in $\mathbb W_p(\Omega)$ and
\[
|\mu'|(t)\le\|\mathbf v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t)}
\quad\text{for a.e. }t.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For p greater than one on a compact Euclidean domain, an absolutely continuous Wasserstein curve admits a weak continuity-equation velocity field whose Lp norm does not exceed its metric speed. Conversely, a weak continuity-equation solution with time-integrable Lp velocity norm is an absolutely continuous Wasserstein curve, with metric speed bounded by that norm almost everywhere.
assumptions_latex: Forward direction: $(\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ is absolutely continuous in $\mathbb W_p(\Omega)$.
Converse direction: $\mu_t\in\mathcal P_p(\Omega)$, $\mathbf v_t\in L^p(\mu_t;\mathbb R^d)$, the continuity equation holds weakly, and $\int_0^1\|\mathbf v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t)}dt<\infty$.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&(\mu_t)_t\in\operatorname{AC}(\mathbb W_p(\Omega))\Rightarrow\exists(\mathbf v_t)_t:\ \partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(\mathbf v_t\mu_t)=0,\ \|\mathbf v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t)}\le|\mu'|(t)\ \text{a.e.};\\&\left[\partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(\mathbf v_t\mu_t)=0,\ \int_0^1\|\mathbf v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t)}dt<\infty\right]\Rightarrow(\mu_t)_t\in\operatorname{AC}(\mathbb W_p(\Omega)),\ |\mu'|(t)\le\|\mathbf v_t\|_{L^p(\mu_t)}\ \text{a.e.}\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: At-most-one-solution result in an absolutely continuous \(\mathbb W_2\) class, with the extract's final absolute-continuity condition understood as \(\rho_t\ll\mathcal L^d\) for almost every time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be a compact smooth domain and let \(\mathbf v_t:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) satisfy, for a constant \(C\) independent of \(x,y,t\), \[(\mathbf v_t(x)-\mathbf v_t(y))\cdot(x-y)\le C|x-y|^2,\] together with \(\mathbf v_t\cdot\mathbf n=0\) on \(\partial\Omega\). For a prescribed initial datum \(\rho_0\), the equation \(\partial_t\rho_t+\nabla\cdot(\rho_t\mathbf v_t)=0\) has at most one solution among curves in \(AC(\mathbb W_2(\Omega))\) satisfying \(\rho_t\ll\mathcal L^d\) for almost every \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact smooth domain, a uniformly one-sided Lipschitz velocity field tangent to the boundary yields at most one continuity-equation solution with the prescribed initial datum among absolutely continuous Wasserstein-2 curves whose measures have densities for almost every time.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fiberwise Characterization of Optimal Tangent-Plan Couplings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disintegration criterion and integral representation for the tangent-plan distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13}\in\mathcal P_2(X^2)\) have common first marginal \(\mu\), and let \(\gamma\in\Gamma^1(\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13})\). Then \(\gamma\) minimizes the cost defining \(W_\mu(\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13})\) if and only if, in its disintegration with respect to \(\mu\),
\[\gamma_{x_1}\in\Gamma_o\!\left(\gamma_{x_1}^{12},\gamma_{x_1}^{13}\right)\quad\text{for }\mu\text{-a.e. }x_1\in X.\]
Moreover,
\[W_\mu^2(\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13})=\int_X W_2^2\!\left(\gamma_{x_1}^{12},\gamma_{x_1}^{13}\right)\,d\mu(x_1).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupling of two tangent plans is globally optimal exactly when its conditional coupling is Wasserstein-optimal in almost every fiber over the common base point. The squared tangent-plan distance is the integral of the squared fiberwise Wasserstein distances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma\text{ minimizes the }W_\mu\text{ cost}\iff \gamma_{x_1}\in\Gamma_o(\gamma_{x_1}^{12},\gamma_{x_1}^{13})\text{ for }\mu\text{-a.e. }x_1,\quad W_\mu^2=\int_XW_2^2(\gamma_{x_1}^{12},\gamma_{x_1}^{13})\,d\mu.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm, Inner Product, and Distance for Tangent Plans
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fiber-coupling geometry for two plans with a common base marginal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13}\in\mathcal P_2(X^2)\) satisfy \(\pi^1_\#\gamma^{12}=\pi^1_\#\gamma^{13}=\mu\). Define
\[\|\gamma^{12}\|_\mu^2:=\int_{X^2}|x_2|^2\,d\gamma^{12}(x_1,x_2),\]
\[\langle\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13}\rangle_\mu:=\max_{\gamma\in\Gamma^1(\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13})}\int_{X^3}\langle x_2,x_3\rangle\,d\gamma,\]
and
\[W_\mu^2(\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13}):=\min_{\gamma\in\Gamma^1(\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13})}\int_{X^3}|x_2-x_3|^2\,d\gamma,\]
where \(\Gamma^1(\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13})\) consists of \(\gamma\in\mathcal P(X^3)\) with \(\pi^{1,2}_\#\gamma=\gamma^{12}\) and \(\pi^{1,3}_\#\gamma=\gamma^{13}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two square-integrable plans sharing their first marginal, the tangent-plan norm is the second moment of displacement. Their inner product maximizes the paired displacement inner product, and their squared distance minimizes the paired squared displacement difference, over all three-plans having the prescribed two marginals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\gamma^{12}\|_\mu^2=\int|x_2|^2d\gamma^{12},\quad \langle\gamma^{12},\gamma^{13}\rangle_\mu=\max_{\Gamma^1}\int\langle x_2,x_3\rangle d\gamma,\quad W_\mu^2=\min_{\Gamma^1}\int|x_2-x_3|^2d\gamma.

\[
\mathbf u_s=e^{\mathbf f_s/\varepsilon},\qquad \mathbf v_s=e^{\mathbf g_s/\varepsilon},
\]
where \((\mathbf f_s,\mathbf g_s)_{s=1}^S\) solves
\[
\max_{(\mathbf f_s,\mathbf g_s)_s}
\left\{
\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\left(
\langle\mathbf g_s,\mathbf b_s\rangle-
\varepsilon\left\langle\mathbf K_se^{\mathbf g_s/\varepsilon},e^{\mathbf f_s/\varepsilon}\right\rangle
\right):
\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\mathbf f_s=0
\right\}.
\]
This constrained program has the same value as formulation (9.14).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal scaling vectors in the referenced entropy-regularized barycenter formulation are componentwise exponentials of potential vectors. The potentials solve the displayed weighted maximization problem subject to the vector constraint that the weighted f-potentials sum to zero. Its value equals that of the referenced formulation (9.14).

\lambda_s,\mathbf b_s,\mathbf K_s\ \text{have the dimensions and meanings fixed by the referenced barycenter formulation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf u_s=e^{\mathbf f_s/\varepsilon},\quad \mathbf v_s=e^{\mathbf g_s/\varepsilon},\quad (\mathbf f_s,\mathbf g_s)_s\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\sum_s\lambda_s\mathbf f_s=0}\sum_s\lambda_s\left(\langle\mathbf g_s,\mathbf b_s\rangle-\varepsilon\langle\mathbf K_se^{\mathbf g_s/\varepsilon},e^{\mathbf f_s/\varepsilon}\rangle\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Wasserstein Barycenters and Their Coupling LP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational definition and joint-coupling formulation for barycenters of finitely many weighted histograms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(b_s\in\Delta_{n_s}\), \(\lambda\in\Delta_S\), and \(C_s\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n_s}\). A finite Wasserstein barycenter is a minimizer of
\[
\min_{a\in\Delta_n}\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s L_{C_s}(a,b_s).
\]
Equivalently, this problem is the linear program
\[
\min_{\substack{a\in\Delta_n,\;P_s\in\mathbb{R}_+^{n\times n_s}}}
\left\{\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\langle P_s,C_s\rangle:\;P_s\mathbf 1_{n_s}=a,\;P_s^\top\mathbf 1_n=b_s\ \text{for every }s\right\}.
\]
When \(n_s=n\) and \(C_s=D^p\) for every \(s\), the variational objective becomes \(\sum_s\lambda_sW_p^p(a,b_s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A barycenter of finitely many weighted histograms minimizes their weighted optimal-transport costs. Introducing a nonnegative coupling between the barycenter and each input yields an equivalent linear program in which all couplings share the barycenter marginal. On a common grid with a p-power distance cost, the objective is the weighted sum of pth-power Wasserstein distances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{a\in\Delta_n}\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_sL_{C_s}(a,b_s)=\min_{\substack{a\in\Delta_n,\;P_s\ge 0\\P_s\mathbf1_{n_s}=a,\;P_s^\top\mathbf1_n=b_s\ \forall s}}\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\langle P_s,C_s\rangle.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directional Barycenters with Inverse-Radon Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eulerian approximation obtained from independently optimized one-dimensional projected barycenters; it is not generally an exact barycenter because the projection family may be Radon-inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given probability measures \(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_S\) on \(\mathbb R^d\) and barycentric weights \(\lambda_s\), compute for each \(\theta\)
\[
\rho_\theta^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\rho_\theta\in\mathcal M_+^1(\mathbb R)}
\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\mathcal W_2\!\left(\rho_\theta,P_{\theta\sharp}\beta_s\right)^2,
\]
using one-dimensional monotone rearrangement, and define
\[
\alpha_R:=\mathcal R^+(\rho^\star).
\]
In general, \(\rho^\star\) need not lie in \(\operatorname{range}(\mathcal R)\), because the Radon transform is not surjective. Consequently, \(\alpha_R\) is only a reconstruction-based approximation and need not solve the target barycenter problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method computes a one-dimensional Wasserstein barycenter of the projected inputs in every direction and applies inverse Radon reconstruction. Independently optimized projections need not come from any common multidimensional measure, so the reconstruction is not generally an exact barycenter.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal R^+\text{ is defined on the computed projection family}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_R=\mathcal R^+(\rho^\star),\qquad \rho^\star\notin\operatorname{range}(\mathcal R)\text{ may occur, so }\alpha_R\text{ need not be an exact barycenter}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Sample Quadratic Wasserstein Barycenter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variational definition for finitely many weighted probability measures; it does not assert existence or uniqueness of a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(N\in\mathbb N\), probability measures \(\rho^1,\ldots,\rho^N\in\mathcal P(\Omega)\), and weights \(\lambda_i\ge 0\), a quadratic Wasserstein barycenter is any measure \(\bar\rho\in\mathcal P(\Omega)\) such that
\[
\bar\rho\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\rho\in\mathcal P(\Omega)}\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i W_2^2(\rho,\rho^i).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given finitely many probability measures and nonnegative weights, a quadratic Wasserstein barycenter is any probability measure minimizing the weighted sum of squared 2-Wasserstein distances to the input measures. This definition alone does not guarantee that a minimizer exists or is unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar\rho\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\rho\in\mathcal P(\Omega)}\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i W_2^2(\rho,\rho^i)

assumptions_latex: The two input measures and equal barycenter weights are those displayed in the statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A convex mixture of optimal matchings yields a barycenter with four atoms, whereas either extremal matching yields only two.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu_0=\tfrac12(\delta_{(-1,0)}+\delta_{(1,0)})\) and \(\mu_1=\tfrac12(\delta_{(0,-1)}+\delta_{(0,1)})\), let \(\pi^+\) and \(\pi^-\) be the two bijective optimal couplings. The mixture \(\pi=\tfrac12(\pi^++\pi^-)\) is also optimal. Its midpoint pushforward is \(\nu=	frac14\sum_{a,b\in\{-1,1\}}\delta_{(a/2,b/2)}\), which has four atoms. By contrast, the midpoint pushforward of either \(\pi^+\) or \(\pi^-\) has two atoms. Hence convex multiplicity of optimal couplings can smear barycentric mass across additional locations without changing the optimal objective value.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Standard compact-restriction approximation scheme
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the additional deterministic-map and absolute-continuity conclusions when the initial measure is absolutely continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M$ be a smooth complete Riemannian manifold and let $c$ be induced by a Lagrangian satisfying the classical hypotheses. Let $\Pi$ be a dynamical optimal plan with $(e_0,e_1)_\#\Pi=\pi$ and $(e_t)_\#\Pi=\mu_t$, where $\pi$ is optimal between $\mu_0$ and $\mu_1$. For compact sets $K_\ell$ of action-minimizing curves with $\Pi(\bigcup_\ell K_\ell)=1$ and $Z_\ell:=\Pi(K_\ell)>0$, define $\Pi_\ell:=Z_\ell^{-1}\mathbf1_{K_\ell}\Pi$, $\mu_{t,\ell}:=(e_t)_\#\Pi_\ell$, $\pi_\ell:=(e_0,e_1)_\#\Pi_\ell$, and restrict $c$ to $\operatorname{proj}_{M\times M}(K_\ell)$. Then $(\mu_{t,\ell})_{t\in[0,1]}$ is a displacement interpolation, $\pi_\ell$ is an associated optimal plan, and $\mu_{t,\ell}$ has support compact uniformly in $t$. Moreover, $Z_\ell\uparrow1$, $Z_\ell\pi_\ell\uparrow\pi$, $Z_\ell\mu_{t,\ell}\uparrow\mu_t$, and $Z_\ell\Pi_\ell\uparrow\Pi$. If $\mu_0\ll\mathrm{vol}$, then $\pi$ is concentrated on the graph induced by a $c$-convex potential $\psi$; every $\mu_{0,\ell}$ is absolutely continuous and $\pi_\ell$ is deterministic. There is a $c_\ell$-convex $\psi_\ell$ agreeing with $\psi$ on $C_\ell:=\operatorname{proj}_M(\operatorname{Spt}\pi_\ell)$, with $\widetilde\nabla\psi=\nabla\psi_\ell$ on $C_\ell$ outside a volume-null set. In addition, every $\mu_{t,\ell}$ is absolutely continuous, and for $t_0\in[0,1)$ and $t\in[0,1]$, the optimal map $T_{t_0\to t,\ell}$ is deterministic and equals $T_{t_0\to t}$ $\mu_{t_0,\ell}$-almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting a dynamical optimal plan to compact families of minimizing curves and renormalizing produces compactly supported displacement interpolations and optimal plans converging monotonically to the originals. With an absolutely continuous initial measure, deterministic optimal maps, compatible transport potentials, absolute continuity along the restricted interpolations, and agreement with the original intermediate transport maps are preserved.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a smooth complete Riemannian manifold}
c\text{ is induced by a Lagrangian satisfying the classical conditions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Z_\ell\uparrow1,\quad Z_\ell\pi_\ell\uparrow\pi,\quad Z_\ell\mu_{t,\ell}\uparrow\mu_t,\quad Z_\ell\Pi_\ell\uparrow\Pi,\text{ with the stated compactness, optimality, and absolute-continuity/map-preservation properties.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic Benamou-Brenier action in density-momentum and measure formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the quadratic perspective integrand by \[\Phi(r,w)=\begin{cases}|w|^2/r,&r>0,\\0,&(r,w)=(0,0),\\+\infty,&r=0\text{ and }w\ne0.\end{cases}\] For densities relative to a reference measure, the dynamic action is \(\mathcal A(\rho,m)=\int\Phi(\rho,m)\). Intrinsically for measures, \(\mathcal A(\rho,m)=\int|v|^2\,d\rho\) when \(m=v\rho\) for some \(v\in L^2(\rho;\mathbb R^d)\), and \(\mathcal A(\rho,m)=+\infty\) otherwise. Minimizing this action subject to the continuity equation and endpoint constraints gives the squared quadratic dynamic transport cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic transport action integrates kinetic energy per unit mass; it is finite precisely when momentum has a square-integrable velocity density relative to mass.
knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Action Functionals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the dynamic-action leaf, but the perspective formula, intrinsic measure formulation, finiteness characterization, and normalization of the dynamic transport cost lack a cited authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian Action on a Polish Space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines an axiomatic path-space action, its endpoint costs, its partition representation, and endpoint-constrained minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (\mathcal X,d) be a Polish space and let t_i,t_f\in\mathbb R. A Lagrangian action consists of lower-semicontinuous functionals \mathcal A^{s,t} on C([s,t];\mathcal X), for t_i\le s<t\le t_f, and cost functions c^{s,t} on \mathcal X\times\mathcal X such that: (i) the action is additive across consecutive time intervals; (ii) c^{s,t}(x,y)=\inf\{\mathcal A^{s,t}(\gamma):\gamma\in C([s,t];\mathcal X),\ \gamma_s=x,\ \gamma_t=y\}; and (iii) for every \gamma\in C([t_i,t_f];\mathcal X), \mathcal A^{t_i,t_f}(\gamma)=\sup_{N\in\mathbb N}\sup_{t_i=t_0\le\cdots\le t_N=t_f}\sum_{j=1}^{N}c^{t_{j-1},t_j}(\gamma_{t_{j-1}},\gamma_{t_j}). A curve is action-minimizing if it minimizes \mathcal A^{t_i,t_f} among curves with the same endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lagrangian action is a lower-semicontinuous, time-additive family of path functionals. Its endpoint costs are obtained by minimizing over connecting curves, and its full action equals the supremum of accumulated costs over finite time partitions. An action-minimizing curve minimizes the action among curves with its endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\mathcal A^{s,t},c^{s,t})\text{ is a Lagrangian action precisely when conditions (i)--(iii) hold.}
