knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-cone interpretation of nonsmoothness created by a hard feasible-set indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Wasserstein normal cone generated by the constraint is defined through the indicator subdifferential: \[N_K(\mu):=\partial I_K(\mu).\] Hence \(N_K(\mu)=\varnothing\) whenever \(\mu\notin K\). For \(\mu\in K\), a field \(\xi\in L^2(\mu;\mathbb R^d)\) belongs to \(N_K(\mu)\) precisely when it satisfies the selected Wasserstein subgradient condition for \(I_K\). Thus an extended-real constraint can introduce set-valued nonsmoothness even when the unconstrained objective is differentiable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lower Semicontinuity of a Compact Marginal Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded marginalization theorem on Hausdorff spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) be Hausdorff, let \(\mathcal Y\) be compact Hausdorff, and let \(\varphi:\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\to[-\infty,+\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous. Define \(f:\mathcal X\to[-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(f(x)=\inf_{y\in\mathcal Y}\varphi(x,y)\). Suppose \(\gamma_n\in\mathcal P(X_1\times X_2)\) converges narrowly to \(\gamma=\int\gamma_{x_1}\,d\mu_1(x_1)\), where \(\mu_1=(\pi^1)_\#\gamma\), and the barycenter \(\bar\gamma(x_1)=\int x_2\,d\gamma_{x_1}(x_2)\) exists. If \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\int f(x_2)\,d\gamma_n=\int f(\bar\gamma(x_1))\,d\mu_1(x_1)<+\infty,\] then \[\gamma=(\operatorname{id}_{X_1},\bar\gamma)_\#\mu_1.\] The same graph-concentration conclusion holds when \((\pi^1)_\#\gamma_n=\mu_1\) and \(f:X_1\times X_2\to[0,+\infty]\) is a normal integrand with \(f(x_1,\cdot)\) strictly convex for \(\mu_1\)-almost every \(x_1\), under the analogous finite equality; in that case \(\bar\gamma_n\to\bar\gamma\) in \(\mu_1\)-measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the lower-limit integral of a nonnegative lower-semicontinuous strictly convex function attains exactly its value at the conditional barycenters, the limiting plan has no conditional dispersion: it is concentrated on the graph of its barycenter map. With fixed first marginals and an almost-everywhere strictly convex normal integrand, the same concentration holds and the barycenter maps converge in measure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Probabilistic superposition principle for the continuity equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between narrowly continuous measure solutions and probability superpositions of characteristic ODE trajectories, subject to the stated integrability conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let p>1, and let (\mu_t)_{t\in[0,T]}\subset\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d) be narrowly continuous and solve the continuity equation for a Borel vector field v_t satisfying the stated condition (8.1.21). Then there exists \boldsymbol\eta\in\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d\times\Gamma_T) concentrated on pairs (x,\gamma) such that \gamma\in AC^p(0,T;\mathbb R^d), \gamma(0)=x, and \dot\gamma(t)=v_t(\gamma(t)) for \mathcal L^1\text{-a.e. }t, with \mu_t=(e_t)_\#\boldsymbol\eta for every t\in[0,T]. Conversely, if \boldsymbol\eta is concentrated on such characteristic pairs and \int_0^T\int |v_t(\gamma(t))|\,d\boldsymbol\eta(x,\gamma)\,dt<\infty, then \mu_t:=(e_t)_\#\boldsymbol\eta solves the continuity equation and \mu_0=(e_0)_\#\boldsymbol\eta.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For p>1, every narrowly continuous solution of the continuity equation driven by a suitable Borel vector field satisfying the stated integrability condition can be represented as the time marginals of a probability measure concentrated on absolutely continuous characteristic curves. Conversely, an integrable probability superposition of such characteristic curves induces a solution of the continuity equation, with initial measure equal to its time-zero marginal.
assumptions_latex: (\mu_t)_{t\in[0,T]}\subset\mathcal P(\mathbb R^d)\text{ is narrowly continuous and solves the continuity equation}
v:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\text{ is Borel and satisfies condition }(8.1.21)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classical Conditions on a Lagrangian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a regularity and coercivity regime for a time-dependent Lagrangian on a complete Riemannian manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M be a smooth complete Riemannian manifold and L:TM\times[0,1]\to\mathbb R a Lagrangian. The classical conditions are: (a) L is C^1 in all variables; (b) v\mapsto L(x,v,t) is strictly convex and superlinear; (c) there exist K,C>0 such that L(x,v,t)\ge K|v|-C for every (x,v,t)\in TM\times[0,1]; and (d) there is a locally Lipschitz map \phi_t(x_0,v_0,t_0) on TM\times[0,1]\times[0,1], valued in TM, such that every action-minimizing curve \gamma belongs to C^1([0,1];M) and satisfies (\gamma(t),\dot\gamma(t))=\phi_t(\gamma(t_0),\dot\gamma(t_0),t_0).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lagrangian satisfies the classical conditions when it is continuously differentiable, strictly convex and superlinear in velocity, has a uniform linear lower-growth bound, and generates a locally Lipschitz flow followed by every continuously differentiable action-minimizing curve.
assumptions_latex: M\text{ is a smooth complete Riemannian manifold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ satisfies the classical conditions exactly when conditions (a)--(d) hold.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Shortening Lemma for Power Costs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform interior-time separation estimate for two Euclidean displacement segments satisfying a two-pair power-cost inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(0<\alpha<1\), let \(x_1,y_1,x_2,y_2\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and suppose
\[
|x_1-y_1|^{1+\alpha}+|x_2-y_2|^{1+\alpha}\le |x_1-y_2|^{1+\alpha}+|x_2-y_1|^{1+\alpha}.
\]
Define \(\gamma_i(t)=(1-t)x_i+ty_i\) for \(i=1,2\). For every \(t_0\in(0,1)\), there exists \(K(\alpha,t_0)>0\), independent of the four points, such that
\[
|\gamma_1(t_0)-\gamma_2(t_0)|\ge K(\alpha,t_0)\sup_{0\le t\le1}|\gamma_1(t)-\gamma_2(t)|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two Euclidean displacement segments whose matched power cost does not exceed the crossed matching cost, their separation at any fixed interior time controls, by a positive factor depending only on the power and that time, their maximum separation over the entire interpolation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K(\alpha,t_0)>0\ \text{such that}\ |\gamma_1(t_0)-\gamma_2(t_0)|\ge K(\alpha,t_0)\sup_{0\le t\le1}|\gamma_1(t)-\gamma_2(t)|.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: c-Cyclically Monotone Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition for an extended-real-valued transport cost on a product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let c:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}. A set \Gamma\subset X\times Y is c-cyclically monotone if, for every k\in\mathbb{N}, every permutation \sigma of \{1,\ldots,k\}, and every \{(x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_k,y_k)\}\subset\Gamma, one has \sum_{i=1}^k c(x_i,y_i)\leq\sum_{i=1}^k c(x_i,y_{\sigma(i)}).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset Gamma of X × Y is c-cyclically monotone when every finite matching of its listed x- and y-components has cost no greater than any permutation of those y-components.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i=1}^k c(x_i,y_i)\leq\sum_{i=1}^k c(x_i,y_{\sigma(i)})

children.title: Minimizer Stability
children.top_down_role: Persistence of minimizing states under perturbation or variational convergence.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space and \((F_n)\) is equicoercive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_XF_n\to\min_XF\), and every cluster point of \((x_n)\) belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_XF\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fundamental theorem of Gamma-convergence under equicoercivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fundamental minimizer theorem for equicoercive Gamma-convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \((x_n)\) is relatively compact. Every cluster point \(x\) minimizes \(F\), and the minimum values converge: \(F(x)=\min_XF\) and \(\inf_XF_n\to\min_XF\). If \(F\) has a unique minimizer \(x_*\), then the entire sequence converges, \(x_n\to x_*\). The same conclusions hold for exact minimizers by taking \(\varepsilon_n=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equicoercive Gamma-convergence carries approximate minimizers to minimizers of the limit and makes minimum values converge.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimizer Stability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An authoritative source and precise theorem locator are required. As written, equicoercivity does not by itself bound approximate-minimizer energies unless the limit has a finite value, so properness of the Gamma-limit or an equivalent finite-energy hypothesis is needed for the asserted relative compactness and finite minimizer conclusion.

children.title: Resolvent Stability
children.top_down_role: Continuity of proximal or resolvent constructions under changing energies.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a proper metric space, \(\tau>0\), and \(F_n\xrightarrow{\Gamma}F\).
\(x_n\to x\), and the penalized functionals \(y\mapsto F_n(y)+d^2(y,x_n)/(2\tau)\) are equicoercive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_\tau^{F_n}(x_n)\to J_\tau^F(x)\) and \(F_{n,\tau}(x_n)\to F_\tau(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimizer stability applied to Moreau--Yosida perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability of single-valued metric resolvents at a fixed time step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_n\in J_\tau^{F_n}(x_n)\). The squared-distance perturbations Gamma-converge to \(y\mapsto F(y)+d^2(y,x)/(2\tau)\). Consequently, minimizer stability gives \(y_n\to y\), where \(y\) is the unique element of \(J_\tau^F(x)\), and the Moreau-envelope values satisfy \(F_{n,\tau}(x_n)\to F_\tau(x)\). Without uniqueness, every cluster point of \((y_n)\) belongs to \(J_\tau^F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gamma-convergence and compactness make proximal minimizers and envelope values stable; uniqueness upgrades subsequential convergence to full convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Stability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The result is plausible as an application of minimizer stability, but no source is supplied. The conclusion treats the generally set-valued resolvent as a point, whereas the statement later introduces selections. A sourced version must quantify resolvent selections, ensure their existence, and state set-valued convergence separately if that is intended.

children.top_down_role: Relations between stable resolvent problems and limiting minimizers.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is proper and \(F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is lower semicontinuous with nonempty compact sublevels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(y_k,\operatorname*{argmin}F)\to0\) and \(F(y_k)\to\min F\).

Distance from a point to a set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: vanishing proximal penalty as the step size diverges
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-step resolvents converge to global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(z\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\), resolvent minimality yields \(F(y_k)+d^2(y_k,x)/(2\tau_k)\le F(z)+d^2(z,x)/(2\tau_k)\). Hence \(F(y_k)\to\min F\). Compactness of sublevels makes \((y_k)\) relatively compact, and lower semicontinuity places every cluster point in \(\operatorname*{argmin}F\). Therefore its distance to the minimizer set tends to zero; if the minimizer is unique, then \(y_k\) converges to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As the resolvent step grows, its distance penalty vanishes and proximal minimizers approach the global minimizer set.
knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent-to-Minimizer Passage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The large-step resolvent conclusion is standard under suitable properness, existence, and compactness assumptions, but no citation is supplied. The phrase 'nonempty compact sublevels' is ambiguous, and the statement contains a proof argument rather than only the theorem. A source is needed to fix the precise hypotheses before revision.

children.title: Loss of Compactness
children.top_down_role: Escape, concentration, or oscillation regimes obstructing variational limits.

assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)\) carries the Wasserstein distance \(W_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_n\xrightarrow{\Gamma}F\), but \((\mu_n)\) has no \(W_2\)-convergent subsequence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: translating Dirac masses exhibit escape to infinity in Wasserstein space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Escape to infinity despite exact Gamma-convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constant sequence of functionals Gamma-converges to \(F\), and every \(\mu_n\) is an exact minimizer. Nevertheless, \(W_2(\mu_n,\mu_m)=|n-m|\), so \((\mu_n)\) is not Cauchy and has no convergent subsequence. Thus Gamma-convergence without equicoercivity does not ensure compactness or convergence of minimizers; in Wasserstein space, control of mass escape and second moments is indispensable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translating Dirac masses are exact minimizers of a Gamma-convergent sequence but escape to infinity, showing why equicoercivity is essential.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Compactness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The translating-Dirac construction is mathematically coherent and the counterexample content kind fits the loss-of-compactness leaf. However, the record has no inspectable source with a specific locator, so it cannot be accepted at this review layer.

children.title: Metric-Slope Stability
children.top_down_role: Persistence of slope information under convergence of measures or energies.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space and \(F_n,F:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper and lower semicontinuous.
For every \(x_n\to x\) with \(F_n(x_n)\to F(x)\), \(|\partial F|(x)\le\liminf_n|\partial F_n|(x_n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\partial F|\) is lower stable along energy-convergent sequences.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: slope liminf condition used in variational convergence of gradient flows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower stability of descending slopes under Gamma-convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Metric-slope stability is the lower-semicontinuity requirement that whenever \(x_n\to x\) and the energies also converge, \(F_n(x_n)\to F(x)\), one has \(|\partial F|(x)\le\liminf_{n\to\infty}|\partial F_n|(x_n)\). Together with suitable compactness, this inequality prevents dissipation from disappearing in the variational limit and is the slope component of stability results for minimizing movements and curves of maximal slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slope stability requires the limit slope not to exceed the lower limit of approximating slopes along sequences whose positions and energies converge.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Slope Stability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed slope inequality is introduced as an assumption and then merely restated as the conclusion. This is a stability condition or definition, not an established property following from Gamma-convergence alone. A source is needed to determine the intended named condition and its precise scope.

children.title: Slope-Stability Failure
children.top_down_role: Regimes where limiting energies do not retain the expected slope behavior.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_n\xrightarrow{\Gamma}F\), yet slope lower stability fails at \(x=0\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean descending slope of a differentiable function
A sequence converging to zero with vanishing derivative

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: vanishing-amplitude, high-frequency perturbations preserve energies but alter derivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oscillatory perturbations destroy slope convergence despite uniform energy convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The functions \(F_n\) converge locally uniformly, hence Gamma-converge, to \(F\), and their quadratic terms give equicoercivity. Since \(F_n'(x)=2x+1+2\cos(nx)\), continuity provides points \(x_n\to0\) with \(F_n'(x_n)=0\). Moreover, \(F_n(x_n)\to F(0)\), but \(|\partial F_n|(x_n)=0\) while \(|\partial F|(0)=|F'(0)|=1\). Therefore the required slope liminf inequality fails even though energies and minimizers remain compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small high-frequency energy perturbations can converge uniformly while creating nearby critical points, so their slopes need not converge from below.
knowledge_statements.title: Slope-Stability Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oscillatory example is internally consistent: local uniform convergence gives Gamma-convergence, nearby zeros of the derivatives can approach zero, and the limiting slope there is one. The counterexample kind fits the failure leaf, but an inspectable source locator is absent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Arithmetic–Geometric Mean and Determinant Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States weighted scalar AM–GM, concavity of the determinant root, and the associated multiplicative determinant inequality for positive-semidefinite matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i\geq0\), \(\lambda_i\geq0\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i=1\). With the convention \(0^0=1\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i x_i\geq\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\lambda_i}\). If \(A,B\in S_n^+(\mathbb R)\) and \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), then \[\bigl(\det(\lambda A+(1-\lambda)B)\bigr)^{1/n}\geq\lambda(\det A)^{1/n}+(1-\lambda)(\det B)^{1/n},\] and \[\det(\lambda A+(1-\lambda)B)\geq(\det A)^\lambda(\det B)^{1-\lambda}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted arithmetic mean of nonnegative numbers dominates the corresponding weighted geometric mean. For positive-semidefinite matrices, the nth root of the determinant is concave, and the determinant satisfies the corresponding multiplicative inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i x_i\geq\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\lambda_i};\quad \bigl(\det(\lambda A+(1-\lambda)B)\bigr)^{1/n}\geq\lambda(\det A)^{1/n}+(1-\lambda)(\det B)^{1/n};\quad \det(\lambda A+(1-\lambda)B)\geq(\det A)^\lambda(\det B)^{1-\lambda}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimal-Subpath Characterization of Dynamic Transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prefix-and-suffix optimality for homogeneous-cost transport, including the trajectory-crossing boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be absolutely continuous probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^n$ or a smooth complete Riemannian manifold, let $c$ be a homogeneous cost, and assume that the Monge minimization problem has a unique solution. A family $(T_t)_{0\le t\le1}$ solves the time-dependent minimization problem if and only if, for every $t_0\in[0,1]$, $(T_t)_{0\le t\le t_0}$ gives an optimal transport from $\mu$ to $(T_{t_0})_\#\mu$ and $(T_t)_{t_0\le t\le1}$ gives an optimal transport from $(T_{t_0})_\#\mu$ to $\nu$. If trajectories cross at $t_0$, the latter family must be interpreted in a generalized transport sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a homogeneous cost and uniqueness of the Monge solution, a dynamic interpolation is optimal exactly when every prefix and suffix is optimal for its induced endpoint measures. A generalized interpretation is required after an intermediate trajectory crossing.

c\text{ is a homogeneous transport cost}
\text{the Monge minimization problem has a unique solution}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (T_t)_{0\le t\le1}\text{ is dynamically optimal}\iff\forall t_0,\text{ its prefix and suffix are optimal for their induced endpoint measures, with generalized interpretation after crossings}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Displacement convexity of a negative-power density functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional displacement convexity and preservation of a common positive density lower bound along the associated Wasserstein geodesic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(d=1\), \(\Omega=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R\), and \(q>0\). For \(\rho\ll\mathcal L^1\), define \(F(\rho)=\int_a^b \rho(x)^{-q}\,\mathrm dx\). Then \(F\) is displacement convex in \(\mathbb W_p(\Omega)\). In particular, if \(\rho_0,\rho_1\ge c>0\) and \((\rho_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\) is the geodesic connecting them, then \(\rho_t(x)\ge c\) for every \(t\in[0,1]\), with the density inequality understood almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a one-dimensional interval, the integral of the negative q-th power of an absolutely continuous density is displacement convex. In particular, a common positive lower bound for the endpoint densities is preserved along their Wasserstein geodesic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(\rho)=\int_a^b\rho(x)^{-q}\,\mathrm dx\text{ is displacement convex in }\mathbb W_p(\Omega);\quad \rho_t\ge c\text{ for every }t\in[0,1]\text{ in the lower-bound specialization.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Plan-Based Displacement Convexity and the Cost-Generalized Variant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines displacement convexity using optimal-plan interpolations in quadratic Wasserstein space and records the analogous construction for strictly convex costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\sigma_t(x,y)=(1-t)x+ty\). A set \(\mathcal P\subset P_2(\mathbb R^n)\) is displacement convex if, for every \(\rho_0,\rho_1\in\mathcal P\), every optimal quadratic-cost transport plan \(\pi\) between them, and every \(t\in[0,1]\), one has \(\rho_t=(\sigma_t)_\#\pi\in\mathcal P\). A functional \(F\) on such a set is displacement convex if \(t\mapsto F(\rho_t)\) is convex on \([0,1]\) for every such interpolation. For a strictly convex cost \(c(x-y)\), the analogous notion of \(c\)-displacement convexity uses a cost-optimal plan, provided \(T_c(\mu,\nu)<+\infty\) for all \(\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plan-based displacement convexity requires closure under interpolations generated by optimal quadratic-cost transport plans, and functional values must be convex along all such interpolations. The analogous definition applies to a strictly convex transport cost when every pair in the family has finite transport cost.
assumptions_latex: \pi\text{ is optimal for the quadratic-cost Monge--Kantorovich problem}
c(x-y)\text{ is strictly convex and }T_c(\mu,\nu)<+\infty\ \forall\mu,\nu\in\mathcal P\text{ for the }c\text{-variant}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\sigma_t)_\#\pi\in\mathcal P;\qquad t\mapsto F((\sigma_t)_\#\pi)\text{ is convex on }[0,1],\text{ with the analogous definition for optimal }c\text{-cost plans}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hamilton–Jacobi formulation of Kantorovich duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The main equality is clear. The extract's separate attainment note uses the undefined symbol \(\mathcal T_r\), which must not be silently normalized to \(\mathcal T_c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be strictly convex and superlinear, and let \(\mu,\nu\) be probability measures on \(\mathbb R^n\). Then
\[
\mathcal T_c(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{\varphi}\left\{\int_{\mathbb R^n}\varphi(1,x)\,d\nu(x)-\int_{\mathbb R^n}\varphi(0,x)\,d\mu(x)\right\},
\]
where the supremum ranges over solutions of
\[
\partial_t\varphi+c^*(\nabla_x\varphi)=0,\qquad \varphi(0,\cdot)=\varphi_0\in C_b(\mathbb R^n).
\]
The extract additionally states that the supremum is attained when \(\mathcal T_r(\mu,\nu)<+\infty\), provided more general initial data are allowed; the symbol \(r\) is not defined in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly convex superlinear cost, the Kantorovich transport value equals the supremum of the terminal-minus-initial expectations over Hamilton–Jacobi solutions with bounded continuous initial data. A separate attainment claim is retained with its unresolved transport-cost notation.
assumptions_latex: c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ is strictly convex and superlinear}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Displacement, Lambda-Displacement, and Variable-Curvature Displacement Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functionals on the absolutely continuous quadratic-Wasserstein space; the defining inequalities quantify over every constant-speed minimizing geodesic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:\mathcal P_2^{\mathrm{ac}}(M)\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}. It is displacement convex if every constant-speed minimizing geodesic (\mu_t) in \mathcal P_2^{\mathrm{ac}}(M) satisfies F(\mu_t)\le(1-t)F(\mu_0)+tF(\mu_1) for every t\in[0,1]. It is \lambda-displacement convex if every such geodesic satisfies F(\mu_t)\le(1-t)F(\mu_0)+tF(\mu_1)-\frac{\lambda t(1-t)}2W_2(\mu_0,\mu_1)^2 for every t\in[0,1]. It is \Lambda-displacement convex if, for every such geodesic and every associated Hamilton--Jacobi solution (\psi_t), F(\mu_t)\le(1-t)F(\mu_0)+tF(\mu_1)-\int_0^1\Lambda(\mu_s,\widetilde\nabla\psi_s)G(s,t)\,ds for every t\in[0,1], assuming for each t that the integrand is bounded below by an integrable function of s. The last notion reduces to \lambda-displacement convexity when \Lambda(\mu,v)=\lambda\|v\|_{L^2(\mu)}^2, and \lambda-displacement convexity reduces to displacement convexity when \lambda=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Displacement convexity is convexity along every constant-speed minimizing quadratic-Wasserstein geodesic. Lambda-displacement convexity adds the squared-Wasserstein curvature correction. Lambda-displacement convexity with a variable quadratic form instead uses a Green-kernel correction along an associated Hamilton–Jacobi velocity field, subject to an integrable lower bound. These notions specialize successively to constant-lambda and ordinary displacement convexity.
assumptions_latex: (\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\text{ is a constant-speed minimizing geodesic in }\mathcal P_2^{\mathrm{ac}}(M)
\text{For }\Lambda\text{-displacement convexity, }(\psi_t)\text{ is an associated Hamilton--Jacobi solution}
\text{For each }t,\ s\mapsto\Lambda(\mu_s,\widetilde\nabla\psi_s)G(s,t)\text{ is bounded below by an integrable function}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Lambda\text{-displacement convexity specializes to }\lambda\text{-displacement convexity when }\Lambda(\mu,v)=\lambda\|v\|_{L^2(\mu)}^2,\text{ and the latter specializes to displacement convexity when }\lambda=0.

u_0(x)=\varphi(x)-\frac{|x|^2}{2},\qquad

\qquad \rho_t=(T_t)_\#\rho_0.

\]
holds weakly on \((0,1)\times\mathbb R^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict, Uniform, and Semiconvex Variants of Displacement Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the variants for the displacement interpolations of Definition 5.12 in the quadratic-cost Euclidean setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Using the displacement interpolations \((\rho_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\) of a displacement-convex set \(\mathcal P\), \(F\) is strictly displacement convex if \(\rho_0\ne\rho_1\) implies that \(t\mapsto F(\rho_t)\) is strictly convex on \([0,1]\). For \(\lambda>0\), it is \(\lambda\)-uniformly displacement convex if \(\frac{d^2}{dt^2}F(\rho_t)\geq\lambda\mathcal T_2(\rho_0,\rho_1)\) for all endpoints and \(t\in(0,1)\). It is semi-displacement-convex with constant \(C\geq0\) if \(\frac{d^2}{dt^2}F(\rho_t)\geq-C\mathcal T_2(\rho_0,\rho_1)\). Here \(\mathcal T_2\) is the total quadratic transportation cost. Similar definitions may be formulated for nonquadratic costs and for measures on Riemannian manifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict displacement convexity means strict convexity along interpolations between distinct measures. Uniform displacement convexity imposes a positive curvature lower bound scaled by quadratic transport cost, while semi-displacement-convexity permits a negative lower bound. The source notes analogous notions for other costs and Riemannian manifolds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criteria for Displacement Convexity of Internal, Potential, and Interaction Energies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collects sufficient and converse criteria for three standard energy-functional families, including the fixed-mean restriction for strong interaction-energy conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be displacement convex, with \(\mathcal P\subset P_{\mathrm{ac}}(\mathbb R^n)\) for (i) and \(\mathcal P\subset P_2(\mathbb R^n)\) for (ii)--(iii), and suppose \(\mathcal U,\mathcal V,\mathcal W\) are well-defined on \(\mathcal P\) with values in \(\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). (i) If \(U(0)=0\) and \(\Psi(r)=r^nU(r^{-n})\) is convex and nonincreasing on \((0,+\infty)\), then \(\mathcal U\) is displacement convex. Conversely, if \(\Psi\) is nonincreasing and \(\mathcal U\) is displacement convex on \(P_{\mathrm{ac}}(\mathbb R^n)\), then \(\Psi\) is convex. (ii) If \(V\) is convex, strictly convex, \(\lambda\)-uniformly convex, or semiconvex with constant \(C\), then \(\mathcal V\) has the corresponding displacement-convexity property. If \(\mathcal V\) is displacement convex on \(P_2(\mathbb R^n)\), then \(V\) is convex. (iii) Convexity or semiconvexity with constant \(C\) of \(W\) implies the corresponding displacement property of \(\mathcal W\). If \(W\) is strictly convex or \(\lambda\)-uniformly convex, then \(\mathcal W\) has the corresponding displacement property on each fixed-mean class \(\mathcal P_m\). If \(\mathcal W\) is displacement convex on \(P_2(\mathbb R^n)\), then \(W\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The transformed internal-energy integrand gives a sufficient displacement-convexity criterion and, under monotonicity, a converse. Convexity variants of an external potential transfer to its potential energy. Convexity and semiconvexity of an interaction kernel transfer to interaction energy, while strict and uniform conclusions require a fixed-mean class. Global displacement convexity of the potential or interaction energy implies convexity of the underlying function.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal U,\mathcal V,\mathcal W:\mathcal P\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ are well-defined}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Psi\text{ convex and nonincreasing}\Rightarrow\mathcal U\text{ displacement convex};\quad V\text{ and }W\text{ convexity variants imply the stated displacement variants};\quad \mathcal W\text{ is strictly or uniformly displacement convex only on }\mathcal P_m\text{ under the corresponding hypotheses};\quad \text{the stated global converses hold}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent Characterizations of Riemannian Lambda-Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The Hessian inequality is global on the manifold, while the other equivalent conditions quantify over every constant-speed minimizing geodesic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let (M,g) be a Riemannian manifold and let \Lambda:TM	o\mathbb R be continuous, with \Lambda(x,\cdot) quadratic. Assume that every constant-speed geodesic \gamma satisfies \lambda[\gamma]:=\inf_{0\le s\le1}\Lambda(\gamma_s,\dot\gamma_s)/|\dot\gamma_s|^2>-\infty. For F\in C^2(M), the following are equivalent: (i) 
abla^2F(x)[v,v]\ge\Lambda(x,v) for all (x,v)\in TM; (ii) every constant-speed minimizing geodesic \gamma satisfies F(\gamma_t)\le(1-t)F(\gamma_0)+tF(\gamma_1)-\int_0^1\Lambda(\gamma_s,\dot\gamma_s)G(s,t)\,ds for all t\in[0,1]; (iii) every such \gamma satisfies F(\gamma_1)\ge F(\gamma_0)+\langle
abla F(\gamma_0),\dot\gamma_0angle+\int_0^1\Lambda(\gamma_t,\dot\gamma_t)(1-t)\,dt; and (iv) every such \gamma satisfies \langle
abla F(\gamma_1),\dot\gamma_1angle-\langle
abla F(\gamma_0),\dot\gamma_0angle\ge\int_0^1\Lambda(\gamma_t,\dot\gamma_t)\,dt. Equivalence is preserved when (ii), (iii), and (iv) are respectively replaced by the same inequalities with correction terms \lambda[\gamma]t(1-t)d(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)^2/2, \lambda[\gamma]d(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)^2/2, and \lambda[\gamma]d(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)^2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice continuously differentiable function on a Riemannian manifold, a pointwise quadratic Hessian lower bound is equivalent to corrected interpolation, endpoint-support, and directional-gradient inequalities along every constant-speed minimizing geodesic. The corresponding bounds using the least normalized value of the quadratic form along each geodesic are equivalent as well.
assumptions_latex: \Lambda:TM\to\mathbb R\text{ is continuous and }\Lambda(x,\cdot)\text{ is quadratic}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla^2F\ge\Lambda\iff\text{the corrected geodesic interpolation, endpoint-support, and directional-gradient inequalities hold, including their }\lambda[\gamma]\text{-based variants.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geodesic and Weak Geodesic Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General complete geodesic spaces; the weak notion quantifies existentially over geodesics joining each endpoint pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (\mathcal X,d) be a complete geodesic space and F:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}. The function F is geodesically convex if, for every constant-speed geodesic (\gamma_t)_{t\in[0,1]}, F(\gamma_t)\le (1-t)F(\gamma_0)+tF(\gamma_1) for all t\in[0,1]. It is weakly geodesically convex if, for every x_0,x_1\in\mathcal X, there exists at least one constant-speed geodesic \gamma from x_0 to x_1 satisfying this inequality for every t\in[0,1].
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function on a complete geodesic space is geodesically convex when the convexity inequality holds along every constant-speed geodesic. It is weakly geodesically convex when every pair of points admits at least one constant-speed geodesic along which the inequality holds.
assumptions_latex: (\mathcal X,d)\text{ is a complete geodesic space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is geodesically convex when the inequality holds along every constant-speed geodesic; weak geodesic convexity requires one such geodesic for each endpoint pair.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riemannian Lambda-Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real-valued functions on a Riemannian manifold, with variable quadratic or constant metric curvature correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M be a Riemannian manifold and let \Lambda(x,v) be a continuous quadratic form satisfying \lambda[\gamma]:=\inf_{0\le s\le1}\Lambda(\gamma_s,\dot\gamma_s)/|\dot\gamma_s|^2>-\infty along every constant-speed geodesic. A function F:M\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\} is \Lambda-convex if, for every constant-speed minimizing geodesic \gamma and every t\in[0,1], F(\gamma_t)\le(1-t)F(\gamma_0)+tF(\gamma_1)-\int_0^1\Lambda(\gamma_s,\dot\gamma_s)G(s,t)\,ds. If \Lambda=\lambda g with \lambda\in\mathbb R, this is called \lambda-convexity; when \lambda=0 it is ordinary geodesic convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lambda-convexity on a Riemannian manifold is the geodesic interpolation inequality corrected by the Green-kernel integral of a continuous quadratic form. Taking the form to be lambda times the metric gives lambda-convexity, and lambda equal to zero gives ordinary geodesic convexity.
assumptions_latex: \Lambda(x,\cdot)\text{ is a continuous quadratic form satisfying the finite geodesic lower-bound condition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is }\Lambda\text{-convex when the corrected interpolation inequality holds on every constant-speed minimizing geodesic; }\Lambda=\lambda g\text{ gives }\lambda\text{-convexity, and }\lambda=0\text{ gives ordinary geodesic convexity.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lambda-Convexity along Generalized Geodesics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition using a common-base generalized geodesic and its coupling-dependent squared endpoint cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\). A functional \(\phi\) is \(\lambda\)-convex along generalized geodesics if, for every \(\mu^1,\mu^2,\mu^3\in D(\phi)\), there exists a generalized geodesic \(\mu_t^{2\to3}\) with base \(\mu^1\), induced by a plan \(\boldsymbol\mu\in\Gamma(\mu^1,\mu^2,\mu^3)\) whose \((1,2)\)- and \((1,3)\)-marginals are optimal, such that
\[
\phi(\mu_t^{2\to3})\leq(1-t)\phi(\mu^2)+t\phi(\mu^3)-\frac\lambda2t(1-t)W_{\boldsymbol\mu}^2(\mu^2,\mu^3)
\quad\text{for every }t\in[0,1].
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional is lambda-convex along generalized geodesics when every three domain points admit a generalized geodesic between the second and third, based at the first, along which the lambda-convexity inequality holds with the coupling-dependent endpoint cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall t\in[0,1],\quad\phi(\mu_t^{2\to3})\leq(1-t)\phi(\mu^2)+t\phi(\mu^3)-\frac\lambda2t(1-t)W_{\boldsymbol\mu}^2(\mu^2,\mu^3).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity of the Wasserstein Proximal Functional
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity enhancement for the Wasserstein proximal functional under generalized-geodesic convexity of its energy term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(\phi:\mathcal P_2(X)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and \(\lambda\)-convex along generalized geodesics. For every \(\mu^1\in D(\phi)\) and every \(0<\tau<1/\lambda^-\), the functional
\[
\Phi(\tau,\mu^1;\mu):=\frac1{2\tau}W_2^2(\mu^1,\mu)+\phi(\mu)
\]
satisfies the referenced convexity assumption with convexity parameter \(\tau^{-1}+\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a proper functional is lambda-convex along generalized geodesics, adding a Wasserstein proximal quadratic centered at a domain point gives the convexity property required by the referenced assumption, with parameter one over tau plus lambda, under the stated step-size restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Phi(\tau,\mu^1;\cdot)=\frac1{2\tau}W_2^2(\mu^1,\cdot)+\phi\text{ satisfies the referenced convexity assumption with parameter }\tau^{-1}+\lambda.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Squared Wasserstein Distance along a Generalized Geodesic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact quadratic identity and resulting 1-convexity inequality for squared Wasserstein distance along a generalized geodesic based at the distance center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu^1,\mu^2,\mu^3\in\mathcal P_2(X)\), and let \(\boldsymbol\mu\in\Gamma(\mu^1,\mu^2,\mu^3)\) satisfy \(\pi^{1,2}_\#\boldsymbol\mu\in\Gamma_o(\mu^1,\mu^2)\) and \(\pi^{1,3}_\#\boldsymbol\mu\in\Gamma_o(\mu^1,\mu^3)\). For \(t\in[0,1]\), define \(\mu_t^{2\to3}=((1-t)\pi^2+t\pi^3)_\#\boldsymbol\mu\). Then
\[
W_2^2(\mu^1,\mu_t^{2\to3})=\int_{X^3}|(1-t)x_2+tx_3-x_1|^2\,d\boldsymbol\mu
\]
\[
=(1-t)W_2^2(\mu^1,\mu^2)+tW_2^2(\mu^1,\mu^3)-t(1-t)W_{\boldsymbol\mu}^2(\mu^2,\mu^3)
\]
\[
\leq(1-t)W_2^2(\mu^1,\mu^2)+tW_2^2(\mu^1,\mu^3)-t(1-t)W_2^2(\mu^2,\mu^3).
\]
Consequently, \(\frac12W_2^2(\mu^1,\cdot)\) is 1-convex along this curve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a triple coupling whose base-to-endpoint marginals are optimal, the squared distance from the base to the induced generalized geodesic obeys an exact quadratic interpolation identity. Bounding the coupling-dependent endpoint cost below by the Wasserstein distance gives 1-convexity along that curve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac12W_2^2(\mu^1,\cdot)\text{ is 1-convex along }(\mu_t^{2\to3})_{t\in[0,1]}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Map Criterion for Generalized-Geodesic Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent testing criterion using regular base measures and essentially injective maps with cyclically monotone graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi:\mathcal P_2(X)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be lower semicontinuous and suppose that, for every \(\nu\in D(\phi)\), there exist \(\nu_h\in\mathcal P_2^r(X)\) such that \(\nu_h\to\nu\) in \(\mathcal P_2(X)\) and \(\phi(\nu_h)\to\phi(\nu)\). Then \(\phi\) is \(\lambda\)-convex along generalized geodesics if and only if, for every \(\mu\in\mathcal P_2^r(X)\) and every pair of \(\mu\)-essentially injective maps \(\mathbf r^0,\mathbf r^1\in L^2(\mu;X)\), each having cyclically monotone graph,
\[
\phi(((1-t)\mathbf r^0+t\mathbf r^1)_\#\mu)
\leq(1-t)\phi(\mathbf r^0_\#\mu)+t\phi(\mathbf r^1_\#\mu)
-\frac\lambda2t(1-t)\int_X|\mathbf r^0(x)-\mathbf r^1(x)|^2\,d\mu(x)
\]
for every \(t\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under lower semicontinuity and approximation by regular measures without loss of functional value, lambda-convexity along generalized geodesics is equivalent to checking the convexity inequality on interpolations of admissible cyclically monotone maps from every regular base measure.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf r^0,\mathbf r^1\in L^2(\mu;X)\text{ are }\mu\text{-essentially injective and each has cyclically monotone graph}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \phi\text{ is }\lambda\text{-convex along generalized geodesics}\iff\text{the stated map-interpolation inequality holds for every admissible }\mu,\mathbf r^0,\mathbf r^1\text{ and }t\in[0,1].

children.top_down_role: Implications and separations between ordinary and generalized-geodesic convexity.

assumptions_latex: The same parameter \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\) is used for both notions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{generalized-geodesic }\lambda\text{-convexity}\Longrightarrow\text{geodesic }\lambda\text{-convexity}\), while the converse is not automatic.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: ordinary displacement geodesics arise as special generalized geodesics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implication between Wasserstein generalized and ordinary geodesic convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convexity along generalized geodesics implies ordinary displacement \(\lambda\)-convexity because an optimal displacement interpolation can be realized as a generalized geodesic by taking one endpoint as the common base. The reverse implication does not follow from the definitions: generalized geodesics include interpolations generated by two optimal base couplings whose induced endpoint coupling need not be optimal. Hence generalized-geodesic convexity imposes inequalities on a strictly larger family unless additional structure identifies the two curve classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized-geodesic convexity implies ordinary displacement convexity; the reverse needs extra structure because generalized interpolations form a larger class.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity-Notion Comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication is plausible under the usual existential generalized-geodesic convention, but its exact formulation depends on the conventions used in the two preceding definitions. No source is supplied to establish those conventions or support the claim that the converse is not automatic.

assumptions_latex: \(d\ge1\), and \(U:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is convex, lower semicontinuous, and satisfies \(U(0)=0\).
\(s\mapsto s^dU(s^{-d})\) is convex and nonincreasing on \((0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal U(\mu)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}U(\rho(x))\,dx\) is displacement convex on absolutely continuous measures \(\mu=\rho\,dx\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: McCann displacement-convexity condition for internal energies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: McCann's sufficient internal-energy regime on Euclidean Wasserstein space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the stated McCann condition, \(\mathcal U\) is convex along quadratic-Wasserstein displacement geodesics between absolutely continuous probability measures for which the energy is finite. For the power family \(U_m(r)=r^m/(m-1)\) with \(m\ne1\), the condition holds precisely in the standard regime \(m\ge1-1/d\); the limiting case \(U_1(r)=r\log r\) also satisfies it. The functional is extended by lower semicontinuity when singular measures occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: McCann's transform criterion makes internal energies displacement convex; power energies satisfy it from the threshold m at least 1 minus 1/d.
knowledge_statements.title: Internal-Energy Convexity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: McCann's transform criterion is the appropriate condition for this leaf, but the uncited power-law addendum is not reliable as stated at all endpoints: for example, the claimed closed threshold includes the problematic case m=0 when d=1. The lower-semicontinuous extension to singular measures also requires the recession-term convention to be specified. An authoritative source is needed.

children.title: Potential-Energy Convexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Spatial-potential conditions governing displacement convexity of external energies.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal V(\mu)=\int_{mathbb{R}^d}V(x)\,d\mu(x)\) is well-defined on its effective domain in \(\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal V\) is \(\lambda\)-geodesically convex along every quadratic-Wasserstein geodesic.

notation.meaning: Quadratic-Wasserstein space of probability measures with finite second moment.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: integration of a lambda-convex potential preserves lambda-convexity along displacement interpolations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-Wasserstein potential energies on Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(V((1-t)x+ty)\le (1-t)V(x)+tV(y)-\frac{\lambda}{2}t(1-t)|x-y|^2\) for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(t\in[0,1]\), then every constant-speed Wasserstein geodesic \((\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\) satisfies \[\mathcal V(\mu_t)\le (1-t)\mathcal V(\mu_0)+t\mathcal V(\mu_1)-\frac{\lambda}{2}t(1-t)W_2^2(\mu_0,\mu_1).\] Thus convex, strictly convex, and uniformly convex potentials induce the corresponding displacement-convexity regimes, subject to finiteness of the displayed energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrating a lambda-convex potential against a measure produces a lambda-geodesically convex functional in quadratic-Wasserstein space.
knowledge_statements.title: Potential-Energy Convexity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property and container fit are mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source is cited. The assumption defining the integral also contains malformed \mathbb notation and requires correction after sourcing.

children.title: Interaction-Energy Convexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Kernel conditions governing displacement convexity of interaction energies.

assumptions_latex: \(W:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, even, and \(\lambda\)-convex.
\(\mathcal W(\mu)=\frac12\iint W(x-y)\,d\mu(x)d\mu(y)\) is finite on the measures considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convex \(W\) yields displacement convexity; \(\lambda\)-convex \(W\) yields \(\lambda\)-geodesic convexity on each fixed-barycenter class.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convexity follows by integrating the kernel inequality along an optimal displacement interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation-invariant pair interactions, including the fixed-barycenter refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a geodesic induced by an optimal coupling \(\gamma\) of \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\), kernel \(\lambda\)-convexity gives \[\mathcal W(\mu_t)\le(1-t)\mathcal W(\mu_0)+t\mathcal W(\mu_1)-\frac{\lambda}{2}t(1-t)\bigl(W_2^2(\mu_0,\mu_1)-|m(\mu_1)-m(\mu_0)|^2\bigr).\] Consequently, convex kernels give displacement-convex interaction energies. If the endpoints have the same barycenter, the last factor equals \(W_2^2(\mu_0,mu_1)\), giving \(\lambda\)-geodesic convexity on that class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex interaction kernels yield displacement-convex energies; a lambda modulus is retained after removing the translation mode, notably on fixed-barycenter measures.
knowledge_statements.title: Interaction-Energy Convexity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-barycenter refinement is plausible and the property kind fits, but the precise modulus formula needs an authoritative locator. The final Wasserstein distance contains malformed \mu notation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Piecewise Convexity Criterion for One-Dimensional Interaction Energies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient displacement-convexity condition on an interval, requiring convexity separately on the two coordinate-order regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega=(a,b)\), \(\Delta^+=\{(x,y)\in\Omega\times\Omega:y\ge x\}\), and \(\Delta^-=\{(x,y)\in\Omega\times\Omega:y\le x\}\). If \(W\) restricted to each of \(\Delta^+\) and \(\Delta^-\) is convex, then \(\mathcal W\) is displacement convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an interval, convexity of the interaction kernel separately above and below the diagonal is sufficient for displacement convexity of the interaction energy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal W\text{ is displacement convex}.

children.title: Coupled-Energy Convexity
children.top_down_role: Convexity behavior for energies combining potential and interaction components.

assumptions_latex: \(V\) is \(\lambda_V\)-convex and \(W\) is even, lower semicontinuous, and \(\lambda_W\)-convex.
\(\mathcal E=\mathcal V+mathcal W\) is proper on \(\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On a fixed-barycenter class, \(\mathcal E\) is \((\lambda_V+lambda_W)\)-geodesically convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive potential-interaction energies on fixed-barycenter Wasserstein classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For endpoints \(\mu_0,mu_1\) having the same barycenter and any associated constant-speed Wasserstein geodesic \((\mu_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\), the component inequalities imply \[\mathcal E(mu_t)\le(1-t)\mathcal E(mu_0)+t\mathcal E(mu_1)-\frac{lambda_V+lambda_W}{2}t(1-t)W_2^2(mu_0,mu_1).\] Hence the coupled energy is displacement convex when \(\lambda_V+lambda_W\ge0\), strictly convex along nonconstant geodesics when the sum is positive, and may lose convexity when the negative component dominates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Potential and interaction convexity moduli add on fixed-barycenter classes, determining convex, strictly convex, or nonconvex coupled-energy regimes.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled-Energy Convexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Adding the component convexity moduli is plausible and fits this property container, but it is uncited. Multiple formulas contain missing backslashes, so the displayed mathematical statement is not currently reliable.

children.title: Uniqueness of Minimizers
children.top_down_role: Single-minimizer consequences of strict or quantified displacement convexity.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a geodesic metric space and \(\mathcal E:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper.
\(\mathcal E\) is strictly geodesically convex on its effective domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E\) has at most one minimizer.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: strict convexity along a geodesic joining two minimizers contradicts minimality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness from strict convexity along connecting geodesics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that for every distinct \(x_0,x_1\in D(mathcal E)\) there is a geodesic \((x_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\) satisfying \[\mathcal E(x_t)<(1-t)\mathcal E(x_0)+t\mathcal E(x_1)\qquad\text{for every }t\in(0,1).\] Then two distinct global minimizers cannot exist. In particular, any displacement-strictly-convex functional on a geodesically connected subset of \(\mathcal P_2\) has at most one minimizer there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper energy that is strictly convex along geodesics has at most one global minimizer on each geodesically connected domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness of Minimizers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role and uniqueness claim are standard under the stated connecting-geodesic hypothesis, but no authoritative source is supplied. Effective-domain notation is malformed in several fields.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness of Minimizers for Internal–Potential–Interaction Energies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness consequences of strict displacement convexity for an energy on absolutely continuous probability measures over Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For absolutely continuous probability measures \(\rho\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), define
\[
F(\rho)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}U(\rho(x))\,dx+\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}V(x)\,d\rho(x)+\frac12\iint_{\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n}W(x-y)\,d\rho(x)\,d\rho(y).
\]
Assume that \(U\) satisfies condition \((5.17)\), \(\inf_{\mathbb{R}^n}V> -\infty\), and \(V\) and \(W\) are convex. If \(V\) is strictly convex, then \(F\) has at most one minimizer. Respectively, if \(W\) is strictly convex, then \(F\) has at most one minimizer, possibly up to translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the sum of internal, potential, and pairwise interaction energies on absolutely continuous probability measures, under the stated internal-energy condition, lower bound on the potential, and convexity assumptions, strict convexity of the potential yields at most one minimizer. Strict convexity of the interaction yields at most one minimizer up to the possible translation ambiguity.
assumptions_latex: V\text{ is strictly convex, or respectively }W\text{ is strictly convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V\text{ strictly convex}\Rightarrow F\text{ has at most one minimizer};\qquad W\text{ strictly convex}\Rightarrow F\text{ has at most one minimizer up to possible translation}.

children.title: Stability of Minimizers
children.top_down_role: Dependence of minimizing measures on perturbations of data or energies.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a proper metric space and \(\mathcal E_n,mathcal E:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(\mathcal E_n\) Γ-converges to \(\mathcal E\) with respect to \(d\), and \((\mathcal E_n)\) is equicoercive.
Each \(x_n\) minimizes \(\mathcal E_n\), while \(\mathcal E\) has a unique minimizer \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_n\to x_*\) and \(\min_X\mathcal E_n	o\min_X\mathcal E\).

notation.meaning: Unique minimizer of the limit energy.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fundamental theorem of equicoercive Gamma-convergence plus uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential stability under metric Γ-convergence and equicoercivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every sequence of minimizers \((x_n)\) is relatively compact, every cluster point minimizes \(\mathcal E\), and the minimum values satisfy \[\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathcal E_n(x_n)=\min_{x\in X}mathcal E(x).\] Since \(\mathcal E\) has the unique minimizer \(x_*\), the whole sequence converges: \(d(x_n,x_*)\to0\). Applied with \(d=W_2\), this gives Wasserstein stability of minimizers under equicoercive Γ-convergent energy perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equicoercive Γ-convergence carries minimizers to the unique minimizer of the limit energy and carries minimum values to the limiting minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Stability of Minimizers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the stability container, but its compactness and minimum-value conclusions depend on the exact definitions of equicoercivity and metric Γ-convergence. No source is supplied, and several occurrences of \mathcal E are malformed.

children.title: Quantitative Minimizer Control
children.top_down_role: Distance control for minimizers derived from strengthened convexity.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is geodesic and \(\mathcal E:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and \(\lambda\)-geodesically convex for \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^2(x,x_*)\le \frac{2}{\lambda}(\mathcal E(x)-\mathcal E(x_*))\) for every \(x\in D(\mathcal E)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive geodesic convexity yields quadratic growth at a minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic growth and distance control for positively geodesically convex energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a geodesic \((x_t)_{t\in[0,1]}\) from \(x_*\) to \(x\), \(\lambda\)-geodesic convexity and minimality imply \[\mathcal E(x)-\mathcal E(x_*)\ge\frac{\lambda}{2}d^2(x,x_*).\] Consequently \(x_*\) is unique, and every \(\varepsilon\)-minimizer satisfying \(\mathcal E(x)\le\u0000mathcal E(x_*)+varepsilon\) obeys \(d(x,x_*)\le\u0000sqrt{2\varepsilon/lambda}\). For \(X=mathcal P_2\), the metric is \(W_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive geodesic convexity converts energy excess into a sharp square-distance bound and confines every epsilon-minimizer near the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative Minimizer Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic-growth property and constant are plausible for positive geodesic convexity, and the content kind fits. The statement nevertheless has embedded null characters and missing commands in its epsilon-minimizer formula, while providing no citation.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is geodesic and \(\mathcal E:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\lambda\)-geodesically convex for \(\lambda>0\).
\(x_*\) minimizes \(\mathcal E\), and \(|\partial\mathcal E|\) denotes its descending metric slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Energy excess, distance to equilibrium, and metric slope satisfy quadratic functional inequalities.

notation.meaning: Descending metric slope of the energy.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: lambda-geodesic convexity yields metric slope and transport-energy inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric analogues of gradient-domination and transport-energy inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in D(mathcal E)\), positive geodesic convexity yields \[\mathcal E(x)-\mathcal E(x_*)\le\frac{1}{2\lambda}|\partial\mathcal E|^2(x),\qquad d^2(x,x_*)\le\frac{2}{\lambda}igl(mathcal E(x)-\mathcal E(x_*)\bigr).\] Hence \(d(x,x_*)\le|partial\mathcal E|(x)/\lambda\). In Wasserstein applications these inequalities connect displacement convexity to entropy-production, logarithmic-Sobolev-type, and transport-entropy estimates once the energy and its slope are identified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive displacement convexity links energy excess, Wasserstein distance to equilibrium, and squared metric slope through functional inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Functional-Inequality Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A principle is suitable for this interface topic, but the slope inequality requires a source confirming the precise metric-space hypotheses and slope convention. Several commands in the displayed formulas are malformed.

assumptions_latex: \(d\ge1\) and \(\mathcal E(mu)=int_{mathbb R^d}-|x|^2\,d\u0000mu(x)\) on \(\mathcal P_2(mathbb R^d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal E\) is not displacement convex.

notation.meaning: Dirac probability measure at a point.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Dirac displacement interpolations reduce potential-energy convexity to ordinary convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure caused by a concave external potential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose distinct \(x_0,x_1\in\u0000mathbb R^d\) and the Wasserstein geodesic \(\mu_t=delta_{(1-t)x_0+tx_1}\) between \(\delta_{x_0}\) and \(\delta_{x_1}\). Then \[\mathcal E(mu_t)=-|(1-t)x_0+tx_1|^2>(1-t)(-|x_0|^2)+t(-|x_1|^2)\] for every \(t\in(0,1)\). Thus displacement convexity already fails on Dirac measures when the underlying potential is nonconvex; no regularity of the transported measures repairs this failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The negative quadratic potential produces a concave energy even along geodesics of Dirac measures, so displacement convexity fails.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Displacement Convexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative-quadratic example correctly targets failure of displacement convexity, and counterexample is the appropriate role. However, the record has embedded null characters, extensively malformed notation, and no inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Superdifferentiability Estimate for Powered Wasserstein Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling-dependent first-order upper expansion with explicit remainder bounds in the regimes above and below p=2.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let X be a Hilbert space, 1<p<\infty, \mu^1,\mu^2\in\mathcal P_p(X), \boldsymbol\mu^{12}\in\Gamma_o(\mu^1,\mu^2), and let \psi be defined as in (10.2.7). For every \mu^3\in\mathcal P_p(X) and \boldsymbol\mu\in\Gamma(\boldsymbol\mu^{12},\mu^3), set d=W_{p,\boldsymbol\mu}(\mu^1,\mu^3). Then
\[\psi(\mu^3)-\psi(\mu^1)+\int_{X^3}\langle j_p(x_2-x_1),x_3-x_1\rangle\,d\boldsymbol\mu\le R_p(d),\]
where
\[R_p(d)=\begin{cases}(p-1)d^2\bigl(W_p(\mu^1,\mu^2)+d\bigr)^{p-2},&p\ge2,\\ \dfrac{2^{2-p}}{p-1}d^p,&1<p\le2.\end{cases}\]
Consequently,
\[\limsup_{\substack{W_{p,\boldsymbol\mu}(\mu^3,\mu^1)\to0\\ \boldsymbol\mu\in\Gamma(\boldsymbol\mu^{12},\mu^3)}}\frac{\psi(\mu^3)-\psi(\mu^1)+\int_{X^3}\langle j_p(x_2-x_1),x_3-x_1\rangle\,d\boldsymbol\mu}{W_{p,\boldsymbol\mu}(\mu^3,\mu^1)}\le0.\]
If \boldsymbol\mu\in\Gamma_o(\boldsymbol\mu^{12},\mu^3), the coupled distance in these formulas may be replaced by W_p(\mu^1,\mu^3).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal plan from the base measure to the target yields a coupling-dependent first-order upper expansion of the powered Wasserstein distance, with an explicit quadratic remainder for p at least 2 and an order-p remainder for p at most 2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \psi(\mu^3)-\psi(\mu^1)+\int_{X^3}\langle j_p(x_2-x_1),x_3-x_1\rangle\,d\boldsymbol\mu\le R_p\bigl(W_{p,\boldsymbol\mu}(\mu^1,\mu^3)\bigr),\quad\limsup\frac{\psi(\mu^3)-\psi(\mu^1)+\int\langle j_p(x_2-x_1),x_3-x_1\rangle\,d\boldsymbol\mu}{W_{p,\boldsymbol\mu}(\mu^3,\mu^1)}\le0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subdifferentiability under a Unique Map-Induced Optimal Plan
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order lower expansion at a base measure whose optimal plan to the fixed target is unique and induced by a map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let X be a Hilbert space, 1<p<\infty, and \mu^1,\mu^2\in\mathcal P_p(X). Suppose
\[\Gamma_o(\mu^1,\mu^2)=\{\mu^{1\mid2}\},\qquad \mu^{1\mid2}=(i\times r)_\#\mu^1.\]
For \psi(\mu)=\frac1pW_p^p(\mu,\mu^2),
\[\liminf_{\substack{W_p(\mu^1,\mu^3)\to0\\ \boldsymbol\mu\in\Gamma_o(\mu^1,\mu^3)}}\frac{\psi(\mu^3)-\psi(\mu^1)+\int_{X^2}\langle j_p(r(x_1)-x_1),x_3-x_1\rangle\,d\boldsymbol\mu}{W_p(\mu^3,\mu^1)}\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the optimal plan from the base measure to the target is unique and induced by a transport map, that map determines a subgradient-type first-order lower expansion of the powered Wasserstein distance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Slope and minimal subdifferential characterization of the relaxed internal energy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the finite-slope implication, equality for regular measures, and the absolutely continuous converse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:[0,+\infty)\to\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable and satisfy (10.4.15), (10.4.21), and (10.4.23). Suppose \(\mu=\rho\mathcal L^d+\mu_s\in\mathcal P_p(\mathbb R^d)\), \(\mu_s\perp\mathcal L^d\), and \(|\partial\mathcal F^*|(\mu)<+\infty\). Then \(L_F(\rho)\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^d)\) and \(\nabla L_F(\rho)=\mathbf w\rho\) for some \(\mathbf w\in L^q(\rho\mathcal L^d;\mathbb R^d)\), with \[\left(\int_{\mathbb R^d}|\mathbf w|^q\rho\,dx\right)^{1/q}\le |\partial\mathcal F^*|(\mu).\] If \(\mu\in\mathcal P_p^r(\mathbb R^d)\), equality holds and \(\mathbf w=\partial^\circ\mathcal F^*(\mu)\). Conversely, if \(\mu=\rho\mathcal L^d\), \(L_F(\rho)\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,1}(\mathbb R^d)\), and \(\nabla L_F(\rho)=\mathbf w\rho\) for some \(\mathbf w\in L^q(\mu;\mathbb R^d)\), then \(\mathcal F^*\) has finite slope at \(\mu\) and \(\mathbf w=\partial^\circ\mathcal F^*(\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite slope gives a weak pressure gradient represented by an Lq vector field whose norm is bounded by the slope. For regular measures the norm equals the slope and the field is the minimal subdifferential. Conversely, the stated pressure-gradient representation for an absolutely continuous measure gives finite slope and identifies the minimal subdifferential.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is convex and differentiable and satisfies (10.4.15), (10.4.21), and (10.4.23)}
\text{For the converse: }\mu=\rho\mathcal L^d,\ L_F(\rho)\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,1},\ \nabla L_F(\rho)=\mathbf w\rho,\ \mathbf w\in L^q(\mu)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differentiability of Powered Wasserstein Distance at Regular Measures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order differentiability expressed using optimal transport maps from a regular base measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let X be a Hilbert space, 1<p<\infty, and \mu^1\in\mathcal P_p^r(X). For every \mu^2\in\mathcal P_p(X), define \psi(\mu)=\frac1pW_p^p(\mu,\mu^2). Then
\[\lim_{\mu^3\to\mu^1}\frac{\psi(\mu^3)-\psi(\mu^1)+\int_X\left\langle j_p\bigl(t_{\mu^1}^{\mu^2}(x)-x\bigr),t_{\mu^1}^{\mu^3}(x)-x\right\rangle\,d\mu^1(x)}{W_p(\mu^3,\mu^1)}=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular base measure, the powered Wasserstein distance to any fixed target has a first-order expansion determined by the optimal transport maps from the base measure to the target and to the perturbing measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{\mu^3\to\mu^1}\frac{\psi(\mu^3)-\psi(\mu^1)+\int_X\langle j_p(t_{\mu^1}^{\mu^2}(x)-x),t_{\mu^1}^{\mu^3}(x)-x\rangle\,d\mu^1(x)}{W_p(\mu^3,\mu^1)}=0

children.title: Local Slopes
children.top_down_role: Descending behavior measured through nearby Wasserstein perturbations.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space and \(\phi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local descending slope is the asymptotic maximal rate of decrease of \(\phi\) near \(x\).

notation.meaning: Positive part of a real number.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard strong local slope in metric variational analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong descending slope for an extended-real functional on a metric space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\u0000in D(phi)\), define \[|\partial\phi|(x):=limsup_{\substack{y\to x\\y\ne x}}\frac{(phi(x)-phi(y))^+}{d(x,y)}.\] If \(x\notin D(phi)\), set \(|\partial\phi|(x)=+infty\); if \(x\) is isolated in \(D(phi)\), set \(|\partial\phi|(x)=0\). The definition measures only descending variations and depends solely on arbitrarily small metric neighborhoods of \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local slope is the largest asymptotic decrease of a functional per unit metric displacement near a point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the local-slope container, including the isolated-point convention, but no authoritative definition is cited. Null characters and missing commands make the current formula invalid.

children.title: Relaxed Slopes
children.top_down_role: Lower-semicontinuous slope envelopes under measure and energy approximation.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space and \(\phi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxed slope is the sequential lower-semicontinuous envelope of the local slope under joint state-energy convergence.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard relaxed-slope envelope used in metric gradient-flow theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential relaxation retaining convergence of both states and energies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\u0000in D(phi)\), define \[|\partial^-phi|(x):=inf\left\{\liminf_{n\to\infty}|\partial\phi|(x_n):x_n\to x,\phi(x_n)\to\phi(x)\right\}.\] Set \(|\partial^-phi|(x)=+infty\) for \(x\notin D(phi)\). This relaxation permits approximation by nearby finite-energy states while preventing an energy jump from artificially lowering the slope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The relaxed slope is the lower-semicontinuous envelope of local slopes along sequences converging in both state and energy.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Slopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits, but relaxed-slope conventions differ on whether state convergence, energy convergence, or bounded energy is required. An authoritative locator is necessary, and the displayed notation is malformed.

children.title: Global Slopes
children.top_down_role: Slope quantities controlled through comparisons with arbitrary measures.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space and \(\phi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper.
\(\lambda\inmathbb R\) is the selected geodesic-convexity parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The global \(\lambda\)-slope compares \(x\) with every competing state.

notation.meaning: Global descending slope adjusted by the convexity modulus.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard global lambda-slope associated with geodesically convex functionals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global comparison slope adapted to a prescribed convexity modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\u0000in D(phi)\), define \[\mathfrak L_lambda[\phi](x):=sup_{\substack{y\in D(phi)\\y\ne x}}\left(\frac{phi(x)-phi(y)}{d(x,y)}+\frac{lambda}{2}d(x,y)\right)^+.\] Set \(\mathfrak L_lambda[\phi](x)=+infty\) outside \(D(phi)\). Unlike the local slope, this quantity tests all finite-energy competitors and incorporates the quadratic correction dictated by \(\lambda\)-geodesic convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global lambda-slope takes the worst energy decrease per distance over all competitors, with the correction required by lambda-convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Slopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global comparison formula is plausible and definition is the correct role, but its sign and normalization convention require a cited source. The current record also contains null characters and missing LaTeX commands.

children.title: Slope Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Relations among local, relaxed, and global slope constructions.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a geodesic metric space and \(\phi:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxed, local, and global \(\lambda\)-slopes coincide on \(D(phi)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: geodesic lambda-convexity globalizes the local slope and ensures its appropriate lower semicontinuity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coincidence theorem under lower semicontinuity and geodesic convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\u0000in D(phi)\), \(\lambda\)-geodesic convexity yields the descending-slope representation \[|\partial^-phi|(x)=|\partial\phi|(x)=mathfrak L_\lambda[\phi](x)=sup_{y\ne x}\left(\frac{phi(x)-phi(y)}{d(x,y)}+\frac{lambda}{2}d(x,y)\right)^+.\] Without the convexity hypothesis, relaxation can strictly decrease the local slope and distant competitors can make the global slope strictly larger.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For lower-semicontinuous lambda-geodesically convex energies, relaxed, local, and global lambda-slopes agree; without convexity, the inequalities may be strict.
knowledge_statements.title: Slope Hierarchy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hierarchy property fits the container, but coincidence with the relaxed slope depends on the precise relaxation convention and metric convexity hypotheses. No source is cited, and the displayed identity contains null characters and malformed commands.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Slope and Minimal Subdifferential of a Relative Internal Energy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes finite slope and the minimal Wasserstein subdifferential of \(\mathcal F(\cdot\mid\gamma)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu=\sigma\gamma\in D(\mathcal F)\). Then \(|\partial\mathcal F|(\mu)<\infty\) if and only if \(L_F(\sigma)\in W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)\) and \(\nabla L_F(\sigma)=\sigma\mathbf w\) for some \(\mathbf w\in L^q(\mu;\mathbb R^d)\). In that case, \(\|\mathbf w\|_{L^q(\mu)}=|\partial\mathcal F|(\mu)\) and \(\mathbf w=\partial^\circ\mathcal F(\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a measure with density sigma relative to gamma, the relative internal energy has finite metric slope exactly when the pressure transform has a local weak gradient equal to sigma times an Lq vector field. That vector field is the minimal subdifferential and its Lq norm equals the slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\partial\mathcal F|(\mu)<\infty\iff \exists\mathbf w\in L^q(\mu;\mathbb R^d):\ L_F(\sigma)\in W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega),\ \nabla L_F(\sigma)=\sigma\mathbf w;\quad \|\mathbf w\|_{L^q(\mu)}=|\partial\mathcal F|(\mu),\ \mathbf w=\partial^\circ\mathcal F(\mu).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Histogram derivatives of the entropically regularized transport loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint sensitivity with respect to the two input histograms, including the unregularized boundary case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\varepsilon>0\), the map \((\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\mapsto L_{\mathbf C}^{\varepsilon}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\) is convex and differentiable, with \(\nabla L_{\mathbf C}^{\varepsilon}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)\), where \((\mathbf f,\mathbf g)\) is the unique solution of the associated regularized optimal-transport dual system normalized by \(\sum_i f_i=\sum_j g_j=0\). For \(\varepsilon=0\), such dual-potential pairs are subgradients; the loss is differentiable when the normalized pair is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With positive entropic regularization, the transport loss is jointly convex and differentiable in its input histograms, and its gradient is the uniquely normalized pair of optimal dual potentials. Without regularization, optimal normalized dual potentials give subgradients, and uniqueness yields differentiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla L_{\mathbf C}^{\varepsilon}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=(\mathbf f,\mathbf g);\quad \varepsilon=0\Rightarrow(\mathbf f,\mathbf g)\in\partial L_{\mathbf C}^{0}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b),\text{ with differentiability under uniqueness.}

children.title: Strong Subdifferentials
children.top_down_role: First-order transport support expressed through strong remainder control.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E:\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and \(\mathcal E(\mu)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\xi\in\partial_{m s}\mathcal E(\mu)\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic Wasserstein space over Euclidean space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uniform first-order support under arbitrary near-diagonal transport plans is a standard strong Wasserstein subdifferential convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the coupling-uniform Euclidean strong-subdifferential convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A field \(\xi\) is a strong Wasserstein subgradient of \(\mathcal E\) at \(\mu\) if, for every \(\nu\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)\) and every \(\gamma\in\Gamma(\mu,\nu)\),
\[
\mathcal E(\nu)-\mathcal E(\mu)\geq
\int_{\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d}\langle\xi(x),y-x\rangle\,d\gamma(x,y)
+o\!\left(\left(\int|y-x|^2\,d\gamma\right)^{1/2}\right),
\]
where the remainder divided by the displayed transport displacement tends to zero uniformly as that displacement tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strong subgradient supports the energy to first order uniformly along every sufficiently small transport coupling.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Subdifferentials

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Strong Subdifferentials container and is internally coherent, but no inspectable citation supports this particular coupling-uniform convention or its uniform little-o remainder.

children.title: Extended Subdifferentials
children.top_down_role: Generalized cotangent objects accommodating broader transport couplings.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E:\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and \(\mathcal E(\mu)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\xi\in\partial\mathcal E(\mu)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: optimal-plan first-order support is the standard extended Wasserstein subdifferential formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses an optimal-plan, vector-field extended subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A field \(\xi\) belongs to the extended Wasserstein subdifferential of \(\mathcal E\) at \(\mu\) if, as \(\nu\to\mu\) in \(W_2\),
\[
\mathcal E(\nu)-\mathcal E(\mu)
\geq \inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma_o(\mu,\nu)}
\int_{\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d}
\langle\xi(x),y-x\rangle\,d\gamma(x,y)
+o\bigl(W_2(\mu,\nu)\bigr).
\]
The remainder is scalar and its quotient by \(W_2(\mu,\nu)\) tends to zero whenever \(0<W_2(\mu,\nu)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended subgradient gives a first-order lower support inequality evaluated through optimal transport plans.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended Subdifferentials

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical role is correctly a definition, but terminology for extended Wasserstein subdifferentials varies, especially between vector-field and plan-valued formulations. An authoritative source must confirm the optimal-plan infimum convention used here.

children.title: Plan Subdifferentials
children.top_down_role: Subdifferential information encoded by transport plans rather than vector fields.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E:\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and finite at \(\mu\).
\(\boldsymbol\alpha\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d)\) has first marginal \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\boldsymbol\alpha\in\boldsymbol\partial\mathcal E(\mu)\).

notation.meaning: Plan whose coordinates represent position and generalized velocity
Admissible triple plans with prescribed position-velocity marginal and optimal position-target marginal

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: triple-plan pairing is the standard relaxation of vector-field Wasserstein subgradients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Plan-valued relaxation allowing nondeterministic generalized velocities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\mathfrak C_o(\boldsymbol\alpha,\nu)\) as the set of probability measures \(\Theta\) on triples \((x,v,y)\) such that \((x,v)_\#\Theta=\boldsymbol\alpha\) and \((x,y)_\#\Theta\in\Gamma_o(\mu,\nu)\). The plan \(\boldsymbol\alpha\) is a plan subgradient when, as \(\nu\to\mu\) in \(W_2\),
\[
\mathcal E(\nu)-\mathcal E(\mu)
\geq\inf_{\Theta\in\mathfrak C_o(\boldsymbol\alpha,\nu)}
\int\langle v,y-x\rangle\,d\Theta(x,v,y)
+o\bigl(W_2(\mu,\nu)\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A plan subgradient replaces a velocity field by a position-velocity distribution and pairs it with optimal displacement through compatible triple plans.
