children.title: Problem-Size Scaling Limits
children.top_down_role: Computational boundaries arising as discrete instances grow.

assumptions_latex: The cost matrix \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) is supplied explicitly with arbitrary entries.
Arithmetic and random access to one machine-word entry each have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact solution requires \(\Omega(mn)\) input inspections in the worst case, while explicit dense-plan output requires \(\Omega(mn)\) writes.

notation.meaning: Numbers of source and target atoms.
Number of positive entries in an output coupling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information and output-size limits for explicitly represented discrete transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the explicit-input RAM model, an algorithm solving arbitrary exact discrete transport instances must inspect \(\Omega(mn)\) cost entries in the worst case: an uninspected entry can be altered so that it changes the optimum. Writing a dense coupling likewise costs \(\Omega(mn)\). A sparse optimizer can instead be represented by \(s\le m+n-1\) weighted index pairs, requiring \(O(m+n)\) output words, but this sparsity does not remove the \(\Omega(mn)\) cost-input barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary dense costs impose a worst-case mn input barrier. Sparse optimal plans reduce output size to linear, whereas explicitly writing a dense plan remains quadratic.
knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Size Scaling Limits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits, but the adversarial input-inspection lower bound requires a precisely defined solution/output model and a supporting complexity source. The supplied inventory does not support this transport-specific claim.

children.title: Degeneracy-Induced Scaling Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Performance degradation caused by degenerate sparse structures.

assumptions_latex: A transportation linear program is solved by a basis-pivoting method.
Degenerate basic feasible solutions and nonunique optima are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No positive lower bound on objective decrease per pivot, and hence no progress-based iteration bound, follows without additional safeguards.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degenerate transportation-simplex behavior, not a universal lower bound for all algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a degenerate transport vertex, fewer than \(m+n-1\) variables are positive although a basis contains \(m+n-1\) arcs. A pivot can then have zero step length, so \(\pi^{k+1}=\pi^k\) and \(\Delta J=0\); with tied reduced costs, distinct bases may also represent the same optimizer. Thus objective decrease cannot certify per-pivot progress. For example, equal two-point marginals with \(C=0\) admit degenerate optimal bases and zero objective change. Anti-cycling rules ensure termination but do not create a strictly positive objective decrease at every pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerate transport bases permit zero-length, zero-improvement pivots. Therefore objective decrease alone cannot yield an iteration bound, even when anti-cycling ensures eventual termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Induced Scaling Bottlenecks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and zero-length degenerate pivots are plausible, but a transportation-simplex source and a specified pivot/basis convention are needed to support the example and termination qualification.

children.title: Laguerre Cell Construction
children.top_down_role: Geometric construction of weighted transport cells.

knowledge_statements.title: Laguerre Cell Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additively weighted cells for general semi-discrete transport costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\), the Laguerre cell of \(y_i\) at weight \(\psi\) is
\[L_i(\psi)=\{x\in\Omega:c(x,y_i)-\psi_i\le c(x,y_j)-\psi_j\ \text{for every }j\}.\]
The cells cover \(\Omega\), and distinct cells intersect only on sets where two or more weighted scores tie. A measurable deterministic tie rule can form a disjoint measurable partition; when every tie set has source measure zero, this modification does not change any cell mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Laguerre cell contains points for which one site minimizes cost after subtraction of its weight. The cells cover the source domain, with overlaps occurring only at ties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cells \(L_i(\psi)\) cover \(\Omega\), with intersections confined to tie sets.

notation.meaning: Laguerre cell assigned to site i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lipschitz cost error under marginal meshing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers the mesh construction and the resulting first-order optimal-value error in the maximum mesh diameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact and let \(V_1,\ldots,V_\ell\) be mutually disjoint, bounded, convex cells with nonempty interiors whose union covers \(X\) and whose maximal diameter is \(h\). Choosing \(a_j\in V_j\), define \(\widehat\mu=\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\mu(V_j)\delta_{a_j}\). If each of \(N\) compactly supported marginals is discretized in this way and \(c\) is Lipschitz with constant \(L_c\), then product cells have diameter at most \(\sqrt N h\), and the induced optimal-cost error satisfies \(\Delta(c)=O(L_c\sqrt N h)\), hence \(O(L_c h)\) for fixed \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concentrating each mesh cell's mass at a point in that cell produces a finite marginal approximation. For N compactly supported marginals and a Lipschitz cost, the product-cell diameter is at most the square root of N times the mesh size, so the optimal transport cost error is linear in the mesh size up to a constant.
assumptions_latex: V_1,\ldots,V_\ell\ \text{are mutually disjoint, bounded, convex cells with nonempty interiors covering }X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{diam}(V_{j_1}\times\cdots\times V_{j_N})\le\sqrt N h,\qquad \Delta(c)=O(L_c\sqrt N h)

children.title: Cellwise Mass Integration
children.top_down_role: Evaluation of source mass over semi-discrete cells.

assumptions_latex: \(\mu=\rho(x)\,dx\) is a finite source measure on \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d\).
All Laguerre tie sets have \(\mu\)-measure zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cell mass is \(m_i(\psi)=\mu(L_i(\psi))=\int_{L_i(\psi)}\rho(x)\,dx\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cell-mass identity underlying numerical quadrature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the Laguerre partition induced by \(\psi\), the mass transported to site \(y_i\) is
\[m_i(\psi)=\mu(L_i(\psi))=\int_{L_i(\psi)}\rho(x)\,dx.\]
Because tie sets are \(\mu\)-null, the value is independent of the tie convention and \(\sum_{i=1}^N m_i(\psi)=\mu(\Omega)\). Any cellwise quadrature intended to evaluate the semi-discrete dual gradient must approximate these integrals consistently; exact integration yields the exact mass residuals \(b_i-m_i(\psi)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each target mass is the source density integrated over its Laguerre cell. Null tie sets make the result partition-independent, and all cell masses sum to total mass.
knowledge_statements.title: Cellwise Mass Integration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is precise and fits cellwise mass integration, but no cited source with a specific semi-discrete transport or cell-integration locator is provided.

children.title: Cellwise Moment Integration
children.top_down_role: Evaluation of geometric or cost moments over cells.

knowledge_statements.title: Cellwise Moment Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First moments and barycenters of Laguerre cells.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The vector first moment of a Laguerre cell is
\[q_i(\psi)=\int_{L_i(\psi)}x\,d\mu(x)=\int_{L_i(\psi)}x\rho(x)\,dx.\]
If \(m_i(\psi)>0\), its source barycenter is \(\bar x_i(\psi)=q_i(\psi)/m_i(\psi)\). Because the tie sets are \(\mu\)-null, summation gives \(\sum_i q_i(\psi)=\int_\Omega x\,d\mu(x)\). If \(m_i(\psi)=0\), then \(q_i(\psi)=0\), while the normalized barycenter is undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrating the position vector against the source measure over each Laguerre cell gives its first moment. Division by positive cell mass gives the barycenter; a zero-mass cell has no defined barycenter.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu=\rho(x)\,dx\) is a finite measure on \(\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) with finite first moment.
Each \(L_i(\psi)\) is measurable, and all Laguerre tie sets have \(\mu\)-measure zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The first cell moment is \(q_i(\psi)=\int_{L_i(\psi)}x\rho(x)\,dx\), and its barycenter is \(q_i(\psi)/m_i(\psi)\) when \(m_i(\psi)>0\).

notation.meaning: Vector-valued first moment of cell i.
Cell barycenter when its mass is positive.

children.title: Degenerate Cell Handling
children.top_down_role: Numerical treatment of empty, collapsing, or poorly resolved cells.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Cell Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe conventions for empty or zero-mass Laguerre cells.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cell is mass-degenerate when \(m_i(\psi)=\mu(L_i(\psi))=0\). Its unnormalized quantities then satisfy \(m_i(\psi)=0\) and \(q_i(\psi)=0\), but the quotient \(q_i(\psi)/m_i(\psi)\) is undefined and must not be evaluated. For the concave-dual convention \(\nabla\Phi(\psi)=b-m(\psi)\), the corresponding residual component is \(b_i\). Interface-based Newton systems can be singular in the presence of degenerate cells, so a method may require damping, regularization, or active-set handling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a zero-mass cell, retain zero mass and unnormalized moment but do not form its barycenter. Its dual residual remains the target mass, and second-order updates may need safeguards.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu\) is finite and has finite first moment, and \(m_i(\psi)=\mu(L_i(\psi))\) and \(q_i(\psi)=\int_{L_i(\psi)}x\,d\mu(x)\).
The semi-discrete concave dual uses target masses \(b_i\ge0\) and gradient convention \(\nabla\Phi(\psi)=b-m(\psi)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(m_i(\psi)=0\), then \(q_i(\psi)=0\), the barycenter is undefined, and the dual residual component is \(b_i-m_i(\psi)=b_i\).

notation.meaning: Mass and first moment of cell i.
Target mass assigned to site i.

assumptions_latex: Dual values and cell masses can be evaluated deterministically, and tie sets are \(\mu\)-null.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns \(\psi^k\) when \(\|b-m(\psi^k)\|\le\tau\), certifying the prescribed mass tolerance.

notation.meaning: Projection onto the zero-sum gauge subspace.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected deterministic gradient ascent for the semi-discrete concave dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\psi^0\in H\). At iteration \(k\), construct the Laguerre cells, compute \(m_i^k=\mu(L_i(\psi^k))\), and set \(g^k=b-m^k\). If \(\|g^k\|\le\tau\), stop and output \(\psi^k\). Otherwise choose \(\eta_k>0\) by a deterministic ascent line search and update
\[\psi^{k+1}=P_H(\psi^k+\eta_k g^k).\]
Here \(g^k=\nabla\Phi(\psi^k)\) under the null-tie assumption. The projection fixes the additive gauge without changing Laguerre cells.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly integrate deterministic Laguerre-cell masses and ascend by their target-mass residual, fixing the additive gauge. Stop when the residual norm meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Dual Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the topic and the gradient sign is internally consistent, but “deterministic ascent line search” is underspecified and no source establishes convergence or admissible line-search conditions. The stopping rule only certifies the computed residual tolerance.

assumptions_latex: Laguerre ties occur with probability zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update uses an unbiased dual-gradient estimator, and the weighted average \(\bar\psi^K\) is the algorithmic output.

notation.meaning: Winning Laguerre-cell index for sample x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected stochastic ascent for a sampled semi-discrete dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\psi^0\in H\). Given \(X_k\), select \(I_k=I_{\psi^k}(X_k)\) and form \(G_k=b-M e_{I_k}\). Then \(\mathbb E[G_k\mid\psi^k]=b-m(\psi^k)=\nabla\Phi(\psi^k)\). Update
\[\psi^{k+1}=P_H(\psi^k+\eta_kG_k).\]
After \(K\) iterations, output the weighted average \(\bar\psi^K=(\sum_{k<K}\eta_k\psi^k)/(\sum_{k<K}\eta_k)\), or stop earlier when an independently estimated mass residual satisfies the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a source point, assign it to its current Laguerre cell, and ascend with the resulting unbiased mass-residual estimate. Return a step-size-weighted average.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Dual Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The estimator is unbiased under the stated sampling model and the algorithm kind fits, but no source supports the stochastic scheme, averaging choice, or any convergence interpretation. A specific stochastic semi-discrete transport locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Discrete entropy and entropy-regularized transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the discrete entropy and regularized transport objective and records uniqueness on the finite entropy domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(H(P)=-\sum_{i,j}P_{ij}(\log P_{ij}-1)\), with the analogous vector definition and the extracted convention \(H(a)=-\infty\) if any coordinate is nonpositive. Wherever \(0<P_{ij}\leq1\), \(\nabla^2H(P)=-\operatorname{diag}(1/P_{ij})\), so \(H\) is \(1\)-strongly concave. For \(\varepsilon>0\), \[L_C^\varepsilon(a,b)=\min_{P\in U(a,b)}\bigl\{\langle P,C\rangle-\varepsilon H(P)\bigr\}.\] If the feasible set meets the finite entropy domain, the objective is \(\varepsilon\)-strongly convex and has a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discrete entropy is minus the sum of P_ij times log(P_ij) minus 1. On the positive probability domain it is 1-strongly concave. Consequently, when the transport polytope contains a finite-entropy coupling, adding minus epsilon times entropy produces an epsilon-strongly convex transport problem with a unique optimizer.
assumptions_latex: U(a,b)\text{ contains a coupling in the finite domain of }H
0<P_{ij}\leq1\text{ wherever the Hessian formula is used}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_C^\varepsilon(a,b)=\min_{P\in U(a,b)}\bigl(\langle P,C\rangle-\varepsilon H(P)\bigr)\text{ has a unique minimizer.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KL-divergence representation of discrete EOT
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents the discrete entropic transport problem as a left KL/Bregman projection of a fixed Gibbs tensor onto the prescribed-marginal coupling set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the finite discrete EOT setting with \(\varepsilon>0\), define the Gibbs tensor by
\[
\xi_r:=\exp\!\left(-\frac{C_r}{\varepsilon}\right).
\]
Then minimizing the EOT objective over \(\Pi(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N)\) is equivalent to
\[
\min_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N)}\operatorname{KL}(\gamma,\xi).
\]
Indeed, under the extended KL convention, \(\varepsilon\operatorname{KL}(\gamma,\xi)\) and \(\langle C,\gamma\rangle+\varepsilon H(\gamma)\) differ only by a term independent of \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive epsilon, exponentiating minus the cost divided by epsilon gives a fixed Gibbs tensor. Discrete entropically regularized transport is equivalently the minimization of KL divergence from the variable transport plan to this Gibbs tensor over all couplings with the prescribed marginals.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Discrete entropically regularized multi-marginal transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the finite discrete EOT objective, its extended-value entropy, and the boundary convention at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu_i\), \(i\in[N]\), be discrete marginals on finite sets of cardinalities \(\ell_i\), let \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell_1\times\cdots\times\ell_N}\), and let \(\varepsilon>0\). The entropically regularized transport problem is
\[
\min_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N)} F_\varepsilon[\gamma],\qquad F_\varepsilon[\gamma]=\langle C,\gamma\rangle+\varepsilon H(\gamma),
\]
where
\[
H(\gamma)=\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\sum_r\gamma_r(\log\gamma_r-1),&\gamma\geq0,\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
The convention is \(0\log0=0\); consequently, the right derivative at zero of \(t\mapsto t(\log t-1)\) is \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite discrete marginals, entropically regularized optimal transport minimizes transport cost plus epsilon times the extended negative entropy over the coupling set. The convention 0 log 0 = 0 is used, and the scalar entropy summand has right derivative minus infinity at zero.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a positive integer and each \(\mu_i\) is a discrete marginal on a finite set of cardinality \(\ell_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \min_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_N)}\{\langle C,\gamma\rangle+\varepsilon H(\gamma)\}\), where \(H(\gamma)=\sum_r\gamma_r(\log\gamma_r-1)\) for \(\gamma\geq0\), \(H(\gamma)=+\infty\) otherwise, and \(0\log0=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entropic transport as a KL projection of the Gibbs kernel
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents the entropy-regularized optimizer as a left-argument KL projection onto the prescribed-marginal coupling set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\operatorname{KL}(P\mid K)=\sum_{i,j}\left[P_{ij}\log\!\left(\frac{P_{ij}}{K_{ij}}\right)-P_{ij}+K_{ij}\right],\qquad K_{ij}=e^{-C_{ij}/\varepsilon}.\] For \(\varepsilon>0\), the entropy-regularized transport optimizer satisfies \[P_\varepsilon=\operatorname{Proj}^{\operatorname{KL}}_{U(a,b)}(K):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in U(a,b)}\operatorname{KL}(P\mid K).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the Gibbs kernel K_ij equal to exp(-C_ij/epsilon), the entropically regularized transport plan is the KL projection of K onto the set of couplings with marginals a and b.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_\varepsilon=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in U(a,b)}\operatorname{KL}(P\mid K).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite balanced transport regularized relative to the positive product measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), define
\[F_\varepsilon(\pi)=\langle C,\pi\rangle+\varepsilon\,\mathrm{KL}(\pi\|r),\qquad \pi\in\Pi(a,b).\]
Because \(r_{ij}>0\) and the scalar entropy integrand is strictly convex, \(F_\varepsilon\) is strictly convex on every nontrivial segment in \(\Pi(a,b)\). Since the transportation polytope is compact and nonempty, the regularized problem has exactly one minimizer \(\pi^\varepsilon\). On positive entries, the entropy curvature is \(\varepsilon/\pi_{ij}>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding positive relative-entropy regularization makes the finite transport objective strictly convex on the feasible polytope, selecting a unique optimal coupling.
knowledge_statements.title: Entropic Strict Convexification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict-convexity and uniqueness property is mathematically consistent for positive marginals and positive regularization, but no entropic-transport citation with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every entry satisfies \(\pi_{ij}^\varepsilon=a_i b_j\exp((f_i+g_j-C_{ij})/\varepsilon)>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gibbs representation and full support for finite positive marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist dual potentials \(f\) and \(g\), unique up to \((f,g)\mapsto(f+t\mathbf1,g-t\mathbf1)\), such that
\[\pi_{ij}^\varepsilon=a_i b_j\exp\!\left(\frac{f_i+g_j-C_{ij}}{\varepsilon}\right).\]
Equivalently, \(\pi^\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(u)K\operatorname{diag}(v)\) for positive scaling vectors \(u,v\) chosen to enforce the marginals. Hence every finite-cost pair receives strictly positive mass, replacing the sparse support of an unregularized vertex by a smooth full-support coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entropic optimizer is a diagonally scaled Gibbs kernel. With positive marginals and finite costs, every source-target pair receives positive mass.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Potential Smoothing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional log-sum-exp smoothing of the discrete dual transform.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each source index \(i\), the hard transform \(\min_j(C_{ij}-g_j)\) is replaced by \(T_{\varepsilon,i}(g)\). This function is concave and infinitely differentiable on \(\mathbb R^n\), with
\[\nabla T_{\varepsilon,i}(g)=-p_i(g),\qquad \nabla^2T_{\varepsilon,i}(g)=-\frac1\varepsilon\bigl(\operatorname{Diag}(p_i(g))-p_i(g)p_i(g)^{\mathsf T}\bigr).\]
Thus nondifferentiable selection among tied minimizers becomes Gibbs-weighted selection. The Hessian is negative semidefinite and annihilates \(\mathbf1\). Correspondingly, the transform is affine-equivariant under constant shifts: \(T_{\varepsilon,i}(g+t\mathbf1)=T_{\varepsilon,i}(g)-t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Entropy replaces the hard minimum over target potentials by a smooth log-sum-exp. Its gradient is a negative Gibbs assignment, its Hessian is a negative covariance, and constant potential shifts change the transform affinely.
assumptions_latex: All costs \(C_{ij}\) and potentials \(g_j\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The entropic transform is infinitely differentiable, with gradient \(-p_i(g)\) and Hessian \(-\varepsilon^{-1}(\operatorname{Diag}p_i-p_ip_i^{\mathsf T})\).

notation.meaning: Entropic soft minimum for source index i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual representation of entropically regularized discrete transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized dual-potential representation and the componentwise exponential correspondence between optimal potentials and transport scaling vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the standing discrete entropic-transport setting,
\[
\mathrm L_{\mathbf C}^{\varepsilon}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=\max_{\mathbf f\in\mathbb R^n,\,\mathbf g\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{\langle\mathbf f,\mathbf a\rangle+\langle\mathbf g,\mathbf b\rangle-\varepsilon\left\langle e^{\mathbf f/\varepsilon},\mathbf K e^{\mathbf g/\varepsilon}\right\rangle\right\}.
\]
For optimal dual potentials \((\mathbf f,\mathbf g)\), the corresponding scaling vectors satisfy
\[
(\mathbf u,\mathbf v)=\left(e^{\mathbf f/\varepsilon},e^{\mathbf g/\varepsilon}\right),
\]
where exponentiation is componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The entropically regularized discrete transport value has an unconstrained maximization representation in terms of dual potentials. Optimal potentials correspond to the transport scaling vectors through componentwise exponentiation by the inverse regularization parameter.

\mathbf K\text{ is the kernel associated with }\mathbf C\text{ and }\varepsilon\text{ in the standing entropic-transport setting}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the transport cost evaluated at an entropically regularized optimal coupling and the explicitly normalized, self-cost-corrected divergence used to remove its nonzero diagonal bias.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varepsilon>0\). For discrete probability measures \(\alpha,\beta\) with weights \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b\), suppose \(C_{ij}=d(x_i,x_j)^p\), \(\mathbf P^\star\) solves the entropically regularized transport problem, and \((\mathbf f^\star,\mathbf g^\star)\) are corresponding dual solutions. Define \(\mathfrak P_{\mathbf C}^{\varepsilon}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b):=\langle\mathbf P^\star,\mathbf C\rangle=\left\langle e^{\mathbf f^\star/\varepsilon},(\mathbf K\odot\mathbf C)e^{\mathbf g^\star/\varepsilon}\right\rangle\) and \(\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\beta)^p:=\mathfrak P_{\mathbf C}^{\varepsilon}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\). For general probability distributions, if \(\pi^\star\) is an entropically regularized optimal coupling, define \(\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\beta)^p:=\int_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal X}d(x,y)^p\,\mathrm d\pi^\star(x,y)\). Because generally \(\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\alpha)\neq0\), define \(\widetilde{\mathcal W}_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\beta)^p:=2\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\beta)^p-\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\alpha,\alpha)^p-\mathcal W_{p,\varepsilon}(\beta,\beta)^p\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sinkhorn Alternating Scaling Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded algorithm statement including the marginal equations, scaling gauge, and the extract's qualitative convergence assertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\mathbf P=\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf u)\mathbf K\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf v)\), the marginal constraints are
\[\mathbf u\odot(\mathbf K\mathbf v)=\mathbf a,\qquad \mathbf v\odot(\mathbf K^\top\mathbf u)=\mathbf b.\]
Beginning with a positive \(\mathbf v^{(0)}\), with \(\mathbf v^{(0)}=\mathbb 1_m\) as the displayed initialization, Sinkhorn's iteration is
\[\mathbf u^{(\ell+1)}=\frac{\mathbf a}{\mathbf K\mathbf v^{(\ell)}},\qquad \mathbf v^{(\ell+1)}=\frac{\mathbf b}{\mathbf K^\top\mathbf u^{(\ell+1)}},\]
where division is componentwise. The scaling representation is invariant under \((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\mapsto(\lambda\mathbf u,\mathbf v/\lambda)\) for \(\lambda>0\). Different positive initializations can yield different scaling representatives, but the iterations converge to representatives producing the same optimal coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sinkhorn's algorithm alternately rescales the kernel to impose its two prescribed marginals. The scaling vectors have a reciprocal scaling ambiguity, while the induced coupling is common at convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf P=\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf u)\mathbf K\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf v)\) is in \(\mathbf U(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)\).
The componentwise quotients in the iteration are well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The alternating updates enforce the two marginal equations successively, and their induced couplings converge to the same optimal coupling despite the gauge freedom in \((\mathbf u,\mathbf v)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hilbert-Metric Convergence and Residual Bounds for Sinkhorn Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded Sinkhorn convergence theorem using the strictly positive-kernel contraction setting inherited from its cited dependency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the positive-kernel contraction setting, the Sinkhorn scalings satisfy
\[(\mathbf u^{(\ell)},\mathbf v^{(\ell)})\to(\mathbf u^\star,\mathbf v^\star),\]
with
\[d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf u^{(\ell)},\mathbf u^\star)=O(\lambda(\mathbf K)^{2\ell}),\qquad d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf v^{(\ell)},\mathbf v^\star)=O(\lambda(\mathbf K)^{2\ell}).\]
For \(\mathbf P^{(\ell)}=\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf u^{(\ell)})\mathbf K\operatorname{diag}(\mathbf v^{(\ell)})\),
\[d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf u^{(\ell)},\mathbf u^\star)\leq\frac{d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf P^{(\ell)}\mathbb 1_m,\mathbf a)}{1-\lambda(\mathbf K)},\]
\[d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf v^{(\ell)},\mathbf v^\star)\leq\frac{d_{\mathcal H}((\mathbf P^{(\ell)})^\top\mathbb 1_n,\mathbf b)}{1-\lambda(\mathbf K)}.\]
If \(\mathbf P^\star\) is the unique regularized optimal coupling, then
\[\|\log(\mathbf P^{(\ell)})-\log(\mathbf P^\star)\|_\infty\leq d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf u^{(\ell)},\mathbf u^\star)+d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf v^{(\ell)},\mathbf v^\star).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sinkhorn's scaling vectors converge geometrically in Hilbert's projective metric. Their errors are bounded by marginal residuals and control the entrywise logarithmic error of the induced coupling.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf K\in\mathbb R_{+,*}^{n\times m}\) is in the positive-kernel setting of the preceding contraction theorem, with \(\lambda(\mathbf K)<1\).
\((\mathbf u^{(\ell)},\mathbf v^{(\ell)})\) are the Sinkhorn scaling iterates for marginals \((\mathbf a,�\mathbf b)\).
\(\mathbf P^\star\) is the unique solution of the regularized transport problem under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaling iterates converge at rate \(O(\lambda(\mathbf K)^{2\ell})\) in \(d_{\mathcal H}\), obey the displayed marginal-residual estimates, and satisfy the displayed logarithmic coupling-error bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hilbert-Metric Contraction of a Positive Kernel
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded contraction theorem used in Sinkhorn convergence analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf K\in\mathbb R_{+,*}^{n\times m}\). For all \(\mathbf v,\mathbf v'\in\mathbb R_{+,*}^m\),
\[d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf K\mathbf v,\mathbf K\mathbf v')\leq \lambda(\mathbf K)d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf v,\mathbf v'),\]
where
\[\eta(\mathbf K)=\max_{\substack{i,j\in\llbracket n\rrbracket\\k,r\in\llbracket m\rrbracket}}\frac{K_{ik}K_{jr}}{K_{jk}K_{ir}},\qquad \lambda(\mathbf K)=\frac{\sqrt{\eta(\mathbf K)}-1}{\sqrt{\eta(\mathbf K)}+1}<1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplication by a strictly positive matrix is a strict contraction in Hilbert's projective metric, with an explicit contraction factor determined by the largest cross-ratio of its entries.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf K\in\mathbb R_{+,*}^{n\times m}\) has strictly positive entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf K\mathbf v,\mathbf K\mathbf v')\leq\lambda(\mathbf K)d_{\mathcal H}(\mathbf v,\mathbf v')\) with \(\lambda(\mathbf K)<1\) as explicitly defined by the entrywise cross-ratio maximum.

knowledge_statements.title: Marginal-Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A computable summed-L1 feasibility certificate for nonnegative approximate transport plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the marginal-residual certificate by \[r(P)=\lVert P\mathbf 1-a\rVert_1+\lVert P^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1-b\rVert_1.\] Then \[r(P)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P\in\Pi(a,b).\] For \(\delta\geq0\), call \(P\) \(\delta\)-marginal-feasible when \(r(P)\leq\delta\). Thus the computable inequality \(r(P)\leq\delta\) certifies that the sum of the two marginal L1 discrepancies is at most \(\delta\); it does not by itself certify objective-value accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The summed L1 row- and column-marginal residual is zero exactly for feasible couplings; bounding it by delta directly certifies approximate marginal feasibility but not objective accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb{R}_+^{m\times n}\), and \(a\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\) have equal total mass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[r(P)=0\iff P\in\Pi(a,b),\qquad r(P)\leq\delta\iff P\text{ is }\delta\text{-marginal-feasible}.\]

notation.meaning: sum of the row- and column-marginal L1 residuals

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq \mathcal P_\varepsilon(P)-\mathcal D_\varepsilon(f,g)\leq\delta\) certifies \(\delta\)-optimality of \(P\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for a feasible discrete entropic transport plan and arbitrary dual potentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(U(a,b)=\{P\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}:P\mathbf1=a,\ P^\top\mathbf1=b\}\), \(\mathcal P_\varepsilon(P)=\langle C,P\rangle+\varepsilon\sum_{ij}P_{ij}(\log P_{ij}-1)\), and \(\mathcal D_\varepsilon(f,g)=\langle f,a\rangle+\langle g,b\rangle-\varepsilon\sum_{ij}\exp((f_i+g_j-C_{ij})/\varepsilon)\). For every \(P\in U(a,b)\) and \(f\in\mathbb R^m\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), weak duality gives \(\mathcal D_\varepsilon(f,g)\leq\mathcal P_\varepsilon^\star\leq\mathcal P_\varepsilon(P)\). Hence a computed gap at most \(\delta\) certifies that both displayed objectives are within \(\delta\) of the common optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible plan and dual potentials form a verifiable accuracy certificate when their entropic primal–dual objective gap is at most the requested tolerance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric iteration bound for strictly positive discrete kernels in projective distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v^t\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) be the scaling vector after \(t\) full row-and-column Sinkhorn iterations, and let \(v^\star\) denote the optimal scaling ray. If the induced scaling map is \(\tau\)-contractive in \(d_H\), then \(d_H(v^t,v^\star)\leq\tau^tD_0\), where \(D_0=d_H(v^0,v^\star)\). Therefore, for \(0<\delta<D_0\), the iteration count \(t\geq\lceil\log(D_0/\delta)/(-\log\tau)\rceil\) guarantees \(d_H(v^t,v^\star)\leq\delta\). The count treats one row update followed by one column update as one iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projective contraction by a factor τ yields a logarithmic iteration count in the inverse target error.

children.title: Per-Iteration Arithmetic Cost
children.top_down_role: Operation cost of a single scaling sweep.

assumptions_latex: Arithmetic operations and scalar elementary evaluations have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One full row-and-column scaling iteration costs \(\Theta(mn)\) arithmetic operations and uses \(O(m+n)\) auxiliary storage.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense serial arithmetic model without materializing a new transport matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(u\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\) and \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), a full Sinkhorn iteration computes one product \(Kv\), updates \(u=a\oslash(Kv)\), computes one product \(K^\top u\), and updates \(v=b\oslash(K^\top u)\), where \(\oslash\) denotes componentwise division. The two dense matrix-vector products require \(\Theta(mn)\) arithmetic operations; the componentwise updates require \(\Theta(m+n)\). Thus the full iteration costs \(\Theta(mn)\), with \(O(m+n)\) auxiliary storage when \(K\) is already stored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a dense m-by-n kernel, two matrix-vector products dominate each full Sinkhorn iteration, giving Θ(mn) arithmetic cost.

children.title: Total Arithmetic Complexity
children.top_down_role: Aggregate computational work across all scaling iterations.

assumptions_latex: The scaling map contracts projective error by \(\tau\in[0,1)\), from initial error \(D_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The arithmetic cost for projective error \(\delta\) is \(O\!\left(mn\log(D_0/\delta)/(-\log\tau)\right)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense serial total cost obtained by composing iteration count and per-iteration cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\delta<D_0\), take \(T=\lceil\log(D_0/\delta)/(-\log\tau)\rceil\) full iterations. Multiplying this iteration count by the \(\Theta(mn)\) cost of each dense row-and-column scaling step gives total arithmetic work \(O(mnT)\), equivalently \(O\!\left(mn\log(D_0/\delta)/(-\log\tau)\right)\). If \(\tau\) is bounded uniformly away from \(1\), this reduces to \(O(mn\log(D_0/\delta))\). Kernel construction and storage are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total dense arithmetic work equals the per-iteration Θ(mn) cost times the geometric-convergence iteration count.
