children.title: Shared-Marginal Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of common latent marginals across coupled scaling problems.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\pi_Y)_\#\gamma_1=\cdots=(\pi_Y)_\#\gamma_m\).

notation.meaning: Shared marginal on the common space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for couplings sharing their marginal on a common factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \((\gamma_k)_{k=1}^m\) is shared-marginal consistent if there exists \(b\in\mathcal P(Y)\) such that \((\pi_Y)_\#\gamma_k=b\) for every \(k\). Equivalently, all second marginals coincide. In a barycenter formulation where \(b\) is unknown, feasibility requires this common measure together with the prescribed conditions \((\pi_{X_k})_\#\gamma_k=a_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family of couplings is consistent when every coupling has the same marginal on the shared space while retaining its prescribed other marginal.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Marginal Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source with a specific locator supports this multi-coupling formulation.

children.title: Tensor-Scaling Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Storage or computation limits in explicit multi-marginal representations.

assumptions_latex: Each scaling sweep explicitly forms all \(m\) one-mode marginals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{sweep}}=\Theta\!\left(m\prod_{j=1}^m n_j\right)\) and \(M=\Theta\!\left(\prod_{j=1}^m n_j\right)\).

notation.meaning: Arithmetic time for one complete scaling sweep

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense-storage bottleneck for explicit multi-marginal tensor scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the unit-cost arithmetic model, an explicit dense pass over \(K\) costs \(\Theta(\prod_{j=1}^m n_j)\). Computing all \(m\) mode marginals separately therefore costs at most and, for generic dense data, at least \(\Theta(m\prod_{j=1}^m n_j)\) operations per sweep. Storing the kernel or coupling requires \(\Theta(\prod_{j=1}^m n_j)\) numbers. Avoiding these bounds requires exploitable structure, such as tensor factorization or an implicit contraction oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit tensor scaling has product-size memory and essentially product-size work per marginal, making the number of marginals and dimensions decisive bottlenecks.
knowledge_statements.title: Tensor-Scaling Bottlenecks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the bottleneck leaf, but the claimed tight per-sweep lower bound depends on the stipulated separate-marginal implementation and requires a specific supporting source.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\bigcap_{j=1}^q C_j\neq\varnothing\), where every \(C_j\) is closed and convex.
Each KL projection onto \(C_j\) is computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Return \(\gamma^{(t)}\) when \(\max_j d(\gamma^{(t)},C_j)\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Positive reference kernel viewed as a vector

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclic KL-projection form of constrained entropic coupling scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), initialize \(\gamma^{(0)}=K\). At iteration \(t\), choose \(j_t=1+(t\bmod q)\) and set \[\gamma^{(t+1)}=P_{C_{j_t}}^{\mathrm{KL}}(\gamma^{(t)})\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\eta\in C_{j_t}}\mathrm{KL}(\eta\mid\gamma^{(t)}).\] When simultaneous constraints require correction terms, use the corresponding Dykstra KL projection. Stop when every constraint-block residual is at most \(\varepsilon\), and output the last nonnegative coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from the Gibbs kernel, cyclically apply KL projections onto coupling-constraint blocks and stop when all block residuals meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained-Coupling Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Generic cyclic KL projections need not solve projection onto an intersection; the required Dykstra corrections and admissible constraint geometry are not specified. A source is needed to determine the correct constrained-scaling algorithm.

assumptions_latex: The spatial mesh consists of cells \(i\) with volumes \(V_i\) and oriented faces \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_i^k=0\) is the finite-volume continuity equation in every space-time cell.

notation.meaning: Cell-centered density at time layer k
Face flux at the intermediate time layer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-volume staggered placement for dynamic optimal transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Place \(\rho_i^k\) at spatial cell centers and integer time layers, and place the normal flux \(m_f^{k+1/2}\) on spatial faces and half-time layers. Define \[r_i^k=\frac{\rho_i^{k+1}-\rho_i^k}{\Delta t}+\frac{1}{V_i}\sum_{f\subset\partial i}s_{if}m_f^{k+1/2}.\] Boundary-face fluxes encode the prescribed boundary condition. Thus conservation is imposed locally by \(r_i^k=0\), while interpolation of adjacent densities supplies the face or half-time density used in the discrete kinetic action.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Densities occupy cell centers and integer times, while fluxes occupy faces and half-times; their incidence divergence produces a locally conservative continuity equation.
knowledge_statements.title: Staggered-Grid Discretizations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but the formula does not specify whether face fluxes are integrated over face area, and the grid/action interpolation conventions require a topic-specific source.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) and \(G\) are proper, closed, convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned iterate approximately minimizes \(F(z)+G(Az)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual proximal splitting for a convex dynamic-transport discretization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(\min_z F(z)+G(Az)\), choose \(z^0,y^0\), set \(\bar z^0=z^0\), and iterate \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma G^*}(y^k+\sigma A\bar z^k),\qquad z^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau F}(z^k-\tau A^*y^{k+1}),\] \[\bar z^{k+1}=z^{k+1}+\theta(z^{k+1}-z^k),\qquad \theta\in[0,1].\] Stop when prescribed primal and dual residuals are at most \(\varepsilon\); output \(z^{k+1}\) or its ergodic average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split the transport action from linear conservation constraints and alternate explicit primal and dual proximal updates until both optimality residuals are small.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Splitting Solvers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal-dual proximal scheme fits the solver leaf, but the spaces, proximal metrics, residual definitions, and precise convergence assumptions are not sourced or fully specified.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Return \(z^{k+1}\) when the primal and dual residuals do not exceed \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-of-multipliers form for equality-constrained dynamic transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(z^0\) and \(y^0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z\left\{J(z)+\langle y^k,Az-b\rangle+\frac{\beta}{2}\lVert Az-b\rVert^2\right\},\] then update \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\beta(Az^{k+1}-b).\] The inner minimization may itself be solved by separable proximal steps. Stop when \(\lVert Az^{k+1}-b\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) and the chosen dual-stationarity residual is at most \(\varepsilon\); output \(z^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalize the discrete continuity defect, minimize the augmented Lagrangian in the transport variables, then update its multiplier until feasibility and stationarity hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Solvers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The method-of-multipliers algorithm fits the leaf, but the dual-stationarity residual and conditions ensuring a well-defined inner minimizer and convergence require a specific source.

children.title: Discrete Continuity Residuals
children.top_down_role: Defects in the discretized continuity constraint.

assumptions_latex: \(\rho_i^k\) and \(m_f^{k+1/2}\) are defined on a finite-volume staggered grid.
Boundary fluxes are included among the oriented faces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact discrete continuity at cell \(i\) and step \(k\) is equivalent to \(r_i^k=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cellwise residual for a staggered finite-volume continuity equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For cell \(i\) and time step \(k\), the discrete continuity residual is \[r_i^k:=\frac{\rho_i^{k+1}-\rho_i^k}{\Delta t}+\frac{1}{V_i}\sum_{f\subset\partial i}s_{if}m_f^{k+1/2}.\] Its signed value measures local creation or loss of density per unit volume and time. A norm such as \(\lVert r\rVert_1\), \(\lVert r\rVert_2\), or \(\lVert r\rVert_\infty\) supplies a global stopping diagnostic only after the associated volume and time weights are specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The continuity residual is the discrete density increment plus the oriented finite-volume divergence of face fluxes; zero residual means exact local conservation.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Continuity Residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the residual leaf and is internally plausible, but the normalization of face fluxes and the finite-volume convention are not established by an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characteristic-flow representation of the continuity equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean measure-valued continuity equations under the cited regularity, growth, and integrability conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (\mu_t)_{t\in[0,T]} be narrowly continuous and solve \partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\!\cdot(v_t\mu_t)=0 on \mathbb{R}^d, where the Borel field v satisfies conditions (8.1.8) and (8.1.2). Then, for \mu_0-a.e. x, the characteristic system (8.1.9) has a solution X_t(x) on [0,T], and \mu_t=(X_t)_\#\mu_0 for every t\in[0,T]. If p>1 and \int_0^T\!\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|v_t(x)|^p\,d\mu_t(x)\,dt<\infty, then \lim_{h\downarrow0}\int_0^{T-h}\!\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\left|\frac{X_{t+h}(x)-X_t(x)}{h}-v_t(X_t(x))\right|^p d\mu_0(x)dt=0, and \frac{X_{t+h}(x,t)-x}{h}\to v_t(x) in L^p(\mu_t;\mathbb{R}^d) for \mathcal L^1\text{-a.e. }t\in(0,T).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A narrowly continuous solution of the continuity equation satisfying the stated vector-field hypotheses is the pushforward of its initial measure by globally defined characteristics. Under finite p-action with p greater than one, the characteristic difference quotients recover the velocity field in the stated Lp senses.
assumptions_latex: v\text{ is Borel and satisfies (8.1.8) and (8.1.2)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu_t=(X_t)_\#\mu_0\ \forall t\in[0,T],\quad \frac{X_{t+h}-X_t}{h}\to v_t\circ X_t\text{ in the stated space-time }L^p\text{ sense, with the corresponding }L^p(\mu_t)\text{ velocity recovery a.e. in }t.

children.title: Global Mass-Conservation Error
children.top_down_role: Net mass imbalance introduced by discretization or solver tolerance.

assumptions_latex: All physical boundary fluxes use the outward sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_n=\left|\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\Delta t\sum_iV_i r_i^k\right|\).

notation.meaning: Total discrete mass at time layer k
Total outward boundary flux during step k
Global mass-conservation error through step n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cumulative mass defect including prescribed boundary transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the global mass-conservation error through time layer \(n\) by \[E_n:=\left|M^n-M^0+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\Delta t\,\Phi^k\right|.\] Cancellation of every interior face contribution gives \[M^{k+1}-M^k+\Delta t\,\Phi^k=\Delta t\sum_iV_i r_i^k.\] Consequently, \(E_n\) equals the absolute accumulated volume-weighted continuity residual. For impermeable boundaries, \(\Phi^k=0\), so it reduces to \(|M^n-M^0|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global mass error is the change in total cell mass plus cumulative outward boundary flux, equivalently the accumulated volume-weighted continuity residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Mass-Conservation Error

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and the cancellation identity is plausible under integrated-face-flux conventions, but those conventions and the identity lack a supporting source.

children.title: Local Flux-Imbalance Error
children.top_down_role: Cellwise mismatch between temporal mass change and numerical flux.

assumptions_latex: Flux orientation is outward relative to cell \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_i^k=0\) if and only if cell \(i\) is locally conservative during step \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrated cellwise imbalance over one discrete time step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The signed local flux-imbalance error in cell \(i\) during step \(k\) is \[e_i^k:=V_i(\rho_i^{k+1}-\rho_i^k)+\Delta t\sum_{f\subset\partial i}s_{if}m_f^{k+1/2}=\Delta t\,V_i r_i^k.\] The absolute local error is \(|e_i^k|\). The first term is the cell's mass increment and the second is its integrated net outward flux, so their sum vanishes precisely under local discrete conservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local imbalance is a cell's mass change plus its integrated net outward flux; its absolute value measures the cellwise conservation defect.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Flux-Imbalance Error

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the local-error leaf, but dimensional correctness depends on whether each face variable denotes integrated flux rather than flux density; a specific discretization source is required.

children.title: Conservation-Error Propagation
children.top_down_role: Accumulation of local defects across time levels or solver iterations.

assumptions_latex: Interior face fluxes are single-valued with opposite incidence signs in adjacent cells.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_n\leq\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\Delta t\sum_iV_i|r_i^k|\).

notation.meaning: Global mass error through layer n
Volume-weighted residual magnitude at step k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic accumulation bound for finite-volume conservation defects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_k\) be the absolute global mass defect after step \(k\). Summing the discrete continuity equation over cells cancels interior fluxes and yields \[E_{k+1}\leq E_k+\Delta t\sum_iV_i|r_i^k|.\] Iteration gives \[E_n\leq E_0+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\Delta t\,R_k.\] In particular, if the initial mass is exact and \(R_k\leq\delta_k\), then \(E_n\leq\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\Delta t\,\delta_k\); systematic signed residuals may attain linear accumulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global mass error grows by at most the time-integrated, volume-weighted local residual, although consistently signed defects can accumulate linearly.
knowledge_statements.title: Conservation-Error Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the propagation leaf, but the displayed conclusion omits the initial term E_0 without assuming exact initial mass, while the statement includes it. The definition of stepwise E_k also needs alignment with the cumulative error and sourcing.

children.title: Multiscale Transport Solvers
children.top_down_role: Hierarchical transport solution across progressively refined resolutions.

assumptions_latex: A nested hierarchy of transport discretizations \(\mathcal G_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal G_L\) is available.
Restriction and prolongation preserve nonnegativity and total mass.
A convergent single-level solver is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Output the level-\(L\) coupling when its feasibility and optimality residuals are at most \(\varepsilon_L\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coarse-to-fine solver template for discrete optimal transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Restrict the marginals and cost to \(\mathcal G_0\), solve the coarse transport problem to tolerance \(\varepsilon_0\), and obtain \(\gamma_0\). For \(\ell=1,\\ldots,L\), prolongate \(\gamma_{\ell-1}\) to a nonnegative mass-preserving initialization on \(\mathcal G_\ell\), enlarge its active support using neighboring fine cells or reduced-cost tests, and run the single-level solver to tolerance \(\varepsilon_\ell\). Refine again if the active-set certificate or residual fails. Return the finest-level coupling and its residual diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve first on a coarse grid, prolongate the coupling and active support, refine where needed, and resolve successively to the finest tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiscale Transport Solvers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the active-support refinement and certificate are underspecified and unsourced. The iteration range also contains malformed LaTeX (`\\ldots` rather than `\ldots`).

children.title: Domain-Decomposition Transport
children.top_down_role: Transport solution through spatially partitioned subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The discrete coupling indices are covered by overlapping blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_q\).
Each local entropic subproblem has a computable minimizer.
Interface variables are reconciled after every sweep.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Return \(\gamma\) when global marginal and interface residuals are at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlapping-block domain decomposition for entropic discrete transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a positive coupling \(\gamma^0\). During sweep \(t\), for each block \(B_s\), minimize \(J_\varepsilon\) over the entries of \(\gamma\) in \(B_s\), holding exterior entries fixed and imposing the block's residual row, column, and interface mass constraints. Insert the local minimizer, then reconcile duplicated interface quantities by a conservative consensus or dual update. After all blocks, evaluate global marginal and interface residuals. Stop when both are at most \(\varepsilon\); otherwise repeat, using overlapping blocks to communicate corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve local entropic transport problems on overlapping coupling blocks, conservatively reconcile interfaces, and stop when global marginals and interfaces agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Decomposition Transport

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the local constraints, conservative consensus or dual update, and convergence conditions are not defined precisely enough to identify a reliable domain-decomposition method without a source.

children.title: Coarse-to-Fine Support Refinement
children.top_down_role: Progressive restriction or enrichment of candidate transport support.

assumptions_latex: The discrete measures are \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\delta_{x_i}\) and \(\nu=\sum_{j=1}^m b_j\delta_{y_j}\), with \(a\in\Delta_n\) and \(b\in\Delta_m\).
A nested sequence of partitions and a transport cost matrix \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a feasible fine-scale coupling supported on the final active set.

notation.meaning: Transport polytope with marginals a and b.
Active support at refinement level ell.
Restriction of the cost matrix to an active support.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete multilevel refinement with exact marginal constraints at every level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U(a,b)=\{P\in\mathbb{R}_+^{n\times m}:P\mathbf 1_m=a,\ P^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_n=b\}\). Initialize a coarse active set \(S_0\) from pairs of coarse cells and solve \(P_0\in\arg\min\{\langle C,P\rangle:P\in U(a,b),\ \operatorname{supp}(P)\subseteq S_0\}\). At level \(\ell\), refine every cell pair carrying positive mass, optionally add neighboring pairs, and denote the resulting support by \(S_{\ell+1}\). Solve the restricted transport problem over \(S_{\ell+1}\), warm-starting from a feasible disaggregation of \(P_\ell\). Stop when the finest partition is reached or the objective decrease is below a prescribed tolerance. Return the final feasible coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve transport on coarse cells, refine active cell pairs carrying mass, and repeatedly solve restricted fine-scale problems while preserving the original marginals.
knowledge_statements.title: Coarse-to-Fine Support Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports this algorithmic variant. The initial active set need not admit a coupling with the prescribed marginals, and the claimed feasible disaggregation and refinement invariant require a precise construction or hypothesis.

children.title: Subdomain Interface Coupling
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements across neighboring transport subdomains.

assumptions_latex: The source and target indices are partitioned into subdomains.
Each local coupling is nonnegative and has specified local row and column marginals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assembled matrix is globally feasible exactly when every interface balance equation holds.

notation.meaning: Signed incidence coefficient of interface h in subdomain k.
Mass exchanged by subdomain k across interface h.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface conservation condition for assembling discrete subdomain couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each subdomain \(k\), let \(P^{(k)}\geq 0\) satisfy its local marginal equations after including interface flux variables \(f_h^{(k)}\). For every internal interface \(h\), orient the incident subdomains by coefficients \(B_{hk}\in\{-1,0,1\}\). The interface-coupling condition is \[\sum_k B_{hk}f_h^{(k)}=0\qquad\text{for every internal interface }h.\] Together with equality of duplicated interface traces, when traces are represented explicitly, these equations ensure that outgoing mass from one subdomain is incoming mass to its neighbor. Consequently, the blockwise assembly \(P=\sum_k E_kP^{(k)}E_k^{\mathsf T}\), with duplicated interface contributions counted once, satisfies the prescribed global row and column marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local transport plans assemble into a global feasible plan precisely when their duplicated traces agree and signed mass flux balances at every internal interface.
knowledge_statements.title: Subdomain Interface Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asserted necessary-and-sufficient assembly condition depends on an unspecified domain-decomposition model, trace spaces, embeddings, and treatment of duplicated contributions. A source defining these objects and supporting the equivalence is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak convergence of the ray-monotone approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The families are those defined by the surrounding ray-monotone optimal-transport approximation construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: As \(\varepsilon\to0\), the approximations satisfy \(v_{\varepsilon}\rightharpoonup v\) and \(\gamma_{\varepsilon}\rightharpoonup\bar{\gamma}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As epsilon tends to zero, v_epsilon converges weakly to v and gamma_epsilon converges weakly to gamma-bar.
assumptions_latex: \(v_{\varepsilon}\) and \(\gamma_{\varepsilon}\) are the families arising from the stated ray-monotone optimal-transport approximation construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{\varepsilon}\rightharpoonup v\quad\text{and}\quad\gamma_{\varepsilon}\rightharpoonup\bar{\gamma}.\)

children.title: Low-Rank Coupling Approximations
children.top_down_role: Compressed representations of transport couplings.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed factorization defines a feasible coupling of nonnegative rank at most \(r\).

notation.meaning: Transport polytope with marginals a and b.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative-factor representation of rank-constrained discrete transport plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rank-\(r\) coupling approximation is parameterized by \[P=Q\operatorname{diag}(g)^{-1}R^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{k=1}^r g_k^{-1}Q_{:k}R_{:k}^{\mathsf T},\] where \(Q\in\mathbb{R}_+^{n\times r}\), \(R\in\mathbb{R}_+^{m\times r}\), and \(g\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^r\) satisfy \(Q\mathbf 1_r=a\), \(R\mathbf 1_r=b\), \(Q^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_n=g\), and \(R^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_m=g\). These constraints imply \(P\mathbf 1_m=a\) and \(P^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_n=b\), so \(P\in U(a,b)\), while its nonnegative rank is at most \(r\). Optimization over these factors replaces an unrestricted coupling by a latent-mixture approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible coupling is approximated by a sum of r nonnegative rank-one matrices whose factor marginals share the same latent weights.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Coupling Approximations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The factorization is mathematically coherent and fits the representation container, but no inspectable citation supports this low-rank transport parameterization.

children.title: Low-Rank Cost Approximations
children.top_down_role: Compressed structure in transport cost matrices.

assumptions_latex: The exact cost matrix is \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\).
The approximation \(\widetilde C=UV^{\mathsf T}\) has rank at most \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform cost error at most \(\varepsilon\) changes the optimal transport value by at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Optimal discrete transport value for cost C.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value stability under an entrywise low-rank approximation of a discrete cost matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\operatorname{OT}_C(a,b)=\min_{P\in U(a,b)}\langle C,P\rangle\), where \(a\in\Delta_n\), \(b\in\Delta_m\), and \(U(a,b)\) is the corresponding transport polytope. If \(\widetilde C=UV^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\|C-\widetilde C\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon\), then every \(P\in U(a,b)\) has total mass one and hence \(|\langle C-\widetilde C,P\rangle|\leq\varepsilon\). Taking minima gives \[\bigl|\operatorname{OT}_C(a,b)-\operatorname{OT}_{\widetilde C}(a,b)\bigr|\leq\varepsilon.\] Thus a low-rank cost surrogate yields a controlled additive error whenever it uniformly approximates the original costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing a discrete cost matrix by a rank-r surrogate with maximum entrywise error epsilon perturbs the optimal transport value by at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Cost Approximations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perturbation bound is precise and the property kind fits the container, but the record supplies no source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of an Optimal Transport Plan
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment of the stated Kantorovich minimization problem; the extract leaves the ambient-space and measure hypotheses implicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The transport problem \(\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,
u)} I[\pi]\) admits a minimizer: there exists \(\pi^\star\in\Pi(\mu,
u)\) such that \(I[\pi^\star]=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,
u)}I[\pi]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The infimum of the stated transport cost over all couplings of μ and ν is attained by an optimal coupling.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi(\mu,\nu)\) and \(I\) are those of the stated optimal-transport problem
The cost has the lower-semicontinuity and ambient compactness/tightness conditions used by the existence result
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\pi^\star\in\Pi(\mu,\nu): I[\pi^\star]=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}I[\pi]\)

children.title: Kernel Feature Approximations
children.top_down_role: Finite-feature representations of entropic transport kernels.

assumptions_latex: A feature map approximates the kernel uniformly on the sampled supports.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The kernel matrix can be applied through feature factors, with entrywise error controlled by the feature approximation.

notation.meaning: Feature matrices on source and target supports.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-feature factorization of the Gibbs kernel used by entropic transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k_\eta(x,y)=\exp(-c(x,y)/\eta)\), and suppose \(\phi_r\) satisfies \(|k_\eta(x_i,y_j)-\phi_r(x_i)^{\mathsf T}\phi_r(y_j)|\leq\varepsilon\) for every sampled pair. With feature matrices \((\Phi_X)_{i:}=\phi_r(x_i)^{\mathsf T}\) and \((\Phi_Y)_{j:}=\phi_r(y_j)^{\mathsf T}\), the Gibbs matrix admits the approximation \[K\approx\widetilde K=\Phi_X\Phi_Y^{\mathsf T},\qquad \|K-\widetilde K\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon.\] Consequently, matrix-vector products used in scaling iterations may be evaluated as \(\widetilde Kv=\Phi_X(\Phi_Y^{\mathsf T}v)\), using storage and arithmetic linear in the support sizes times \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate the entropic Gibbs kernel by inner products of r-dimensional features, enabling kernel products through two thin matrices with controlled entrywise error.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Feature Approximations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feature representation is coherent, but no citation supports the selected kernel-feature variant or its storage and arithmetic claim.

children.title: Rank-Limited Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Approximation limits imposed by insufficient numerical rank.

assumptions_latex: Approximation is restricted to matrices of rank at most \(r\).
Error is measured in the Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accuracy below the singular-value tail is impossible at fixed rank.

notation.meaning: Singular values of the target matrix in nonincreasing order.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral accuracy barrier for low-rank coupling or cost surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any matrix \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\), define \(e_r(M)=\inf_{\operatorname{rank}(X)\leq r}\|M-X\|_F\). If the singular values of \(M\) are \(\sigma_1(M)\geq\sigma_2(M)\geq\cdots\), then \[e_r(M)=\left(\sum_{k>r}\sigma_k(M)^2\right)^{1/2}.\] Hence no rank-\(r\) coupling or cost approximation can achieve Frobenius error smaller than this tail. In particular, when the singular values decay slowly, attaining tolerance \(\varepsilon\) requires \(r\) large enough that \(\sum_{k>r}\sigma_k(M)^2\leq\varepsilon^2\); fixed-rank methods then lose their intended computational advantage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-rank surrogate cannot beat the singular-value tail; slowly decaying spectra force rank to grow substantially for high accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Limited Accuracy Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The singular-value-tail boundary is mathematically standard and the failure-boundary kind is appropriate, but no authoritative source or locator is provided.

children.title: Stochastic Transport Estimation
children.top_down_role: Transport objectives or couplings estimated from random samples.

assumptions_latex: Independent sample pairs generate integrable random transport estimates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sample average is unbiased for the chosen sampled transport functional and converges almost surely under integrability.

notation.meaning: Transport statistic computed from replication s.
Population expectation of the sampled statistic.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monte Carlo estimation of a transport functional defined on empirical measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(s=1,\ldots,B\), draw independent batches \(X_1^{(s)},\ldots,X_m^{(s)}\sim\mu\) and \(Y_1^{(s)},\ldots,Y_m^{(s)}\sim
u\), construct empirical measures \(\widehat\mu_m^{(s)}=m^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{X_i^{(s)}}\) and \(\widehat
u_m^{(s)}=m^{-1}\sum_j\delta_{Y_j^{(s)}}\), and compute \(Z_s=F(\widehat\mu_m^{(s)},\widehat
u_m^{(s)})\). Return \[\widehat T_B= rac1B\sum_{s=1}^B Z_s.\] If \(\mathbb E|Z_1|<\infty\), then \(\mathbb E[\widehat T_B]=T_m:=\mathbb E[Z_1]\) and \(\widehat T_B	o T_m\) almost surely as \(B	o\infty\). This estimates \(T_m\), not necessarily \(F(\mu,
u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average transport values computed from independent empirical batches. The average consistently estimates the expected minibatch functional, which may differ from population transport.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Transport Estimation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Monte Carlo estimator and its stated target are coherent, but the record has no citation for the sampled-transport formulation or convergence claim.

children.title: Minibatch Transport Objectives
children.top_down_role: Transport criteria evaluated on finite sampled subsets.

knowledge_statements.title: Minibatch Transport Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent equal-size minibatches and a generic empirical transport functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Draw \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) independently from \(\mu\) and \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\) independently from \(
u\), with the two batches independent. Define \(\widehat\mu_m=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\delta_{X_i}\) and \(\widehat
u_m=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m\delta_{Y_j}\). For an integrable transport functional \(F\), such as \(W_p^p\) or an entropically regularized transport value under a fixed convention, the size-\(m\) minibatch objective is \[T_m(\mu,
u)=\mathbb E\!\left[F(\widehat\mu_m,\widehat
u_m)ight].\] The expectation includes all randomness in both batches and defines a population objective that can differ from \(F(\mu,
u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minibatch objective is the expected transport value between independent empirical measures constructed from m source and m target samples.
assumptions_latex: The measures \(\mu\) and \(\nu\) are probability measures on a measurable space.
The empirical transport statistic \(F(\widehat\mu_m,\widehat\nu_m)\) is integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minibatch objective is the expectation of transport between two independent empirical measures of size \(m\).

notation.meaning: Empirical measure formed from m samples of mu.
Empirical measure formed from m samples of nu.

children.title: Minibatch Aggregation Schemes
children.top_down_role: Combination of transport estimates across multiple minibatches.

knowledge_statements.title: Minibatch Aggregation Schemes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean and median aggregation of independently computed minibatch transport statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given integrable batch transport statistics \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_B\), a weighted aggregation scheme returns \(A_w=\sum_{s=1}^B w_sZ_s\), where the deterministic weights satisfy \(w_s\geq0\) and \(\sum_{s=1}^B w_s=1\). If all \(Z_s\) have common mean \(T_m\), then \(\mathbb E[A_w]=T_m\). If they are mutually independent and have finite variances, then \(\operatorname{Var}(A_w)=\sum_{s=1}^B w_s^2\operatorname{Var}(Z_s)\). Alternatively, \(A_{\mathrm{med}}=\operatorname{median}(Z_1,\ldots,Z_B)\) generally targets a median rather than \(T_m\) and has replacement breakdown point approaching one half: contamination of fewer than half the observations cannot move it beyond the range determined by the uncontaminated order statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministically weighted means preserve a common expected minibatch target and have an explicit variance under independence; median aggregation targets a median and resists contamination of fewer than about half the batches.
assumptions_latex: The deterministic aggregation weights satisfy \(w_s\geq0\) and \(\sum_{s=1}^B w_s=1\).
The variance formula additionally assumes mutual independence and finite variances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weighted averaging preserves the common mean target, whereas median aggregation generally changes the target and provides finite-sample resistance to contaminated batches.

children.title: Sampling-Induced Transport Bias
children.top_down_role: Systematic discrepancy caused by finite sampling or batch restriction.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Induced Transport Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete positive sampling bias for independent one-point empirical measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu_q=(1-q)\delta_0+q\delta_1\) with \(0<q<1\), and take \(\mu=
u=\mu_q\). Then \(W_p^p(\mu,
u)=0\). For minibatch size \(m=1\), draw independent \(X,Y\sim\mu_q\). The empirical measures are \(\delta_X\) and \(\delta_Y\), so \(W_p^p(\delta_X,\delta_Y)=|X-Y|^p\). Therefore \[\mathbb E\!\left[W_p^p(\delta_X,\delta_Y)ight]=\mathbb P(X
eq Y)=2q(1-q)>0.\] Thus the independent minibatch objective has bias \(2q(1-q)\) relative to the population transport value, even when the two population measures coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two identical Bernoulli populations have zero Wasserstein distance, but independent one-point batches yield expected transport cost 2q(1-q), demonstrating positive sampling bias.
assumptions_latex: The ground space is \(\{0,1\}\) with cost \(d(x,y)^p=|x-y|^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A one-sample transport objective is strictly positive although the population Wasserstein distance is zero.

children.title: Projection-Based Transport Approximations
children.top_down_role: Lower-dimensional transport surrogates obtained through projections.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Based Transport Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional linear projections of Euclidean probability measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(	heta\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\), let \(P_	heta(x)=\langle	heta,xangle\) and define \(D_	heta(\mu,
u)=W_p(P_{	heta\#}\mu,P_{	heta\#}
u)\). Since \(P_	heta\) is one-Lipschitz, \[D_	heta(\mu,
u)\leq W_p(\mu,
u).\] A finite-direction approximation chooses \(	heta_1,\ldots,	heta_L\) and aggregates the one-dimensional quantities \(D_{	heta_\ell}\), for example by an average or maximum. Each projected problem is one-dimensional and avoids constructing a coupling directly in \(\mathbb R^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project both measures onto selected lines and solve one-dimensional transport problems. Every directional Wasserstein value lower-bounds the full Euclidean Wasserstein distance.
assumptions_latex: The measures \(\mu,\nu\) lie in \(\mathcal P_p(\mathbb R^d)\) with \(p\geq1\).
Directions belong to the unit sphere \(\mathbb S^{d-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transport after projection gives a computable family of one-dimensional lower bounds on the full Wasserstein distance.

notation.meaning: Pushforward of a measure by P_theta.

children.title: Sliced Wasserstein Approximations
children.top_down_role: Transport comparisons aggregated over one-dimensional slices.

knowledge_statements.title: Sliced Wasserstein Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized spherical-average convention for sliced Wasserstein distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sliced Wasserstein distance averages p-th powers of one-dimensional Wasserstein distances over all projection directions, then takes the p-th root.
assumptions_latex: The measures \(\mu,\nu\) belong to \(\mathcal P_p(\mathbb R^d)\) with \(p\geq1\).
The sphere carries its normalized rotation-invariant probability measure \(\sigma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sliced Wasserstein distance is the spherical mean of one-dimensional Wasserstein costs, raised to the power \(1/p\).

notation.meaning: Normalized uniform probability measure on the unit sphere.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Particle Optimization of Sliced Wasserstein Barycenters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the weighted sliced-barycenter objective together with its generally nonconvex particle-gradient approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given fixed probability measures \(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_S\) and barycentric weights \(\lambda_s\), consider
\[
\min_{\alpha\in\mathcal M_+^1(\mathcal X)}\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\operatorname{SW}(\alpha,\beta_s)^2.
\]
Under particle discretizations of \(\alpha=\alpha_x\) and the inputs, define
\[
\mathcal E(x):=\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\mathcal E_{\beta_s}(x),
\qquad
\nabla\mathcal E(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\nabla\mathcal E_{\beta_s}(x).
\]
The generally nonconvex problem \(\min_x\mathcal E(x)\) can be treated by gradient descent with component gradients estimated from randomly sampled projection directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sliced Wasserstein barycenter minimizes a weighted sum of squared sliced Wasserstein distances to fixed input measures. With particle discretization, the objective is generally nonconvex, its gradient is the weighted sum of the individual gradients, and random directions can be used to estimate it.
assumptions_latex: \alpha=\alpha_x\text{ and the input measures are represented by particles for the Lagrangian scheme}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_x\mathcal E(x),\qquad \mathcal E(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\mathcal E_{\beta_s}(x),\qquad \nabla\mathcal E(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S\lambda_s\nabla\mathcal E_{\beta_s}(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hilbertian Sliced Wasserstein Kernel Constructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel consequences of Hilbertian sliced-Wasserstein geometry, distinguishing ordinary positive semidefiniteness from conditional positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because \(\operatorname{SW}\) is isometric to a Hilbert-space distance, for \(\sigma>0\) and \(1\le p\le2\),
\[
k_{\exp}(\alpha,\beta)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{\operatorname{SW}(\alpha,\beta)^p}{2\sigma^p}\right)
\]
is positive semidefinite on finite collections of probability measures. For \(0<p<2\),
\[
k_E(\alpha,\beta)=-\operatorname{SW}(\alpha, eta)^p
\]
is conditionally positive semidefinite: if \(\sum_i c_i=0\), then
\[
\sum_{i,j}c_ic_jk_E(\alpha_i,
\alpha_j)\ge0.
\]
The uncentered matrix \((-\operatorname{SW}(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)^p)_{i,j}\) is therefore not generally positive semidefinite without centering or a base-point correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hilbertian sliced-Wasserstein geometry yields positive-semidefinite exponential kernels in the stated power range. The raw negative distance-power energy kernel is only conditionally positive semidefinite, so an uncentered Gram matrix need not be positive semidefinite.
assumptions_latex: \sum_i c_i=0\text{ for conditional positive semidefiniteness of }k_E
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (k_{\exp}(\alpha_i,\alpha_j))_{i,j}\succeq0,\qquad \sum_{i,j}c_ic_j[-\operatorname{SW}(\alpha_i,\alpha_j)^p]\ge0\text{ when }\sum_i c_i=0

children.title: Max-Sliced Transport Approximations
children.top_down_role: Projection approximations emphasizing the most discriminating direction.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{MaxSW}_p(\mu,\nu)=\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}W_p((P_\theta)_\#\mu,(P_\theta)_\#\nu)\).

notation.meaning: Projection onto the line in direction theta

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of max-sliced Wasserstein distance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the supremum over all one-dimensional linear projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(\theta\in\mathbb S^{d-1}\), let \(P_\theta:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be given by \(P_\theta(x)=\langle\theta,x\rangle\). The order-\(p\) max-sliced transport approximation is
\[
\operatorname{MaxSW}_p(\mu,\nu):=\sup_{\theta\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}W_p\bigl((P_\theta)_\#\mu,(P_\theta)_\#\nu\bigr).
\]
It retains the most discriminating projected transport discrepancy rather than averaging over directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Max-sliced transport is the largest one-dimensional Wasserstein distance obtained by projecting both measures along the same unit direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Max-Sliced Transport Approximations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the max-sliced transport leaf, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is cited.

children.title: Finite-Direction Approximation Error
children.top_down_role: Accuracy loss from using a limited collection of projection directions.

assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\subset\mathbb S^{d-1}\) is a finite \(\delta\)-net with respect to Euclidean distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\leq \operatorname{MaxSW}_p(\mu,\nu)-\max_{\phi\in\Theta}W_p((P_\phi)_\#\mu,(P_\phi)_\#\nu)\leq 2R\delta.\]

notation.meaning: Projection onto the line in direction theta
Covering radius of the direction set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projection stability and a finite spherical net give the stated deterministic bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-direction error bound for compactly supported measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_\theta(x)=\langle\theta,x\rangle\) and define \(g(\theta):=W_p((P_\theta)_\#\mu,(P_\theta)_\#\nu)\). Then \(g\) is \(2R\)-Lipschitz on \(\mathbb S^{d-1}\). Consequently, every finite Euclidean \(\delta\)-net \(\Theta\subset\mathbb S^{d-1}\) satisfies
\[
0\leq \operatorname{MaxSW}_p(\mu,\nu)-\max_{\phi\in\Theta}g(\phi)\leq 2R\delta.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For measures supported in a ball of radius R, maximizing over a finite spherical delta-net underestimates max-sliced transport by at most 2R delta.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Direction Approximation Error

children.title: Coupling Rounding
children.top_down_role: Conversion of approximate couplings into structured finite-precision outputs.

assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}\) and \(a\in\mathbb R_+^m,b\in\mathbb R_+^n\) satisfy \(\mathbf1^\top a=\mathbf1^\top b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Q\mathbf1=a,\qquad Q^\top\mathbf1=b.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: diagonal scaling followed by a rank-one marginal correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact marginal rounding for a nonnegative discrete transport matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(i\), set \(x_i:=1\) when \((P\mathbf1)_i=0\), and otherwise set \(x_i:=\min\{a_i/(P\mathbf1)_i,1\}\). Let \(X:=\operatorname{Diag}(x)P\). For each \(j\), set \(y_j:=1\) when \((X^\top\mathbf1)_j=0\), and otherwise set \(y_j:=\min\{b_j/(X^\top\mathbf1)_j,1\}\). Let \(Y:=X\operatorname{Diag}(y)\), \(e:=a-Y\mathbf1\), and \(f:=b-Y^\top\mathbf1\). If \(\|e\|_1>0\), output
\[
Q:=Y+\frac{ef^\top}{\|e\|_1};
\]
otherwise output \(Q:=Y\). The output is nonnegative and satisfies
\[
Q\mathbf1=a,\qquad Q^\top\mathbf1=b.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale down excessive rows and columns, then add a rank-one correction from the remaining marginal deficits; zero row or column sums use scaling factor one.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Rounding

children.title: Marginal Feasibility Restoration
children.top_down_role: Correction of row or column marginal discrepancies.

assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}\) and the target marginals \(a,b\) have equal total mass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A matrix \(Q\geq0\) with \(Q\mathbf1=a\) and \(Q^\top\mathbf1=b\) is an exact feasibility restoration; its displayed marginals are directly verifiable.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: marginal equalities are the defining feasibility certificate for discrete couplings
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for exact or approximate restoration of discrete coupling marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(Q\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}\), define
\[
r(Q):=Q\mathbf1-a,\qquad s(Q):=Q^\top\mathbf1-b.
\]
The matrix \(Q\) restores both prescribed marginals exactly if and only if \(r(Q)=0\) and \(s(Q)=0\). More generally,
\[
\operatorname{Res}(Q):=\|r(Q)\|_1+\|s(Q)\|_1
\]
is a directly computable certificate of marginal infeasibility, with \(\operatorname{Res}(Q)=0\) precisely for feasible couplings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Row and column residuals certify marginal restoration; their combined norm vanishes exactly when the coupling is feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Marginal Feasibility Restoration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual certificate is correct and fits marginal feasibility restoration, but no inspectable citation with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Support-Preserving Restoration
children.top_down_role: Feasibility correction restricted to admissible coupling support.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A coupling supported on \(E\) exists exactly when \(\sum_{i\in I}a_i\leq\sum_{j\in N_E(I)}b_j\) for every row subset \(I\).

notation.meaning: Columns adjacent through E to a row set I

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: capacitated Hall condition for a bipartite transportation flow
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility criterion for restoring marginals without introducing new support edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(N_E(I):=\{j:\exists i\in I\text{ with }(i,j)\in E\}\). There exists \(Q\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}\) satisfying
\[
Q\mathbf1=a,\qquad Q^\top\mathbf1=b,\qquad Q_{ij}=0\ \text{for }(i,j)\notin E
\]
if and only if, for every \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\),
\[
\sum_{i\in I}a_i\leq\sum_{j\in N_E(I)}b_j.
\]
Thus support-preserving restoration is possible precisely when the permitted bipartite support passes these cut inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginals can be restored on the original support exactly when every row subset has enough neighboring column mass.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Preserving Restoration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The capacitated Hall condition is stated with the necessary equal-total-mass hypothesis and fits support-preserving restoration, but it has no inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: Rounding Cost Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certification of objective degradation introduced by rounding.

assumptions_latex: \(C\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is a finite cost matrix.
\(P,Q\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}\), with \(Q\) the rounded coupling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[|\langle C,Q\rangle-\langle C,P\rangle|\leq\|C\|_\infty\|Q-P\|_1.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: entrywise Hölder inequality for the linear transport objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori certificate based on the observed entrywise rounding displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The rounding-induced objective change satisfies
\[
|\langle C,Q\rangle-\langle C,P\rangle|\leq\|C\|_\infty\|Q-P\|_1.
\]
Thus \(\|C\|_\infty\|Q-P\|_1\) is an a posteriori upper certificate for the absolute cost change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The infinity norm of the cost matrix times the entrywise displacement between the original and rounded matrices certifies the absolute cost change.
knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Cost Certificates

children.title: Regularization Error
children.top_down_role: Discrepancy attributable to replacing exact transport with a regularized problem.

assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\) and \(b\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) are probability vectors, \(C\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(\varepsilon>0\).
\(\pi^\star\in\Pi(a,b)\) minimizes \(\langle C,\pi\rangle\) and has finite \(\operatorname{KL}(\pi^\star\|a\otimes b)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\leq\langle C,\pi_\varepsilon\rangle-\operatorname{OT}_C(a,b)\leq\varepsilon\operatorname{KL}(\pi^\star\|a\otimes b).\]

notation.meaning: Couplings with marginals a and b

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: comparison bound between regularized and unregularized finite transport objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias bound for KL-regularized finite discrete optimal transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the KL-regularized optimizer \(\pi_\varepsilon\) and any unregularized optimizer \(\pi^\star\) satisfying the assumptions,
\[
0\leq\langle C,\pi_\varepsilon\rangle-
\operatorname{OT}_C(a,b)
\leq\varepsilon\operatorname{KL}(\pi^\star\|a\otimes b).
\]
The upper bound is a regularization-error budget for the unregularized transport cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For positive discrete probability marginals, the unregularized cost of a KL-regularized optimizer exceeds the optimal transport cost by at most epsilon times the chosen unregularized optimizer's relative entropy.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Error

children.title: Optimization Error
children.top_down_role: Discrepancy attributable to incomplete numerical solution.

assumptions_latex: \(F_\varepsilon\) is a proper convex regularized transport objective with finite optimum \(F_\varepsilon^\star\).
\(P\) is primal feasible, \(y\) is dual feasible, and weak duality holds for the dual objective \(D_\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\leq F_\varepsilon(P)-F_\varepsilon^\star\leq F_\varepsilon(P)-D_\varepsilon(y).\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual optimization-error certificate for a convex regularized transport problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For primal-feasible \(P\) and dual-feasible \(y\), define
\[
G(P,y):=F_\varepsilon(P)-D_\varepsilon(y).
\]
The regularized-objective optimization error satisfies
\[
0\leq F_\varepsilon(P)-F_\varepsilon^\star\leq G(P,y).
\]
In particular, \(G(P,y)\leq\tau\) certifies optimization error at most \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex regularized transport problem, a feasible primal-dual gap certifies an upper bound on regularized-objective suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimization Error

children.title: Rounding Error
children.top_down_role: Discrepancy introduced during feasibility restoration or output conversion.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is an approximate transport matrix and \(Q\) is its feasible rounded version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rounding error is certified by \(E_{\mathrm{round}}:=\|C\|_\infty\|Q-P\|_1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: specialization of the linear-objective perturbation bound
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost error attributed solely to feasibility-restoring modification of a computed plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a computed matrix \(P\) and its feasible restoration \(Q\), define
\[
E_{\mathrm{round}}:=\|C\|_\infty\|Q-P\|_1.
\]
Then
\[
\left|\langle C,Q\rangle-\langle C,P\rangle\right|\leq E_{\mathrm{round}}.
\]
If the rounding routine separately certifies \(\|Q-P\|_1\leq\rho\), the simpler bound \(E_{\mathrm{round}}\leq\|C\|_\infty\rho\) follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding error is the certified cost perturbation caused by replacing an approximate matrix with a feasible coupling.
knowledge_statements.title: Rounding Error

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated cost-perturbation certificate correctly isolates rounding error and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Composite Error Budget
children.top_down_role: Allocation of total accuracy tolerance across distinct computational errors.

assumptions_latex: \(a,b\) are discrete probability vectors, \(C\) is a finite cost matrix, \(\pi_\varepsilon\) is an exact regularized coupling, \(P\) is a numerical approximation, and \(Q\in\Pi(a,b)\) is its rounded feasible coupling.

The nonnegative quantities \(E_{\mathrm{reg}},E_{\mathrm{opt}},E_{\mathrm{round}}\) satisfy \(\langle C,\pi_\varepsilon\rangle-\operatorname{OT}_C(a,b)\leq E_{\mathrm{reg}}\), \(\langle C,P\rangle-\langle C,\pi_\varepsilon\rangle\leq E_{\mathrm{opt}}\), and \(\langle C,Q\rangle-\langle C,P\rangle\leq E_{\mathrm{round}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\langle C,Q\rangle-\operatorname{OT}_C(a,b)\leq E_{\mathrm{reg}}+E_{\mathrm{opt}}+E_{\mathrm{round}}.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: additive composition of compatible stagewise cost-error certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive end-to-end budget for regularization, numerical optimization, and rounding errors measured in the same transport-cost objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated stagewise bounds, the final feasible coupling \(Q\) satisfies
\[
\langle C,Q\rangle-
\operatorname{OT}_C(a,b)
\leq E_{\mathrm{reg}}+E_{\mathrm{opt}}+E_{\mathrm{round}}.
\]
Thus the sum of the three compatible cost-error bounds is an end-to-end certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When regularization, optimization, and rounding errors are all measured in the same transport-cost objective, their valid bounds add to an end-to-end cost certificate for the final feasible coupling.
knowledge_statements.title: Composite Error Budget

assumptions_latex: For parameters \(\varepsilon,\tau,\rho>0\), a specified three-stage transport procedure returns a feasible coupling \(Q\in\Pi(a,b)\).
The regularization, optimization, and rounding stages have certified additive cost errors at most \(B(\varepsilon)\), \(\tau\), and \(K\rho\), respectively.
Their computational costs are at most \(T_{\mathrm{reg}}(\varepsilon)\), \(T_{\mathrm{opt}}(\varepsilon,\tau)\), and \(T_{\mathrm{round}}(\rho)\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[B(\varepsilon)+\tau+K\rho\leq\eta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \langle C,Q\rangle-\operatorname{OT}_C(a,b)\leq\eta\] and the total computational cost is at most \[T_{\mathrm{reg}}(\varepsilon)+T_{\mathrm{opt}}(\varepsilon,\tau)+T_{\mathrm{round}}(\rho).\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: abstract composition of stagewise error and computational-cost bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract end-to-end composition bound for a specified solver; it does not provide an instantiated asymptotic rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(\eta\geq0\) and parameters \(\varepsilon,\tau,\rho>0\) satisfying
\[
B(\varepsilon)+\tau+K\rho\leq\eta,
\]
the procedure's feasible output \(Q\) satisfies
\[
\langle C,Q\rangle-
\operatorname{OT}_C(a,b)
\leq\eta,
\]
and its total computational cost is at most
\[
T_{\mathrm{reg}}(\varepsilon)+T_{\mathrm{opt}}(\varepsilon,\tau)+T_{\mathrm{round}}(\rho).
\]
The least certified bound within this model is the infimum of this cost expression over all parameters satisfying the error constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a specified three-stage solver that returns a feasible coupling, any allocation of the target additive cost error among regularization, optimization, and rounding yields the sum of the corresponding certified stage costs; optimizing over valid allocations gives the abstract cost-accuracy bound.
knowledge_statements.title: End-to-End Cost-Accuracy Complexity

children.title: Residual Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Accuracy assessed through marginal or optimality residuals.

assumptions_latex: \(P\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}\) approximates a coupling with target marginals \(a,b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Residual accuracy at level \(\eta\) means \(\|P\mathbf1-a\|_1+\|P^\top\mathbf1-b\|_1\leq\eta\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit norm-based definition of marginal residual accuracy
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entrywise \(\ell_1\) marginal-residual criterion for a discrete transport matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the marginal residual accuracy measure by
\[
R(P):=\|P\mathbf1-a\|_1+\|P^\top\mathbf1-b\|_1.
\]
The matrix \(P\) has residual accuracy \(\eta\) when \(R(P)\leq\eta\). Exact marginal feasibility is the limiting case \(R(P)=0\). This condition controls only violations of the coupling constraints; without additional stability assumptions it does not imply objective-value or transport-plan accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual accuracy bounds the combined row- and column-marginal violations, but alone does not guarantee objective or plan accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition precisely defines marginal residual accuracy and correctly warns that it does not alone control objective or plan accuracy. Its content kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Objective Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Accuracy assessed through transport objective values.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le F(\widehat\pi)-F^\star\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{obj}}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports computational optimal-transport objective certificates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive primal-objective accuracy for a feasible discrete transport plan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(b\in\mathbb R_+^n\) have equal mass, let \(\Pi(a,b)\) be their transport polytope, and let \(F:\Pi(a,b)\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). A feasible computed plan \(\widehat\pi\) is objectively \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{obj}}\)-accurate when \[0\le F(\widehat\pi)-F^\star\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{obj}},\qquad F^\star:=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(a,b)}F(\pi).\] A certified lower bound \(L\le F^\star\) verifies this accuracy whenever \(F(\widehat\pi)-L\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{obj}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible transport plan is objectively accurate when its objective value is within the prescribed additive tolerance of the optimum, as certified by a valid lower bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits Objective Accuracy, and the additive-gap and lower-bound implications are mathematically coherent. However, the record has no citation or inspectable locator supporting this computational optimal-transport certificate; the tolerance should also be explicitly declared nonnegative when sourced.

children.title: Transport-Plan Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Accuracy assessed through discrepancy between computed transport plans.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\Pi}(\widehat\pi,\mathcal S^\star)\le\varepsilon_{\pi}\), where \(\mathcal S^\star:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pi\in\Pi(a,b)}F(\pi)\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifies the intended transport-plan metric.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy relative to the optimal-plan set in a declared plan metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a transport objective on a nonempty transport polytope \(\Pi(a,b)\), and suppose its minimizer set \(\mathcal S^\star:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pi\in\Pi(a,b)}F(\pi)\) is nonempty. After fixing a metric \(d_{\Pi}\) on plans, a feasible output \(\widehat\pi\) has transport-plan accuracy \(\varepsilon_{\pi}\) precisely when \[d_{\Pi}(\widehat\pi,\mathcal S^\star):=\inf_{\pi^\star\in\mathcal S^\star}d_{\Pi}(\widehat\pi,\pi^\star)\le\varepsilon_{\pi}.\] The metric and its normalization are part of the certificate and cannot be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Plan accuracy bounds the declared metric distance from the computed feasible plan to the entire set of optimal transport plans.
knowledge_statements.title: Transport-Plan Accuracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits Transport-Plan Accuracy, and distance to the nonempty optimal set is defined consistently. No source identifies this as the intended plan-accuracy notion or supports the requirement that the plan metric and normalization form part of the certificate.

children.title: Cross-Metric Accuracy Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Regimes where improvement in one accuracy metric fails to control another.

assumptions_latex: The optimal set contains distinct plans \(\pi_1^\star\ne\pi_2^\star\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(\pi_1^\star)-F^\star=0\) while \(d_{\Pi}(\pi_1^\star,\pi_2^\star)>0\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this cross-metric failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness prevents objective error from controlling distance to a selected optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For linear discrete transport \(F(\pi):=\langle C,\pi\rangle\), suppose two distinct plans \(\pi_1^\star,\pi_2^\star\in\Pi(a,b)\) are optimal. Then \[F(\pi_1^\star)-F^\star=F(\pi_2^\star)-F^\star=0,\qquad d_{\Pi}(\pi_1^\star,\pi_2^\star)>0\] for every metric \(d_{\Pi}\). Consequently, arbitrarily small—even zero—objective error does not imply proximity to a designated optimizer. Objective accuracy can control distance to the optimal set only under an additional error bound, such as \(d_{\Pi}(\pi,\mathcal S^\star)\le\psi(F(\pi)-F^\star)\) with \(\psi(t)\to0\) as \(t\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When optimal plans are nonunique, zero objective error may coexist with positive distance from a chosen optimizer; a separate error bound is necessary.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Metric Accuracy Mismatch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role exactly fits the container. Nonuniqueness does show that zero objective error need not control distance to a designated optimizer, while the displayed error bound concerns distance to the optimal set. A source is still required for the stated cross-metric boundary and error-bound formulation.

children.title: Transport Memory Complexity
children.top_down_role: Storage demands of couplings, kernels, potentials, or solver state.

assumptions_latex: The problem has \(m\) source and \(n\) target atoms
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dense plan storage is \(\Theta(mnb)\) bytes; an explicit \(k\)-sparse plan requires \(\Theta(kb)\) numerical storage plus indices.

notation.meaning: numbers of source and target atoms
number of stored nonzero plan entries

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses optimal-transport memory complexity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage complexity for explicit dense or sparse discrete transport plans.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For transport between \(m\) source atoms and \(n\) target atoms, explicitly materializing a dense plan \(\pi\in\mathbb R_+^{m\times n}\) requires \(mn\) numerical entries and hence \(\Theta(mnb)\) bytes when each entry occupies \(b\) bytes. If \(C\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and an equally sized kernel are also materialized, each adds \(\Theta(mnb)\) bytes. An explicitly stored plan with \(k\) nonzeros uses \(\Theta(kb)\) numerical bytes, plus \(\Theta(k(\log m+\log n))\) bits for indices. These bounds exclude streamed or implicit representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit dense transport plan needs memory proportional to the product of support sizes; sparse storage scales with the number of retained entries plus indices.
knowledge_statements.title: Transport Memory Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits Transport Memory Complexity, and the dense and sparse counts are plausible under explicit storage. No citation supports the storage model, index representation, or transport-specific interpretation.

children.title: Parallel Transport Execution
children.top_down_role: Concurrency patterns for transport primitives or solver updates.

assumptions_latex: \(p\) workers partition rows or columns without overlap
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each Sinkhorn matrix-vector phase is parallelizable by independent partial products followed by reductions.
review_flags: Execution cost depends on communication, partitioning, and hardware assumptions absent from supplied sources.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Data-parallel execution of dense Sinkhorn scaling iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given positive marginals \(a,b\), a positive kernel \(K\), initial \(v^{(0)}>0\), and \(p\) workers, partition the rows of \(K\) among workers. At iteration \(t\), workers compute disjoint components of \(Kv^{(t)}\), set \(u^{(t+1)}:=a\oslash(Kv^{(t)})\), compute partial column sums contributing to \(K^{\mathsf T}u^{(t+1)}\), reduce those sums, and set \(v^{(t+1)}:=b\oslash(K^{\mathsf T}u^{(t+1)})\). Stop when a declared marginal residual is below tolerance; output the implicit plan \(\operatorname{Diag}(u)K\operatorname{Diag}(v)\). Parallel correctness requires exact assembly of both matrix-vector products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioned workers compute Sinkhorn matrix-vector products and reductions in parallel, stopping when the declared marginal residual meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Transport Execution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Parallel Transport Execution, and the partitioned Sinkhorn phases are internally coherent. The communication, reduction, partitioning, and exact-assembly claims have no supporting source or execution-model locator.

children.title: CPU Execution Regimes
children.top_down_role: Performance characteristics on general-purpose processors.

assumptions_latex: A dense \(m\times n\) kernel is stored in host memory
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Serial dense CPU work is \(\Theta(Tmn)\), with \(\Theta(mn)\) kernel memory.
review_flags: Hardware-dependent constants and parallel scaling require benchmark-specific sources.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operation and storage regimes for dense Sinkhorn execution on CPUs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a dense \(m\)-by-\(n\) kernel, one Sinkhorn iteration performs one multiplication by \(K\), one by \(K^{\mathsf T}\), and \(O(m+n)\) componentwise operations. Thus serial CPU execution for \(T\) iterations costs \(\Theta(Tmn)\) arithmetic operations and stores \(\Theta(mn)\) kernel entries. With \(p\) CPU threads, the ideal compute term is \(\Theta(Tmn/p)\), but reductions and memory traffic remain. The regime is compute-limited only when kernel data are sufficiently reused; otherwise attained time is bounded below by bytes transferred divided by sustainable memory bandwidth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense CPU Sinkhorn costs proportional to iterations times matrix size; multithreading helps only until reductions or memory bandwidth dominate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A dense GPU Sinkhorn regime is feasible when the kernel, scaling vectors, and work buffers fit device memory, in particular when \(mn+O(m+n)\le M\) measured in stored entries. Over \(T\) iterations, the arithmetic work remains \(\Theta(Tmn)\), while the two matrix-vector phases expose \(\Theta(mn)\) parallel entrywise operations per iteration. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Divergence-relaxed unbalanced optimal transport
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static discrete unbalanced transport with divergence-penalized marginals, its balanced infinite-penalty limit, and the KL-specific generalized Sinkhorn updates displayed in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\mathbf a\in\mathbb R_+^n\), \(\mathbf b\in\mathbb R_+^m\), \(\mathbf C\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\), penalties \(\tau_1,\tau_2>0\), and a divergence \(\mathbf D_\varphi\), define
\[
L_{\mathbf C}^{\tau_1,\tau_2}(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)
=\min_{\mathbf P\in\mathbb R_+^{n\times m}}
\langle\mathbf C,\mathbf P\rangle
+\tau_1\mathbf D_\varphi(\mathbf P\mathbf1_m\mid\mathbf a)
+\tau_2\mathbf D_\varphi(\mathbf P^\top\mathbf1_n\mid\mathbf b).
\]
Thus the hard marginal equalities are replaced by divergence penalties. If \(\sum_i a_i=\sum_j b_j\) and the divergence enforces equality when its penalty tends to infinity, then \(\tau_1=\tau_2\to+\infty\) recovers the balanced transport formulation with hard marginals. In the KL-penalized entropic specialization, the generalized Sinkhorn updates are
\[
\mathbf u\leftarrow\left(\frac{\mathbf a}{\mathbf K\mathbf v}\right)^{\tau_1/(\tau_1+\varepsilon)},\qquad
\mathbf v\leftarrow\left(\frac{\mathbf b}{\mathbf K^\top\mathbf u}\right)^{\tau_2/(\tau_2+\varepsilon)},
\]
with componentwise division and exponentiation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbalanced optimal transport replaces exact marginal constraints by divergence penalties. When the input masses agree, sending both penalties to infinity restores hard-marginal balanced transport, provided the divergence enforces equality. For KL marginal penalties with entropic regularization, generalized Sinkhorn iterations use the displayed fractional-power scaling updates.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf a\in\mathbb R_+^n,\quad \mathbf b\in\mathbb R_+^m,\quad \mathbf C\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}
\mathbf D_\varphi\text{ is defined on the relevant nonnegative histograms}
\sum_i a_i=\sum_j b_j\text{ and the divergence penalty enforces marginal equality for the balanced-limit assertion}
\mathbf D_\varphi=\mathrm{KL},\quad \varepsilon>0\text{ for the displayed generalized Sinkhorn updates}
\mathbf K\in\mathbb R_{++}^{n\times m},\quad \mathbf u\in\mathbb R_{++}^n,\quad \mathbf v\in\mathbb R_{++}^m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\mathbf C}^{\tau_1,\tau_2}\text{ is the divergence-relaxed transport objective above; its infinite-penalty balanced limit imposes hard marginals, and its KL-entropic specialization admits the displayed scaling updates.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Source-augmented dynamic Wasserstein–Fisher–Rao formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines dynamic unbalanced transport through a continuity equation with a mass source and a convex action charging momentum and mass variation. The extracted parameter-limit claims are excluded because they are inconsistent with the displayed weighting of the source cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonnegative measures \(\alpha_0,\alpha_1\) on \(\mathbb R^d\), define
\[
\overline{\mathcal C}(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)=\left\{(\alpha_t,J_t,s_t):\partial_t\alpha_t+\operatorname{div}(J_t)=s_t,\ \alpha_{t=0}=\alpha_0,\ \alpha_{t=1}=\alpha_1\right\}.
\]
Given the convex positively \(1\)-homogeneous integrand \(\theta\) and a weight \(\tau>0\), the dynamic Wasserstein–Fisher–Rao objective is
\[
\operatorname{WFR}_{\tau}^{2}(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)=\min_{(\alpha,J,s)\in\overline{\mathcal C}(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)}\int_0^1\!\int_{\mathbb R^d}\left[\theta(\alpha_t(x),J_t(x))+\tau\theta(\alpha_t(x),s_t(x))\right]dx\,dt.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dynamic unbalanced transport permits local creation or destruction of mass by adding a source term to the continuity equation. The Wasserstein–Fisher–Rao value minimizes a convex, one-homogeneous action that charges both transport momentum and the source term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{WFR}_{\tau}^{2}(\alpha_0,\alpha_1)\) is defined by the stated source-augmented dynamic minimization problem.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the intentional loss of base position at zero cone radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In \(\mathfrak C(X)=(X\times[0,\infty))/(X\times\{0\})\), every pair \((x,0)\) and \((y,0)\) represents the same apex \(\mathfrak o\). Consequently,
\[
d_{\mathfrak C}([x,0],[y,0])=0,
\qquad
d_{\mathfrak C}(\mathfrak o,[x,r])=r.
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\Gamma_m(\mu,\nu)=\left\{\pi\in\mathcal M_+(X\times Y):(p_X)_\#\pi\le\mu,\ (p_Y)_\#\pi\le\nu,\ \pi(X\times Y)=m\right\}.
\]
The fixed-mass partial transport problem is
\[
\mathsf{PT}_m^c(\mu,\nu)=\inf_{\pi\in\Gamma_m(\mu,\nu)}\int_{X\times Y}c(x,y)\,d\pi(x,y).
\]
Any minimizer transports exactly \(m\) units while discarding the unused source mass \(\mu-(p_X)_\#\pi\) and unused target capacity \(\nu-(p_Y)_\#\pi\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary-Reservoir Quadratic Wasserstein Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines admissible boundary transport plans and their quadratic transport cost for finite positive measures of possibly unequal mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite positive measures \(\mu,\nu\in\mathcal M_+(\Omega)\), not necessarily probability measures or of equal mass, define
\[
\Pi_b(\mu,\nu):=\left\{\gamma\in\mathcal M_+(\overline\Omega\times\overline\Omega):((\pi_x)_\#\gamma)|_{\Omega^\circ}=\mu,\;((\pi_y)_\#\gamma)|_{\Omega^\circ}=\nu\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
W_{b,2}(\mu,\nu):=\left(\inf_{\gamma\in\Pi_b(\mu,\nu)}\int_{\overline\Omega\times\overline\Omega}|x-y|^2\,d\gamma(x,y)\right)^{1/2}.
\]
Only the interior parts of the marginals are prescribed, so mass may be transported to or from \(\partial\Omega\); boundary-to-boundary mass is unconstrained and may be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A boundary transport plan is a finite positive measure on the product of the closure whose two marginals agree with the given measures only in the interior. The boundary quadratic Wasserstein distance is the square root of the least squared Euclidean transport cost over such plans. Thus finite positive measures need not have equal mass, because excess or missing mass may pass through the boundary, while unconstrained boundary-to-boundary transport may be discarded.

\mathsf{PT}_0^c(\mu,\nu)=0,
\qquad
\mathsf{PT}_{m_1}^c(\mu,\nu)\le\mathsf{PT}_{m_2}^c(\mu,\nu)
\quad\text{whenever }0\le m_1\le m_2\le M.
\]
At \(m=M\), the marginal corresponding to the smaller total mass is saturated. If \(\mu(X)=\nu(Y)=M\), both marginals are saturated and \(\mathsf{PT}_M^c(\mu,
u)=\mathsf{OT}_c(\mu,
u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The prescribed transported mass ranges from zero to the smaller total mass, and the optimal value is nondecreasing in that mass. At the maximum, the smaller measure is fully retained; equal total masses recover balanced transport.
assumptions_latex: \(X,Y\) are Polish spaces, \(\mu\in\mathcal M_+(X)\), and \(\nu\in\mathcal M_+(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The map \(m\mapsto\mathsf{PT}_m^c(\mu,\nu)\) is nondecreasing on \([0,M]\), with \(\mathsf{PT}_0^c(\mu,\nu)=0\).

children.title: Mass-Creation Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Pathological preference for producing mass under weak creation penalties.

assumptions_latex: Creation is charged linearly by \(\alpha_+\int d\zeta^+\), and the remaining action terms are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\alpha_+=0\), creation from the zero measure has zero cost and separation fails.
